News.title: Distressing moment tourist plunges 260ft down canyon after being pushed by smirking staff despite begging ‘please stop’
News.content:
Next

THIS is the horror moment a petrified tourist was forced to take a 260ft plunge after begging staff not to jump into a Russian canyon.

The terrorised woman had plainly changed her mind and was desperately pleading to avoid being tipped over the edge.



“Please don’t throw me like that! Let me go,” the woman cried out before turning to her husband who appears to be filming the video.

As she desperately tried to force herself away from the ledge she continues: “Please… Don’t! I’m begging you!”.



Instructors can be seen laughing as they told her to “calm down” and not “jerk around.”

Suddenly the instructors kicked the back of the woman’s knees before swinging her out from the platform.

The woman gripped onto her harness as she hung, suspended in the air, before suddenly dropping.

The distressing incident took place at the Noh’o tourist attraction on the Sulak River in Dagestan.



One onlooker said: “While she was panicking in her harness, they dragged her to the edge, kicked her leg and sent her plunging down.

“Her husband filmed his wife being subjected to this nightmare – and laughed.”

The woman survived the jump and was even asked if she wanted to take the plunge again when she was brought back to the platform.

But she fumed, “I said no!” adding, “I’m scared.”

The Russian Investigative Committee is reportedly probing the case.



It comes after a woman plunged to her death after being thrown from a bridge swing without a safety rope in Brazil earlier this year.

Maria Eduarda Rodrigues de Freitas, 21, was hurled off a bridge in Limeira, Brazil, plummeting 130ft.

Horrifying video showed the moment she was held in the air by workers and launched off the bridge.



The 21-year-old didn’t realise a safety rope had not been attached to her harness before the terrifying fall.

The rope could be seen tangled on the ground, nowhere near Maria.

Seconds after, voices can be heard in the background of the video shouting: “the rope, people, the rope”.

After Maria hit the ground, police said the workers changed their clothes and at least two allegedly fled the area.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But they were arrested soon afterwards at the Ponte do Esqueleto trail after a chopper tracked them down.



The three men from the video, Luis Felipe Feliciano Egoroff, 32, Vitor de Freitas Gonçalves, 27, and Maicon Fernandes Cintra, 42, were charged with homicide with implied malice.

News.title: Obese rat’s death goes viral as tragic pic shows tubby critter trapped in bin after gorging on rubbish
News.content:
FATTY-TOUILLE Obese rat’s death goes viral as tragic pic shows tubby critter trapped in bin after gorging on rubbish







Next

AN OBESE rat’s death has gone viral after the helpless rodent was pictured trapped inside a bin after gorging on too much rubbish.

The tubby critter is believed to have eaten itself to death and sparked an outpouring of grief among locals – with some even comparing his final moments to a classical piece of art.



With its void-black eyes and tiny paws clawing for help, the dramatic image captured the hearts of New York locals who likened the scene to a grand sculpture.

Although some passersby in Riverside Park shrugged it off as just another day in the Big Apple, many witnesses said they were touched by the fat creature’s tale.



One bystander told the New York Post while walking her dog: “Oh my God. What a terrible death.

“It also looks like a sculpture, a New York sculpture.”



Another resident agreed, saying the bloated critter’s unfortunate predicament was a “New York City still life”.

“It’s a still life, like dead things in a painting,” she said.

A third weighed in with comparisons to the neoclassical artwork “Death of Marat” (1793).

The portrait – which was also used as an album cover for Deathconsciousness – shows French revolutionary Jean-Paul Marat’s murder in a bathtub.



Both depictions of the rat and Marat convey a tragic sense of desolation, with the acceptance of death washed across their visages, the witness argued.

But some New Yorkers weren’t at all moved by the rat’s heart-rending story.

One person said: “It’s New York City. It’s everywhere. I live nearby and they call it Rat Street.

“I moved a year ago and I was shocked when I would see rats but now I’m getting used to it.”

Another chimed in: “That’s gross.”



An elderly man told the outlet the rat’s death should bring about a moment of reflection, to lament on the life it lived.

“I’m not offended by them,” the wise man commented.

“Everyone seems to hate them, so it’s not a popular opinion.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“It’s lived a good life, living in the park.”

News.title: Shock moment 84 dogs found in faeces-covered home – as cruel owner faces jail for leaving pets to fend for themselves
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment 84 dogs were found crammed inside a squalid home after their owner left the pets to fend for themselves.

Around 33 Springer Spaniel-type dogs were found on a filthy staircase at the house in Tickhill, near Doncaster, on April 18 last year.



RSPCA officers and the police discovered a further 20 to 25 of the pooches in a kitchen that was caked in dirt from floor to ceiling.

There were at least 20 piles of faeces on the filthy ground, which the dogs had distributed around the floor and over themselves.



Most of the animals were also covered in faeces and many of their ears had lumps of dirt stuck to them that looked like dreadlocks.

The stench was so bad that one of the police officers had to leave the house to be sick, the RSPCA said.

Children’s social worker David Parkes has now been found guilty of three animal welfare offences.

His wife Delphine Parkes and son Sam Parkes, who lived in the same house, had both admitted the same offences.

All three defendants will be sentenced on December 9 at Doncaster Magistrates Court.

The shocking discovery was made on April 17 after two unsuccessful attempts to check on the dogs.



Police executed a warrant with the RSPCA but had to force their way in through a back door – despite the family being inside.

Animal Rescue Officer Liz Braidley said: “On entry into the property at the rear the conditions were appalling.

“The first room was a small area to the rear of the garage. Every surface from the floor and up the walls was brown in colour, the smell of urine and faeces was overpowering it made my eyes sting.



“We then went through a door to the left which led into the kitchen. There were numerous Spaniel type dogs, all filthy with stained yellow coats. Every part of the floor, walls, and surfaces was caked in a brown residue.

“The dogs all ran to the other side of the room appearing very scared and timid. The smell in this room was unbearable, it was difficult to talk or breathe properly and I was unable to stay in there for extended periods of time.

“There was a further door across the kitchen area. Myself and Inspector Ludlam went through here which led to an area by the staircase to the upper floor.



“There again, were numerous Spaniel type dogs which were impossible to count as they retreated up the stairs where they then sat watching us.”

Delphine Parkes was found in their bedrooms along with two adult Springer Spaniels, two 12-week-old Springer Spaniel Puppies, two adult female Patterdale Terriers and two Patterdale Terrier pups.

Inspectors found her son in his dirty room along with two cats.

Delphine Parkes told the officers the situation had got out of control since Covid and she knew they now had too many dogs.

The couple were told neither themselves or the animals could carry on living in these conditions and David Parkes agreed for all of them to be removed and he signed them over into the care of the RSPCA.



He later disputed ownership during the two-day court hearing and claimed they were owned by his wife and son.

Parkes blamed his heavy workload for not being able to look after the dogs but he knew the names and ages of most of the animals and their feeding plans, purchased the dog food and took them to the vets.

The court heard there was no evidence the family were large-scale breeders but the pets were left unneutered and bred out of control.

A vet who examined 46 of the dogs said 14 of them were emaciated and had been suffering for at least a month.

A further five had infected cuts on their ears, which are believed to have been caused by attempts to cut off matted fur with scissors.



Several had ear infections and one Spaniel had an “excruciatingly painful” broken front leg, which was later successfully treated.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Following the rescue most of the dogs were taken to private boarding facilities on behalf of the RSPCA.

The RSPCA said one Spaniel was sadly put to sleep to prevent further suffering but the rest have been rehomed.

News.title: Dog walking law is being lifted across England TODAY – and will mean owners no longer risk £1,000 fine
News.content:
Next

A DOG walking law is being lifted across England today with owners no longer risking £1,000 fines.

The rule, which has been in place since May, has been scrapped as per its annual schedule.



The ban on walking pooches on beaches is seasonal and is enforced in many areas of the UK every summer.

With autumn arriving, the restrictions were lifted as of September 30.



Councils in coastal areas usually put the rules in place from May until the end of September.

Dogs can be banned from beaches entirely or restricted to certain zones, while other officials place time restrictions for when dogs can be on the beach.

Other councils say that dogs must remain on leads in order to be on the beach.

Councils can enforce the bans via Public Spaces Protection Orders – and dog walkers can be given on-the-spot fines for breaking the rules.

Penalties of £100 are usually given to first-time offenders, while repeatedly going against the rules can mean facing a fine of up to £1,000.

Dog lovers will no longer be at risk of the fines for walking pups on beaches, following the lift.



However, dog fouling on beaches can still land walkers with fixed penalty notices of up to £1,000.

Those who own furry friends are urged to check their local council’s website to find the exact rules surrounding dogs on beaches for their area, as some locations may enforce year-round rules.

News.title: UK weather: Heavy rain, thunder and hail to batter Britain along with 50mph winds – but balmy autumn temps continue
News.content:
RAIN CHECK UK weather: Heavy rain, thunder and hail to batter Britain along with 50mph winds – but balmy autumn temps continue







Next

HEAVY rain, thunder, and even hail is expected to batter Britain today.

Parts of the UK could be hit with 50mph winds, but the balmy autumn temperatures will continue fore the rest of the week.



Heavy downpours are moving eastwards across England today but should ease up by lunchtime.

Scattered showers will hit the west of England and in Wales, potentially paired with thunder, strong winds and eve hail.



Up to 40mm and blustery winds of more than 50mph are set to batter the country.

But the Met Office have predicted that there will be sunny spells accompanying this gloomy weather.



These showers will continue into the evening along the western coast while the rest of the country keeps dry.

Overnight, cool air will sweep in, breaking the humidity and bringing fresher conditions to the country.



This will mean a cooler start to Thursday morning but temperatures will still reach 1C-3C above the seasonal average in most areas of the UK.

Brits have been lapping up balmy temperatures for this time of year thanks to a low pressure system in the Atlantic, pushing warm southern European air in the UK‘s direction.

A spokesperson for the Met Office said of today’s weather conditions: “Heavy rain clears eastwards by midday, followed by sunny spells with showers.

“Mainly across western areas, where some may be heavy with isolated hail and thunder.

“Winds gradually ease but remain gusty, especially in the west. Temperatures above average.



“Tonight, scattered showers continue near western coasts. Elsewhere remains dry with clear spells.

“Cooler than recent nights, especially across eastern and southeastern areas, with isolated fog patches developing in sheltered areas.”

Met Office spokesman Stephen Dixon said Thursday and Friday will be days of “sunshine and showers” and “mixed conditions”.

On Friday and heading into the weekend, more rain is predicted in the north and west of the country along with windy conditions.

But higher pressure will build in the UK over the weekend bringing more settled conditions.



Down south, temperatures will be above the average for this time of year with highs of 21C, and will remain relatively dry.

News.title: Children, 3 & 6, ‘stabbed 50 times by mum’ found covered in blood after ‘boy called grandma to say he was hungry’
News.content:
Next

A MUM allegedly stabbed her two young children at least 50 times before cops found the pair alone and covered in blood.

Taylor Gosnell, 35, is accused of knifing her six-year-old son and three-year-old daughter at their family home in South Carolina.



The kids were only discovered after the little boy called his grandma to say he was hungry, police said.

Spartanburg police raced to the home on Bud Arthur Drive at around 2.30pm on Saturday.



Detectives found the home “in disarray” with numerous items of furniture smashed or broken.

Graham McLellan of the Spartanburg County Sheriff’s Office said: “Between the two children, we’re estimating that there were approximately 50 stab wounds.



“Some of the lacerations were so deep they cut to the bone.”

The horror injuries were described as very severe – with the boy facing possible amputation.

“He’s currently facing the possibility of amputation of fingers and possibly an arm due to the severity of the injury sustained” a court heard.

Police believe the attack was carried out in the early hours of the morning – meaning the children had been lying wounded for several hours.



The mum allegedly used a kitchen knife and a blunt object to attack the youngsters, according to investigators.

The children’s grandma and the mum’s ex-boyfriend alerted the police after walking into the home and finding the children alone with multiple stab wounds.

In a harrowing admission, McLellan said that “there is no preparation that our deputies can have” to see such a disturbing crime scene.

Investigators said the mum later returned to the family home, speaking rapidly and appearing distressed.



Officials were forced to handcuff her to a stretcher in an ambulance, according to the sheriff’s office.

She was later charged with two counts of attempted murder.

On Sunday the mum was denied bond – and was slapped with further warrants for posession of a weapon during a violent crime.

Both children are in stable conditon and are expected to recover, according to the sheriff’s office.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Heartbroken neighbours said they have been “deeply disturbed” by the news and did not hear anything happening.



Cheryl Bryant told news outlet CountOn2: “I’m just praying that they’re placed somewhere that they will be safe and taken care of.”

News.title: Brazen benefit cheat who said he was single to fleece £70k snared after romantic Facebook proposal
News.content:
CAUGHT OUT Brazen benefit cheat who said he was single to fleece £70k snared after romantic Facebook proposal







Next

A BENEFITS cheat was caught red handed through a proposal photo posted onto Facebook, after pocketing £70k in false claims.

Colin Christopher Hegarty, 58, said there was “no point in lying” after he was caught falsely claiming to be single in a bid to nab more benefits.

During the five-year period, Hegarty, from Blackpool, received £70,967.89 from tax-payers pockets while living happily with his partner.

A member of the public submitted a referral in June 2025 alleging that Hegarty was not declaring his true living arrangements.





A huge piece of evidence found by DWP investigators was a Facebook image showing Hegarty proposing to his partner and becoming engaged.

This already a huge piece of evidence, the DWP also found bank statements demonstrating financial links between the couple.

During an Interview Under Caution, Hegarty immediately admitted dishonestly claiming benefits as a single person.

He admitted failing to declare that his partner was living at his address, despite knowing it would affect his entitlement to Universal Credit.



Hegarty told investigators he believed declaring a partner would affect payments received by another non-dependant living in the property.

The court sentenced Colin Hegarty, to a 10-month custodial sentence, which was suspended for 12 months, as well as to 100 hours of unpaid work.

He is also expected to pay back the £70,967.89.

Minister for Innovation, Fraud and Data, Lilian Greenwood said:

“Benefit fraud is not a victimless crime. Every pound stolen is money that should be supporting those who genuinely need help and funding our public services.



“This claimant pocketed almost £71,000 by deliberately misleading the system for years but our investigators caught up with him.

“The message is simple, if you cheat the benefits system, you will be found, you will have to pay the money back, and you could face prosecution.

“And if you know someone defrauding the system, please report it.”

When receiving benefits, claimants must report changes in their circumstances promptly to ensure they receive the correct entitlement and avoid accruing debt.

Members of the public can report suspected benefit fraud online at gov.uk/report-benefit-fraud or via the National Benefit Fraud Hotline on 0800 854 440.



Reports can be made anonymously. DWP investigates all credible allegations and works with prosecutors where appropriate.

News.title: Pathetic mum, 29, sobs as judge slams her for ‘abandoning four children including baby at home alone to go on cruise’
News.content:
DISGRACED MUM Pathetic mum, 29, sobs as judge slams her for ‘abandoning four children including baby at home alone to go on cruise’







Next

A MUM accused of abandoning her four children including a newborn to go on a cruise sobbed in court as a judge blasted her alleged behaviour.

Nathalie Belizaire, 29, used her orange jumpsuit to wipe away tears as she was slammed for allegedly leaving the kids home alone for three days.



The suspect appeared in court on Tuesday – with Judge Mindy Glazer appearing shocked as she read out the allegations.

Belizaire, who was arrested as she disembarked the cruise, was told as she fought back tears: “We are just grateful nothing happened to these kids.”



The astonished judge said: “Who leaves four little kids alone?”

Miami cops cuffed Belizaire on Monday when she got off the Carnival Conquest after one of her children’s fathers reported they had been left alone.



He reportedly became concerned when he saw the mum post on social media about her holiday without the four youngsters.

When the dad went to Belizaire’s home to check, he could see a TV on and the children talking inside – but the mum was nowhere to be seen, according to her arrest report.



Emergency services rushed to the scene and broke in before recovering the kids.

They found “all four minor children inside without adult supervision”, the report says.

Police said the four children hid “together in the bathroom” during the raid.



It is currently unclear how old each of the children are.

But cops revealed one was two months old and the other was two years old.

After being arrested, Belizaire’s attorney said she denied the allegations.

Her lawyer told NBC6: “Of course she (denies the charges)…. One baby, the baby was born in July of this year. Who leaves a baby alone like that?”

Police say although Belizaire made arrangements for her grandma to look after the kids, the relative told cops she never showed up to drop them off.



The suspect allegedly texted her brother telling him to check on her four kids over the weekend.

When she was initially arrested, Belizaire was reportedly initially taken into custody by US Customs and Border Protection.

She was then transferred to local cops and now faces four counts of child neglect without great bodily harm.

Officials said Belizaire refused to give a statement to investigators.

Her bond has been set at £6,500.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

The judge also said according to reports: “You cannot make this up. It says she went on a cruise and left her children home alone.

“These poor kids, four of them, were home alone for three days… I’m just grateful nothing worse happened to these kids.”

News.title: Hospital worker suddenly realises she's having a heart attack after two telltale symptoms
News.content:
Hospital worker suddenly realises she's having a heart attack after two telltale symptoms

Pat feels fortunate her heart attack happened at the hospital where she worked for 50 years, allowing colleagues and specialist medics to quickly come to her aid

View 3 Images The hospital is now encouraging people to recognise the warning signs of a heart attack (Image: Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital)

A woman suffered a heart attack at the hospital where she has worked for five decades.

‌



Pat Ward, 70, began feeling unwell in a taxi on her way to Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital (LHCH), where she works as a switchboard call handler. By the time she arrived for her shift, the pain in her jaw and chest had got worse, and she feared something was seriously wrong.

‌



Pat said: "I arrived on switchboard and told my colleague Debbie that I felt unwell. By now I had jaw and chest pain which had gradually worsened, and it started to feel like my chest was caving in.

‌



"I remember saying to Debbie, ‘I think I’m having a heart attack’, and the rest doesn’t feel real now. It was like a bad dream."

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images Pat recovered from the life-saving procedure (Image: Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital)

‌



Her colleague immediately raised the alarm and specialists at the hospital sprang into action. Within a matter of minutes, Elcy Varughese, an advanced cardiology nurse practitioner arrived.

Elcy said: "I knew when I saw Pat that she was having a heart attack and we took her straight to the Cath Lab [cardiac catheterisation laboratory] where she was met by the specialist team."

Medics carried out an emergency treatment to unblock Pat’s coronary artery, restore blood flow and minimise any heart muscle damage.

‌



Pat said she was fortunate to have fallen ill where she did. She said: “Lucky for me, I was at the right place at the right time.”

The 70-year-old recovered following the life-saving procedure and received rehabilitation, which encouraged her to make “small changes to become more active, move more and go on walks”.

View 3 Images The ward staff had to restrict visitors due to colleagues visiting (Image: Liverpool Heart and Chest Hospital)

‌



Pat has since returned to work and has reflected on the care and support she received from colleagues during her recovery. She said: "At one point they had to restrict visiting on the ward because I had so many colleagues checking in to make sure I was ok – which was so lovely. The care was just fantastic – I was treated like a queen."

Dr Jonathan Hasleton, the consultant cardiologist who treated her, said: “Pat came to us at the point where minutes genuinely matter and the reason she did so well is that the people around her recognised what was happening and acted straight away.

“The message I would want people to take from Pat’s story is not to wait. If you have chest pain, or pain in the jaw, neck or arms, particularly with breathlessness, nausea or sweating, call 999,” he continued.

Article continues below

“People very often talk themselves out of it and that delay is what does the damage.”

The hospital is now encouraging people to recognise the warning signs of a heart attack and seek urgent medical help if they experience the below signs.

News.title: FlyDubai FZ1073 live: Pilot 'tries to crash' flight to Tel Aviv before 'stabbing'
News.content:
Reports suggest a pilot on FlyDubai flight FZ1073 may have tried to crash the plane before his colleague fought back control - passengers say there were 'screams' and thought they were going to die

A passenger flight heading from Dubai to Tel Aviv issued an emergency hijacking code amid claims one of the pilots may have tried to crash the aircraft in a suspected terror attack.

The accused pilot is being questioned, with growing indications that he wanted to take control of the plane and crash it, according to a senior Israeli official quoted by Israeli broadcaster Channel 12 (N12).

Israeli fighter jets were scrambled after FlyDubai flight FZ1073 issued the code 7500 alert. The plane had roughly 150 people on board, and Israeli channels report there was a fight between pilots before the alert was issued.

Passengers claimed there were "screams and blood" and even suggested one of the pilots was stabbed - although this is yet to be confirmed. They said they thought they were going to die as the plane descended rapidly, dropping 14,000ft in just 29 seconds.

The plane eventually headed to Saudi Arabia, an flights at Ben Gurion Airport in Tel Aviv were suspended. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Defence Minister Israel Katz held an urgent security consultation following the incident.

News.title: Hospital bans visitors amid outbreak of highly contagious Victorian disease
News.content:
Hospital bans visitors amid outbreak of highly contagious Victorian disease

Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli, Carmarthenshire, has restricted visitors and closed several wards since Sunday following an outbreak of scabies

View 2 Images The entrance to Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli (file image) (Image: John Myers)

A Welsh hospital has restricted visitors and closed several wards following an outbreak of scabies.

‌



Wards at Prince Philip Hospital in Llanelli, Carmarthenshire, have been closed and visitors restricted since Sunday because of the outbreak, Hywel Dda University Health Board said.

‌



The NHS says scabies is a common skin condition caused by a microscopic mite that can affect people of all ages. It is highly contagious and can spread through prolonged skin-to-skin contact or shared bedding or clothing, but it is not usually associated with serious illness and can be treated effectively.

‌



View 2 Images Scabies is a contagious skin infestation caused by a tiny mite (Image: Getty Images/Science Photo Library RF)

"A number of scabies cases are currently being managed in healthcare and community settings across the Hywel Dda area," which covers Pembrokeshire and Ceredigion, as well as Carmarthenshire, the health board said.

‌



The risk to the wider public remains "low", it added. Patients with planned appointments at the hospital may also be affected by the restrictions, and health bosses said they would contact those affected "as soon as possible".

Sharon Daniel, executive director of nursing, quality and patient experience at Hywel Dda University Health Board, said on Sunday: "We have taken the decision to restrict visitors to Prince Philip Hospital today to limit the spread of scabies on our site and in our community.

"A number of wards are currently closed due to infection and we need the support and understanding of our communities to limit further spread.

Article continues below

"We are taking direct action to treat patients, staff, and contacts, and undertake deep cleaning of our wards, in line with infection prevention control measures.

"Scabies is highly contagious and difficult to eradicate and we are grateful to everyone for their continued support. We will be contacting individuals whose planned care appointments may be impacted by this as soon as possible. This does not impact services provided by the minor injury unit."

In July, a ward at another Carmarthenshire hospital, Glangwili Hospital in Carmarthen, was closed following an outbreak of scabies, Wales Online reports.

News.title: Caroline Crouch's dad reveals her daughter, 6, still doesn't know her dad killed her mum in Athens
News.content:
Caroline Crouch's dad reveals her daughter, 6, still doesn't know her dad killed her mum in Athens

Helicopter pilot Babis Anagnostopoulos is serving a 27-year sentence in jail for murdering 19-year-old Caroline Crouch as she and their then 11-month-old daughter Lydia slept in their home

View 5 Images Caroline Crouch, 19, was murdered by her husband Babis Anagnostopoulos in May 2021

The dad of a British teenager brutally murdered by her husband in Greece has revealed her six-year-old daughter still doesn't know her own father killed her mum.

‌



Helicopter pilot Babis Anagnostopoulos is serving a 27-year sentence in jail for murdering 19-year-old Caroline Crouch as she and their then-11-month-old daughter Lydia slept in their home in Athens in May 2021. Anagnostopoulos callously protested his innocence for more than a month, claiming robbers had broken into their home, killing the family dog, stealing €15,000 (£12,825) cash and €25,000 (£21,375) worth of jewellery, then suffocating Caroline.

‌



His lies were eventually exposed after evidence on Caroline's Fitbit smartwatch refuted his story. Caroline’s dad David, 83, has a framed picture of his granddaughter on the wall of his home in Greece, where he has given a new interview from his bed.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 5 Images Caroline Crouch pictured with her killer husband Babis Anagnostopoulos and their daughter Lydia (Image: Copyright unknown)

Speaking about his granddaughter five years on, he said: "She doesn’t know about her mother, she doesn’t know that she was murdered by some Greek psychopath. I don't know when she'll be old enough to know. He will never meet her.

‌



"He's going to be in prison for a long time and when he gets out she'll be a teenager or 20 or something like that. She's six now so she'll probably be about 20 something. So he'll never meet her."

Lydia now lives in the Philippines with Caroline's mum Susan, who returned to her native country after Caroline's murder. David said: "She lives in the Philippines with her grandmother, goes to school like a normal child. She lives with Grandma Susan, just the two of them. She’s quite a normal six-year-old little girl. She’s a very beautiful little girl."

Asked if she asks about her mother, David, originally from Liverpool, said: "No, not really. She regards Susan, maybe not exactly a mother, but not a grandmother either. A sort of mother figure."

‌



View 5 Images Anagnostopoulos posted a picture of him and Caroline Crouch smiling and holding hands on their wedding day shortly before he was arrested (Image: Instagram)

He added: “Maybe one day she’ll ask where her mother is, her real mother. When she finds out where her mother is, maybe she’ll want to know what happened to her father and then she’ll be able to handle that. But I don’t think she’d want to meet him then.”

Five years on, David admits the pain caused by Caroline's murder has not eased. He said: "I still feel the same and I still feel the same about her killer. I hate him. I hate him with such a visceral feeling because he's a coward.

‌



"He's a little man. He's not very big and he couldn't even fight Caroline face-to-face. He had to wait until she was asleep before putting a pillow over her head. That's not the behaviour of a man. He's little, weak and a narcissist. He hates to be proved wrong."

Anagnostopoulos, 38, who attended a memorial for Caroline and hugged her mum before being arrested, is now studying law in jail. David, who admits he once "quite liked" his son-in-law and thought he was a "pleasant guy", said: "I don't understand why because he can't practice it. You know he never finished high school. He's not terribly smart."

David is pleased that Amazon Prime have made a documentary called The Fit Bit Killer about Caroline and her murder. He said: "I think it's wonderful because for two reasons: No one forgets her, and the second one is makes it more difficult for her killer to get parole."

‌



View 5 Images The murder, in the Glyka Nera suburb of Athens, shocked the world after Anagnostopoulos falsely claimed it was carried out by a burglarly gang (Image: Eurokinissi/REX/Shutterstock)

David's relationship with Caroline's mum Susan collapsed after the killing and she moved home to the Philippines with their granddaughter. He admits he did not consider moving with her in order to stay with Lydia. Asked if he misses his wife, he said: "I don't have a wife. Susan wasn't my wife and no, I don't miss her at all.

"Caroline was the center of my world. I came to Greece on my own and she was the first female companionship I found and we lived together for a while and she had Caroline. When Caroline was killed I lost all my feelings for Susan. When she went off to the Philippines, that was no problem for me."

‌



David has previously claimed that Anagnostopoulos, a helicopter pilot whose principal job was flying people around the Greek islands, wrote a letter to Susan telling her he was lured by the offer of big money to courier a consignment of drugs and killed Caroline on the orders of the gang after she objected and threatened to leave him. Anagnostopoulos and his family have denied the claim.

View 5 Images Caroline's dad David has described her as "the perfect daughter" (Image: Caroline Crouch/Instagram)

Paying tribute to Caroline, David said: “For me, Caroline was the perfect daughter. She was the center of my world. Not her mother, her mother was never the center of my world. Some of the happiest times of my life were when we lived in Alonissos. She had to come to Volos for the orthodontist to have her teeth straightened.

Article continues below

"Not that they were very crooked, but anyway I wanted her to have a perfect smile and we used to get the ferry in Volos. We used to get up to all manner of things. I'd say 'right, what do you want to do now?' and it was always the same thing. First we would go to the pet shop and buy some games and things for her favorite animals.

"Then we would go and sit on the quay in Volos and make up stories about all the people who walked past. We'd have a fine time, just the two of us. They were the happiest times of my life."

News.title: Fears diesel could be rationed as price of fuel hits record high
News.content:
Fears diesel could be rationed as price of fuel hits record high

Nick Butler, who spent 29 years at BP before leaving the company in 2006, said rising prices could see restrictions introduced to ensure vital services such as the NHS have enough supplies

View 2 Images Diesel prices are at a new record high (Image: Getty)

Fears of diesel rationing have been raised after a former BP executive said drivers could face “restraints” on filling up their vehicles this winter.

‌



Diesel prices hit a record 199.72p per litre on Wednesday, according to the RAC. Nick Butler, who spent 29 years at BP before leaving the company in 2006, said rising prices could see restrictions introduced to ensure vital services such as the NHS have enough supplies.

‌



Mr Butler said: “I could well see there are restraints being put in place over this winter on the use of diesel.” When asked if this would mean rationing for drivers, he added: “Yes, yes… if there’s a shortage, and if you have to protect key sectors, then there’s less for everyone else.”

‌



Petrol was last officially rationed in the UK in 1957. The country experienced widespread petrol station closures and shortages in 2021 as drivers panic bought fuel, though no Government restrictions were introduced.

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 2 Images Nick Butler spent 29 years at BP (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



It comes as Andy Burnham remains under pressure to scrap a planned fuel duty rise in the new year. Fuel duty is due to rise by 3p in January, then by another 2p in March, reversing a previous 5p cut that has been in place since March 2022.

The Prime Minister told BBC Breakfast he is looking at “every possible measure” to ease the cost of driving.

Asked whether he would halt the change, Mr Burnham said: “I’m considering everything that might help people in very difficult times and I will be honest and say every possible measure is being looked at.

‌



“The question I’ve got is: ‘How many can I afford? What can we do given the state of the public finances?’”

We also treat our community members to special offers, promotions, and adverts from us and our partners. If you don’t like our community, you can check out any time you like. If you’re curious, you can read our Privacy Notice. NEWSLETTER: Or sign up to the Mirror's Money newsletter here for all the best advice and shopping deals straight to your inbox.

On the BBC’s Today programme, asked whether the country was in an energy crisis that could last for months, he said: “I don’t think that is an overstatement, to be honest.

‌



“When I look at the prices at the pump at this moment in time, if we include diesel and petrol within that, this is very challenging, isn’t it, for people who are filling up today?

“When we look at energy prices in the home, difficult too.”

He said he was “doing what I can” but “it is very difficult indeed, and it’s why the Middle East situation needs to command a lot of our attention”.

Article continues below

RAC head of policy Simon Williams earlier this week said “the cost of filling up an average family car is now almost £110”. This was £31 more than it was at the start of the US-Iran war, at the end of February, he said.

He added: "The UK might have limited leverage when it comes to ending the US-Iran war and ultimately bringing oil prices down, but the Government could take steps to ease the burden on drivers by lowering fuel duty further or reducing VAT."

News.title: Met Police asks for manslaughter charges to be considered over Grenfell Tower fire that killed 72
News.content:
Met Police asks for manslaughter charges to be considered over Grenfell Tower fire that killed 72

The Met Police has shared a major update in the investigation into the deadly Grenfell tower blaze - the force has passed evidence into the CPS for charging decisions

View 2 Images The Met has forwarded files on the Grenfell Tower fire to prosecutors (Image: PA)

The Metropolitan Police revealed it has asked for manslaughter charges in relation to the Grenfell fire as it passed files on 20 companies and 54 individuals to prosecutors.

‌



The deadly blaze in June 2017 in North Kensington, west London, claimed the lives of 72 people and was found by a public inquiry to have been avoidable. The Met it identified 20 organisations and 54 individuals as suspects for criminal offences, as it sent 20 files to the Crown Prosecution Service to allow them to make charging decisions.

‌



The Met said it has asked the CPS to consider potential offences of corporate manslaughter, gross negligence manslaughter, health and safety offences, fraud and fraud-related offences, and misconduct in public office.

‌



View 2 Images The Grenfell Tower fire claimed 72 lives (Image: PA)

The Crown Prosecution Service has vowed to make charging decisions in the case before the 10th anniversary of the disaster, which falls on June 14 2027.

Deputy Assistant Commissioner Kevin Southworth said: "This is a milestone moment in the police investigation into this devastating tragedy which took the lives of 72 people. Our dedicated team of 220 investigators has worked incredibly hard to honour our commitment to the bereaved, survivors, residents and all those affected by the fire to meet this timescale.

‌



"We appreciate, of course, it has taken nine years to get to this point. As we have said before, this is one of the most complex investigations ever undertaken by any UK law enforcement agency - the scale is truly enormous.

"While we know this has had a significant impact on those waiting for answers, it has necessarily taken this long to ensure our investigation is meticulous and presents the very best possible evidence to the CPS for charging decisions."

Grenfell United, which represents some bereaved families and survivors, said: "We expect the Met and the CPS to do everything in their power to make sure this case moves forward without further unnecessary delay. Our families have waited long enough.

‌



"We want those responsible to face justice. If people are found guilty of crimes that cost our loved ones their lives, we want to see them behind bars. Only then will people see that there are real consequences for what happened at Grenfell. No family should have to fight this hard, for this long, for justice."

Frank Ferguson, head of the CPS Special Crime and Counter Terrorism Division, said: "Today marks an important step in the Grenfell Tower investigation, and we understand the enduring impact this tragedy continues to have on bereaved families, survivors and all those affected.

"We recognise that the journey to this point has been long and difficult, and we do not underestimate the toll it has taken on those seeking answers and accountability. Charging decisions will be made independently by CPS prosecutors following a thorough and careful review of all the evidence gathered by the Metropolitan Police Service.

Article continues below

We remain confident that we will complete this process and make charging decisions before the 10th anniversary of the fire on June 14 2027."

The police investigation into the deadly fire looked into more than 15,000 individuals and 700 organisations. The Met said it has also sent 14 overarching evidence files to the CPS.

News.title: New Lidl £9 jacket ‘with high collar’ just like £40 H&M in all stores on Sunday
News.content:
New Lidl £9 jacket ‘with high collar’ just like £40 H&M in all stores on Sunday

Lidl is set to launch a jacket that bears a striking resemblance to a high-end option at H&M

View 3 Images Coming to a Lidl near you this week (Image: Getty Images)

High-end fashion doesn't have to come with a bumper price tag, something Lidl is hoping to prove with its latest clothing collection coming to stores later this week. The supermarket is selling a jacket that bears an uncanny resemblance to a more premium alternative at a rival retailer.

‌



The ESMARA Ladies Beige Teddy Fleece Jacket will arrive in the iconic 'Middle of Lidl Aisle' on Sunday, October 4. Priced at just £8.99, shoppers can pick up what appears to be a fluffy and comfortable design complete with a zip fastening and two oversized pockets.

‌



Interested buyers will need to pick one up in-store, as home delivery is unavailable. To avoid a wasted trip, shoppers can use Lidl's online store finder, where entering a postcode brings up nearby branches and allows customers to view the latest offers available at their local store.

‌



Product features - full list

View 3 Images The ESMARA Ladies Beige Teddy Fleece Jacket at Lidl (Image: Lidl)

Soft and comfortable brushed lining

With high collar and full zip

Pockets with warm lining

Sizes: S-L

Made from 100 per cent polyester, the jacket comes in a soft beige shade that could really suit the autumn and winter vibes. For more information, and to have a more detailed look at the clothing item, make sure to visit the Lidl website where you can also browse similar items also on sale.

‌



It could prove a budget-friendly alternative to a premium-looking jacket available at H&M, where the Oversized Teddy Jacket is priced at £39.99 - more than four times the cost of Lidl's offering.

View 3 Images The Oversized Teddy Jacket at H&M (Image: H&M)

At a glance, the two jackets may look remarkably similar, but there are some differences shoppers will want to know about. H&M's version is available in three colours - light beige, dark brown and dark mole - and in additional sizes.

Article continues below

"Oversized jacket in soft teddy with trims in coated fabric," reads the product description on the H&M website. "Features a funnel collar, two-way zip down the front and large side pockets. Lined."

H&M shoppers will face a £3.99 standard home delivery fee unless they are signed up to the fashion giant's popular loyalty app Hotukdeals. Under the retailer's strict shipping rules, loyalty members get completely free standard shipping but only if they hit a minimum £40 spend threshold.

Bargain hunters looking to bypass the cost altogether can opt for Click and Collect, which remains entirely free for all customers collecting from a local branch. However, if you are in a rush to refresh your wardrobe, Next-Day delivery will set you back £5.99, while ordering partner labels or bulky items comes with a steep premium, scaling all the way up to £24.99 for heavy goods.

News.title: Beautiful village with beach and independent shops that's lovely in the colder months
News.content:
Beautiful village with beach and independent shops that's lovely in the colder months

The village has cobbled streets and a dog-friendly beach with rock pools and fossils, with plenty more to do if the weather isn't on your side

View 3 Images One visitor said the views from the village were "outstanding" (Image: Eric Latham via Getty Images)

A stunning UK village which boasts gorgeous cobbled streets, plenty of independent shops and cafes and a beautiful beach could be the ideal place for an autumnal or winter staycation.

‌



Robin Hood's Bay, which is located in North Yorkshire, boasts a sandy shoreline complete with rock pools and fossils waiting to be discovered, alongside a host of cafés and eateries for visitors to enjoy.

‌



While it's pretty busy during the summer months, it's equally lovely to visit when the weather isn't so good, as the views are spectacular and there's so much to keep you entertained indoors as well.

‌



The beach has been named as the UK's very best winter beach spot by the experts at Holiday Cottages, thanks to the beautiful coastal walks which are all the more satisfying when it's a bit chillier out. The shore itself is dog-friendly and there are plenty of rock pools to look at.

View 3 Images (Image: Peter Shaw via Getty Images)

The Robin Hood's Bay and Fylingdales Museum, nestled in the heart of the village, gives visitors the chance to browse collections and displays of local significance. Just a mile south of Robin Hood's Bay lies Boggle Hole, a quaint cove that has been gradually carved out by the North Sea.

‌



It can be accessed via the Cleveland Way footpath, which treats walkers to spectacular views across the bay. The spot is a firm favourite amongst fossil hunters and welcomes dogs too.

One visitor raved: "It is a lovely little walk from the village, fantastic views, and the added bonus of fossil hunting along the way."

One TripAdvisor reviewer noted it had been "recommended as a good place to find fossils and not too crowded", adding: "Much to my son's delight we found five fossils quite quickly and had a lovely time skimming stones."

‌



View 3 Images The beach has been named one of the UK's best in colder months (Image: Andy Commins / Daily Mirror)

For those keen to delve into the area's rich history, the Old Coastguard Station is a National Trust centre situated at the edge of the village. Visitors can discover the region's geology, the effects of climate change on the coastline, and the abundance of local wildlife.

There's also a café serving sandwiches, pasties, hot drinks and ice cream, along with a selection of second-hand books to browse through.

Article continues below

One beachgoer wrote on TripAdvisor: "Fabulous historic village where every step and corner reveals another fantastic view and makes you fall in love with this gorgeous place again."

Another raved about the "thrilling drive down" to the beach, noting they thoroughly enjoyed the walks around the "amazing location". A third visitor added: "The whole area is stunning. Beautiful cliffs, great walking paths, and the town itself. Heaving in summer but better in other months."

Yet another commented: "The views around are outstanding. It's really so very pretty down there I can't recommend highly enough."

News.title: Move to rejoin EU among options for UK, says Burnham
News.content:
Speaking to BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Burnham said he did not want to leave the question of the EU relationship "hanging" and he wanted to be clear on "where we want Britain to go in the next decade".

Asked whether he wanted the UK to rejoin the EU, he replied that he wanted to "look at the options".

He added he had previously advocated such a move within his lifetime, whilst acknowledging it was "not necessarily the case that that is now".

"We could stay as we are. That's definitely an option, if people think this is the right place to stay," he told the programme.

"We could look at what [former Chancellor] George Osborne has said about a customs union, we could look at what the Liberal Democrats said at their conference about the single market, or we could go all the way."

"So there are clearly options that need to be considered, and we have to look at what is doable and what would be the pros and cons of each," he added.

Jukka Salovaara, the EU's ambassador to the UK, said last week: "The doors are open but it's very much up to the UK public to identify and decide on its level of ambition when it comes to deepening cooperation with the EU."

Lib Dem leader Sir Ed Davey said his party has put forward "concrete plans to boost our economy, strengthen our defences and cut people's taxes by joining the single market and a customs union".

He added: "Talk is cheap. Burnham must stop with all the 'maybes' and get negotiating that better deal for Britain today."

The party's Europe spokesperson Al Pinkerton said last week there is "no rejoin on the table", adding Britain would effectively be treated as a "fresh entrant state" if it wished to join the bloc again.

Pinkerton also said the British public need to be "with you in a sustainable way" and the UK would have to show to its European partners that "it's in their advantage too that Britain re-engages".

Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice accused Burnham of "trying to sneak us back into Brussels via the back door".

Tice said: "He says Brexit has done more harm than good but what's done real harm is a Labour government that can't deliver growth, can't control migration and now wants to outsource the job to Brussels."

He added Reform would "never let this betrayal go unchallenged".

In his conference speech on Tuesday, Burnham blamed Brexit for a loss of control over both immigration and the economy, telling delegates he did not believe the current relationship was "good enough".

He told activists he wanted to use the rescheduled summit later this year to lay out "different options" for the UK's long-term relationship with Europe.

He promised to "find consensus" on an option to clarify the UK's position, although did not offer further detail of how this would be measured.

In response to Burnham's conference speech, Conservative deputy leader Alex Burghart said: "Labour cannot pin the blame for their disastrous economic decisions on a vote that happened over a decade ago.

"Besides, they are already dragging us into the European Union via the back door with their EU reset."

News.title: One of the five men arrested near RAF Fairford called 999 himself
News.content:
Police were alerted to "three suspicious vehicles" in Whelford, a village which lies directly east of the base, by the farmer.

She told the BBC it was "pure luck" she had spotted them, having arrived home to find the road blocked and a "large group of hooded and masked men".

"I believe that my 999 call foiled whatever plans they had," she said.

In the latest development - first reported by the Times newspaper - it is claimed the suspect called police almost an hour before a local farmer also raised the alarm.

A bomb disposal team arrived on scene shortly afterwards and a 400m (1,312ft) cordon was put in place.

But Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of Counter Terrorism Policing, told reporters on Tuesday that the police response that morning had been due to "a range of information".

Police cordons near the base are expected to be completely lifted on Wednesday, while residents from the 85 homes evacuated on Sunday have been allowed to return to their properties.

The five men are all UK nationals aged between 23 and 25. Four of them live in Westminster and one in Camden, and searches of their homes are now complete.

Taylor previously said their bail was "subject to stringent conditions on their movement and contact with others" as they remained under investigation.

"The safety of the public is at the forefront of our investigative decision-making, and this was certainly the case yesterday," he said on Tuesday.

"I understand why this development was surprising to some, but I would like to reiterate that this is an investigative decision and one which is grounded in experience and strategy."

The RAF base has been used as a forward operating location by the US Air Force for decades.

In recent months, US bombers have taken off from the base for the Middle East, after the UK approved a US request to use it for defensive strikes on Iran.

US President Donald Trump on Tuesday told journalists he was "disappointed" the five men had been released on bail.

News.title: Household energy bills forecast to see biggest rise in four years
News.content:
Household energy prices are set to soar in January, with a typical annual bill forecast to jump by Â£276, figures shared with the BBC reveal.

The 16% predicted increase would hit millions of households at the coldest time of year, and would mark the biggest rise in bills for four years.

The forecast from consultancy Cornwall Insight comes a day before prices go up under regulator Ofgem's October price cap and puts increased pressure on the government to support those who will struggle to pay.

Meanwhile, the boss of supplier EDF Simone Rossi has warned the UK is "walking into a second energy crisis" and called for an extension to the VAT cut on electricity which kicks in on Thursday.

News.title: Sussexes condemn 'reckless intrusion' after men spotted near Archie and Lilibet's school
News.content:
The BBC understands that the two men were observed by both private security and school staff, stopping at various points and looking into the school grounds, before returning to a van which police later established was a rental vehicle.

One of the men was later identified to be an international photographer is believed to work for a known European press agency.

"The decision by photographers to conduct themselves in this way around a school is extraordinarily reckless," Harry and Meghan's spokesman said.

"There is a world of difference between legitimate media activity and photographers walking the perimeter of a school, stopping to look into the grounds and monitoring children as they go about their day."

The spokesman continued: "Whatever photographs they may have been seeking, this was not only an unacceptable intrusion into the privacy of children; it was an irresponsible and ill-considered way to conduct themselves in the vicinity of a school."

The children began school in the UK at the start of September, but changed after a few days after security concerns were raised about traffic during the school run.

Earlier this month, it emerged that the Sussexes are going to be given a review of their publicly funded security, following their move back.

News.title: Man City charges leave football fans questioning legitimacy of team's achievements
News.content:
Outside Manchester City's Etihad Stadium is a lustrous silver statue of Sergio Aguero - mouth agape in ecstasy, kit swirling over his head - depicting his goal celebration after securing the club's first Premier League title.

It is the immortalisation of the most famous goal in English league football history, when City snatched the trophy away from Manchester United in the dying seconds of the 2011-12 season.

But what if the goal never happened? What if Aguero had never played for the club? What if City had opted to abide by football's financial rules instead of purposefully breaking them through a "disguised funding scheme"?

The revelation that the club has been found guilty of the charges brought against it by the Premier League three and a half years ago has left football fans around the world questioning the legitimacy of City's achievements between 2009 and 2018, when they were the most successful club in English football and cemented themselves among the global game's elite.

Some fans are referring to it as the asterisk era, and there is a possibility City could be retroactively stripped of the honours they earned during the period, with some clubs seeking legal advice over potential financial compensation.

So how exactly did City's "hugely overstated" income impact their actions in the transfer market, how key were the players who were brought in, and what does it all mean for both the past and the future?

News.title: Police seek charges against 20 firms and 54 people over Grenfell Tower fire
News.content:
The Metropolitan Police has submitted its final investigation file into the Grenfell Tower fire to the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS), seeking charges against 54 individuals and 20 companies.

These include corporate manslaughter, gross negligence manslaughter, health and safety offences, fraud and fraud-related offences and misconduct in public office.

The Met described the case into the fire which killed 72 people at the tower block in North Kensington, west London, as one of the "most complex investigations ever undertaken by any UK law enforcement agency".

The CPS said charging decisions would be made before the 10th anniversary of the disaster, which is on 14 June 2027.

The Met said it had spent Â£150m on Operation Northleigh - its investigation into the fire - which has examined the actions of 15,000 people across 700 organisations.

A public inquiry report released in 2024 found the fire was avoidable and set out how a chain of failures across government and the private sector led to the disaster.

Grenfell United, a bereaved families and survivors group, said "no family should have to fight this hard, for this long, for justice".

"It has taken more than nine years to get here. Nine years, and no one has been held criminally accountable for the deaths of our 72 loved ones.

"We want those responsible to face justice. If people are found guilty of crimes that cost our loved ones their lives, we want to see them behind bars.

"Only then will people see that there are real consequences for what happened at Grenfell."

News.title: Greggs to shut four factories and cut 740 jobs
News.content:
High street bakery brand Greggs has announced plans to shut four of its factories and cut 740 jobs.

It plans to close manufacturing sites at North Lakes near Penrith, Cumbria, Pettigrews in Kelso, Scotland, Seaham in County Durham and Enfield, Greater London, though distribution operations would continue to run from the latter.

The proposals will also impact manufacturing operations at its Treforest site in Wales, but this will also continue as a distribution centre for the business.

The chain, which has headquarters in Newcastle, said its retail shops would not be affected by the proposed changes.

The changes would take place over the next two-and-a-half years, with parts of Greggs' manufacturing processes relocating, the firm said.

The range of products manufactured at its Clydesmill Glasgow and Manchester locations would be reduced and production of tinned bread at Gosforth would be stopped.

Some products would also be sourced from specialist suppliers.

News.title: Regulating AI 'not the right place to start' says Bailey
News.content:
The Governor of the Bank of England has said regulating artificial intelligence (AI) "is not the right place to start" but instead called first for "rigorous" testing to find vulnerabilities and safeguards to contain risk.

Writing his first-ever article for Substack, Andrew Bailey said the risks around AI were "real and increasingly significant".

Bailey said the development of AI should not be halted or prohibited - "on the contrary, the benefits are immense" - but added there must be a system for intervention and to establish boundaries in which AI operates.

In recent weeks, the debate about the potential risks surrounding the rapid development of AI and what it means for humanity has intensified.

The bosses of leading AI firms such as Anthropic and OpenAI have called for development of the technology to slow down and for an internationally co-ordinated approach assessing risks and putting safeguards in place.

OpenAI recently announced that it would not release its latest AI model due to safety concerns.

The idea of a slowdown, however, has been rejected by the likes of President Donald Trump who has said the US is leading the AI race ahead of China, adding: "And, frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins."

But on Tuesday, after hosting a summit with the leading firms in AI such as OpenAI and Anthropic, Trump said executives had signed a "morally binding" document that would serve as a "form of protection" from AI's potential risks.

News.title: Antisemitism on the rise at universities, charity warns
News.content:
Cases of antisemitism affecting university students and staff in the UK increased in the last academic year, according to a charity that monitors antisemitic incidents.

The Community Security Trust (CST) said it had recorded 95 "university-related" incidents in the 2025-26 academic year - up from 83 the year before.

It said the number had fallen from its peak in the year after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023 and the war in Gaza began, but remains "substantially higher" than before that point.

Universities UK (UUK) represents more than 140 institutions and said its members needed to "protect Jewish students and staff", adding that the findings were a "serious concern".

Lucy Powell, education secretary in England, said the findings in the CST report were "deeply troubling".

"We expect universities to take a zero-tolerance approach to antisemitism, and are providing training to help university staff identify and respond to incidents swiftly," she said.

The CST defines an antisemitic incident as "university-related" if it concerns a student, member of staff or academic at a UK university "in their academic or student capacity" - including on campus and online.

In 2022-23, the last academic year before the 7 October attack, the CST recorded 53 incidents. That grew to 272 in 2023-24.

A report from the charity examining the past two academic years says reported incidents fell in 2024-25 and but grew again in 2025-26.

News.title: More talks over Drumcree dispute as stalemate continues
News.content:
Northern Ireland Secretary Sir Chris Bryant is holding further talks with community leaders on Wednesday over the controversial Drumcree march.

It comes after lawyers for the Garvaghy Road Residents Coalition issued a fresh legal bid to try to prevent the march from going ahead.

Members of the Orange Order are still waiting to begin their permitted parade, which was due to take place on Sunday, and walk down the mainly-nationalist Garvaghy Road in Portadown.

The residents' appeal will be the latest challenge to the march, which was given the go ahead after three separate legal hearings over the course of 13 hours late on Saturday and into the early hours of Sunday morning.

Wednesday's talks at Hillsborough Castle are taking place in an upstairs room which, under normal circumstances, is used as a sitting room.

The Garvaghy Road Residents' Coalition and the Portadown Orange Order will wait in separate rooms before going upstairs for talks with the secretary of state.

News.title: Family told to call locksmith over mental health fears
News.content:
The police watchdog has criticised a force after call handlers told a family raising mental health concerns to ring a locksmith.

On 6 August 2025, Hobie Harrison's parents called Norfolk Police to request a welfare check after he failed to respond to them. He was found dead the next day.

The Independent Office for Police Conduct (IOPC) said the force's 101 call handlers should have referred the family to mental health services, but instead suggested they contacted a locksmith.

Norfolk Police said it was reviewing the findings and it had been following the force's Right Care, Right Person (RCRP) policy, external, which limits officer attendance at welfare calls to cases involving "immediate risk to life".

The IOPC said the call handlers should have asked more probing questions to assess Hobie's level of risk and there should have been a better explanation to his parents about why officers were not sent under its RCRP guidelines.

Hobie's parents, Mark and Roberta Harrison, made a second request for a welfare check for their son to Norfolk Police the following day. Officers attended and found the 30-year-old dead in his flat in Norwich.

News.title: 'He was deeply loved': Tribute to former UK school pupil killed in Ukraine
News.content:
A former pupil at a Scottish high school has been killed in action on the frontline in Ukraine.

Arkadii Petrov and his family moved to Dumfries and Galloway when he was a teenager, following Russia's invasion in 2022.

He attended Kirkcudbright Academy before returning to Ukraine to fight and was killed in action in the east of the country.

His mother, Liudmyla, said he was "funny, bright, very charismatic and full of life" and had been an "incredibly loving brother" to his younger sisters and brother.

News.title: Huel ad banned for suggesting its products could replace all meals
News.content:
An advert for Huel meal replacement shakes has been banned by the advertising watchdog for encouraging or condoning "irresponsible" dietary practices.

The ad featured Huel brand ambassador Spencer Matthews sharing an anecdote of a person he met who "only eats Huel" and who won a 260km race "by miles".

The Advertising Standards Authority (ASA) said that viewers could assume from the ad that replacing all conventional food with Huel was "nutritionally appropriate" and was compatible with elite physical performance.

Huel said Matthews' anecdote was not "a recommendation or instruction" and the purpose of the ad was to challenge the misconception that Huel could replace every meal".

The video, which appeared as a sponsored Instagram post and YouTube pre-roll ad, featured Matthews speaking to Huel founder Julian Hearn in the style of a podcast.

The Instagram post included the caption: "Here's how our founder uses Huel. Spoiler alert it's not for every meal."

In the video Hearn said that he has Huel products for breakfast and lunch during the working week, but has a "traditional meal" when he goes home.

In response, Matthews said that when he was competing in an ultramarathon, he met a man who "only eats Huel".

Matthews said he was initially sceptical that the man would be able to manage the race, but then said: "He won it by miles, like literally just left us all in the dirt."

Hearn replied: "In an ideal world, you should have nutritionally complete whole food.

"Most people either don't do that or can't have the time to do that, and therefore that's where Huel fits in the gap."

News.title: Strikes not what we signed up for say Nottingham students as staff walk out
News.content:
A student has said she feels "shorthanded" as staff at University of Nottingham are to go on strike until December.

The University and College Union (UCU) said its members would strike on Wednesday and Thursday and would then carry out "sustained strike action" from 5 October to 11 December over the Future Nottingham restructuring plans.

A spokesperson for the University of Nottingham said it was "disappointed" by the timing of industrial action, adding many students would be "unaffected" by the strikes.

Zoe Monroe, who studies English literature with creative writing, told the BBC the strikes were not what students had signed up for.

The university said previously the proposals could involve programme closures and academic restructure.

It added it had reviewed and considered all Future Nottingham counterproposals, which would now go to the University Council for a decision.

The university had suspended music and language courses and planned hundreds of job cuts earlier this year to deal with "significant financial challenges".

Union members from UCU, Unison and Unite voted in July in favour of a motion of no confidence in the vice-chancellor and other senior leaders after a "complete breakdown of trust".

The first two days of action have been planned to coincide with the university's council meeting at which the final business case for cuts will be considered.

The strike will also include action short of a strike, such as only working to contract and not covering for absent colleagues, the UCU said.

News.title: Leaving your engine running in Wales could cost you £150
News.content:
Drivers in Wales who leave their vehicle engine running while parked will face fines of up to Â£150 from Wednesday.

The change is part of a new measure by the Welsh government to try to reduce harmful pollution and to protect children's health.

The previous punishment for idling, as it is known, was Â£20, but that has now been raised to anywhere from Â£75 to Â£150, depending on circumstances.

The Welsh government said it hoped the increase would "change the habits of people who are polluting communities".

Llyr Gruffydd, cabinet minister for rural resilience and sustainability, said the Â£20 fixed fine for idling was "insufficient", and not being used "in the way everyone might envision it".

Increasing the fee that is available for local authorities to penalise drivers will be a "stronger deterrent", he added.

"We really do feel we need to step up here, clamp down on this as a problem and make sure we protect people's health and generally it will make communities a better place to live in."

Gruffydd said he hoped the higher range of fines would "change the habits of people who are polluting communities and are putting children and vulnerable people's health at risk".

News.title: 'Whole village' turns out for FA Cup row replay
News.content:
A non-league football club has thanked supporters after "the whole village" came out to support them as they won a controversial FA Cup replay.

The original meeting between Mulbarton Wanderers and Woodford Town made international headlines after the Football Association (FA) made the rare decision to order a replay due to a referee's error.

A record crowd of 806 people attended the match in Norfolk, with Wanderers sealing progress thanks to a 2-0 win.

The victory brought with it Â£3,375 from the FA Cup prize fund and a home tie against Gloucester City in the third qualifying round of the world's oldest football competition.

Danny Self, the joint first team manager at Mulbarton, said: "We're over the moon that we've given the fans something to shout out about. Their support was incredible to have."

Victory in Saturday's next round would leave Mulbarton a win away from a potentially lucrative first round proper tie with EFL sides including Sheffield Wednesday and 2021 FA Cup winners Leicester City.

"[To our supporters] see you again on Saturday," the club's other joint boss Ben Thompson said.

"It will be the biggest game in our history and we need the fans again. They're our 12th man".

Mulbarton had to introduce advance ticketing because of "unprecedented demand" due to the tie's media attention.

Ashley Jarvis, who scored both of Mulbarton's goals, added: "It was a great atmosphere. The whole village came out and we're delighted to get the win."

Andy Burnham’s drive to forge closer links with the European Union – including opening the door to reversing Brexit – has partly been inspired by a major interview that The Independent carried out with former chancellor George Osborne.

As first revealed by The Independent earlier this week, the prime minister is looking at a number of options about reversing Brexit, including fully rejoining the EU.

Speaking on BBC Breakfast, Mr Burnham quoted an exclusive interview with Mr Osborne byThe Independent’s editor in chief Geordie Greig where the former chancellor called for the UK to rejoin the customs union.

While the status quo is also on the table in the options Mr Burnham is considering, he made it clear that he thinks “Brexit has done more harm than good.”

open image in gallery George Osborne in conversation with The Independent editor-in-chief Geordie Greig ( The Independent )

He said: “We could look at what (former Conservative chancellor) George Osborne has said about a customs union, we could look at what the Liberal Democrats said at their conference about the single market – or we could go all the way.”

The Independent’s Europe: The Way Back campaign has been at the heart of a new push to forge closer links with Europe and has been helped shine a light on the harms of Brexit.

A major debate is set to be taking place in the Commons on 12 October on whether the UK wants to rejoin the EU. But privately the majority of Mr Burnham’s cabinet support the idea, although have concerns about political risks with a resurgence of Nigel Farage’s Reform UK.

In his speech to the Labour conference in Liverpool, Mr Burnham said: “I will say it straight. Britain has been on the wrong path for a long time. Deindustrialisation. Deregulation. Privatisation. Austerity. Brexit.

“And what has it given us? A country run for vested interests. Not in the public interest. With power held in too few hands. And too many places left to drift.”

He added: “Brexit hasn’t given us control. We’ve lost some of the control we had over our economy, as a decade of low growth has put us in a weaker position. And we’ve lost some of our control over immigration,” he said.

open image in gallery Burnham made it clear rejoin is now back on the table ( AFP/Getty )

Mr Burnham said he would set out “options” on UK-EU relations later this year, telling members that Britain must decide on its “long-term relationship” with the bloc.

Later, first secretary of state Louise Haigh told BBC Radio 4 that “the current settlement [with the EU] is not working for Britain”, and when asked whether a pledge to rejoin could be included, said Labour’s red lines “will remain in place for the duration of this parliament”.

However, as with other reforms such as ending the pension triple lock guarantee, introducing a new national care service and nationalising water, energy and housing it was clear that a reversal of Brexit will feature in the next manifesto.

Ms Haigh added: “Brexit has harmed our economy, has harmed our security, and has harmed our ability to control our borders.

“And later this year, Hamish Falconer in my team will lead the UK government negotiations [with the EU] to get a food deal and an energy deal that will help drive down prices for consumers here in this country.

“But that's not enough. It's not enough to substantially improve our position.”

One minister told The Independent that “it is not if but how” the pledge on Brexit is phrased.

But Reform UK deputy leader Richard Tice told The Independent that Mr Burnham was “trying to sneak us back into Brussels via the back door”.

“He says Brexit has done more harm than good but what's done real harm is a Labour government that can't deliver growth, can't control migration and now wants to outsource the job to Brussels,” he said.

Naomi Smith, chief executive of Best for Britain, which campaigns for the UK to restore its EU membership, said: “It’s vital the Labour government seizes this moment, not in 2029 or a year, or six months time. With the public behind him, progressives imploring them, and the economic case etched in stone, we should signal to the EU - today - that the UK is ready to apply for membership, to take us back to where we belong at the heart of Europe.”

As prime minister Andy Burnham looks at the way ahead for Britain's relationship with Europe, The Independent has been leading the charge, campaigning to secure the absolute best deal for Britain.
