A marble sculpture bought at a reclamation yard for £300 is expected to fetch as much as £100,000 at auction after being identified as the work of a celebrated Italian master sculptor.

The 290-year-old Italian marble maquette, depicting Pope Clement XII Corsini, was discovered by a keen-eyed builder at a salvage yard in Wiltshire.

Originating from a Hampshire country house near Andover, the weathered artwork had been mistaken for concrete by the owners of the yard.

However, the buyer suspected the piece might be special, and his modest gamble is now set to yield a significant return.

The work, which stands 26 inches (just over two foot) tall, was produced by Italian Baroque master Pietro Bracci, who is famous for sculpting the central figure of Rome's iconic Trevi Fountain.

open image in gallery Auctioneer Mark Yuan Richards with the marble maquette ( ZacharyCulpin/BNPS )

He sculpted the Pope maquette as a preparatory model for a monumental bronze figure that once stood in the Great Hall of the Palazzo Nuovo on Rome's Capitoline.

Because the original statue no longer exists, this piece is believed to be the only surviving maquette, making it both important and rare.

The seller, who is remaining anonymous, has consigned the artwork to Salisbury-based auctioneers Woolley & Wallis.

Although given a pre-sale estimate of £10,000, the sculpture could reach 10 times that amount following substantial international interest in the lot ahead of the sale date.

Mark Yuan Richards, Woolley & Wallis furniture specialist, said: "This is an exceptionally exciting discovery.

"To have a rare eighteenth-century marble figure of Pope Clement XII by Pietro Bracci come to light, and now be offered for sale, is a remarkable opportunity.

"Bracci was one of the great sculptors of eighteenth-century Rome, and this extraordinary survivor offers a tangible connection to the world of the papal court and the artistic splendour of the period."

open image in gallery Pietro Bracci sculpted the central figure in Rome’s iconic Trevi Fountain ( City of Rome Major Events, Sport, Tourism and Fashion Department )

The seller is not a professional antiques dealer, but has an "eye" for it, Mr Yuan Richards said.

"He found it at a reclamation yard in the last couple of months. They thought it was concrete so he bought it for £300, then realised it was marble.

"He had a feeling it was good, but he didn't know it was signed or how important it was.

"It is in quite weathered condition, it's been in a garden outside for maybe 50 years so it's not in perfect condition but it's pretty much unique.

"The original bronze was melted down and the only known representation before this was an engraving of it.

"How it ended up in a garden in Hampshire we don't know. It might have been gifted to a Brit on a Grand Tour in the 18th century or a diplomatic gift for someone who knew the pope.

"We've had international interest already and it's still early days. It's hard to predict because Bracci works don't come onto the market hardly ever."

open image in gallery The artwork is signed by Baroque master Pietro Bracci ( ZacharyCulpin/BNPS )

Bracci was a prominent creative figure in 18th-century Rome with a distinguished career, also crafting portraits and tombs for Popes Benedict XIII and XIV.

Commissioned in 1736 and funded by the Roman Senate, the bronze was created to commemorate the pope's gift to the Capitoline Museums.

Pope Clement XII restored papal finances and led a major programme of artistic, civic, and architectural renewal during his decade in power from 1730-1740, which included starting the Trevi Fountain project.

The pope's bronze statue did not remain long at the Palazzo Nuovo; it was moved and later melted down in 1798 during the First Republic.

Prior to the discovery of this marble maquette, an engraving by Stefano and Rocco Pozzi was the only known image of the bronze.

The sculpture goes on sale on 8 October.

A pilot on a flight from Dubai to Israel allegedly stabbed his co-pilot in an attempted hijacking in midair, according to reports.

Israeli fighter jets were scrambled after Flydubai Flight FZ1073 dramatically descended nearly 14,000 feet in less than 30 seconds as it veered off course on Wednesday morning, FlightRadar data shows.

A witness told the Jerusalem Post that one pilot stabbed the other before passengers near the front of the plane forced the attacker out of the cockpit. Two other pilots who were onboard helped land the flight.

Yasmin Abu Kasis, whose ⁠daughter Miriam was on the flight, said that her daughter had told her that she had heard screaming and that a man took a knife, put the pilot on the floor, and that there was blood everywhere. Pictures shared on social media showed passengers with clothes covered in blood.

If you or anyone you know have been impacted by this incident and would like to share your story, please email alex.croft@independent.co.uk

An Israeli official said a “major disaster was narrowly avoided”, according to the outlet, which reported that the Israeli security agencies including the IDF, Mossad and Shin Bet believe the incident may have been intended as an act of terror.

open image in gallery This Flightradar24 map shows a flydubai flight to Israel which was diverted to Saudi Arabia ( Reuters )

Flightradar said an emergency call was made declaring an “unlawful interference” at 05:38 UTC (6:38 BST).

The Boeing 737 ⁠plane then again transmitted the general emergency signal ​before ⁠landing at Tabuk airport in northwestern Saudi Arabia, the website said.

The co-pilot is currently being questioned with “indications are mounting that he intended to take control of the plane and crash it with the passengers on board”, a senior official told N12 News correspondent Amit Segal.

Tabuk Airport said both the pilot and the co-pilot were hospitalised after the plane landed, adding that it was coordinating with Flydubai to secure a replacement aircraft for the around 180 Israelis reported to have been on the flight.

Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu was briefed over the incident, which his office said in a statement was "under control," adding that all efforts were being made to bring ‌the Israeli passengers back to Israel.

The office earlier said that the incident was not believed to have been a hijacking, although reports in Israeli media suggest security officials now believe otherwise.

open image in gallery A Flightradar24 graph shows the dramatic and sudden drop in altitude on the plane ( Flightradar24 )

An airline spokesperson said the flydubai ​flight ⁠experienced an "incident" en route to Tel ‌Aviv and diverted to Tabuk, where it landed safely. All passengers were safe and accounted for, the spokesperson said, without providing any further details.

An Israeli ‌official, speaking on the condition of anonymity, said ‌the pilots had transmitted the emergency signals after getting into a physical altercation with each other. It was not immediately clear if either pilot had intentionally transmitted the signal.

It is not the first time a flight ⁠between Israel and the UAE has landed in Saudi Arabia. A flydubai flight from Dubai to ‌Tel Aviv made an emergency ​landing in Riyadh in September 2025 ‌due to a medical emergency, Israeli media ​reported at the time.

Flydubai operates daily flights between Dubai and ‌Tel Aviv, a route that is popular ⁠among Israeli nationals. The Independent has contacted the airline for comment.

More follows on this developing story....

Tehran has celebrated the scheduled departure of American forces from their remaining bases in neighboring Iraq on Wednesday, as Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps issued an explicit appeal urging U.S. voters to vote out Congressional allies of President Donald Trump.

A 26-page letter published by the Guards on Tuesday calls on the American public to exercise their political power to remove incumbent leaders, reject U.S. backing for Israel, and oppose foreign military interventions.

While the message is unlikely to influence American voters who may never see the Iranian media release, analysts point out that it highlights domestic political vulnerabilities facing Trump and the Republican Party ahead of the November 3 congressional elections, in which Democrats could reclaim legislative control and obstruct Trump's agenda.

"Remove from power the evil, deceitful, and violent politicians who are responsible for America’s current state," the letter said. "Make sure your politicians understand that the world has changed."

open image in gallery An armed Shiite cleric rides aboard a military vehicle past a billboard depicting Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini, founder of the Islamic Republic, during the state-organized "Janfada," or "Sacrifice for Iran," military-style parade in Tehran earlier this month ( AP )

Trump campaigned in 2024 on promises to avoid new foreign conflicts, settle existing wars, and reduce inflation. However, the conflict with Iran, which Trump initiated alongside Israel, has spread across the Middle East and driven up global energy prices.

A Reuters/Ipsos poll released on September 21 showed that just 17% of respondents approved of Trump's handling of the cost of living—the primary issue voters say will guide their decision in November. Meanwhile, only 34% supported the military strikes against Iran.

Trump, who broke with mainstream Republican views in 2016 by calling the initial U.S. invasion of Iraq a major blunder, permitted the final withdrawal on Wednesday under terms agreed in 2024 by former President Joe Biden. The departure comes 23 years after US-led forces removed Saddam Hussein, sparking years of upheaval that ultimately led to the emergence of Islamic State.

open image in gallery Trump campaigned in 2024 pledging to ⁠avoid new wars, end existing conflicts and bring down inflation, but the war with Iran, which Trump launched alongside Israel, has contributed to higher global fuel prices and spread in the Middle East ( Reuters )

Iran, which asserts that its definitive objective is driving American forces out of the entire Middle East, has framed the departure from Iraq as a major victory for its regional "axis of resistance" of allied militant groups.

Neither Washington nor Tehran has managed to secure an exit from the war despite rounds of negotiations and repeated ceasefires. Intensive talks during last week's UN General Assembly in New York have yet to produce any accord to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz, through which 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas passed before fighting broke out in February.

Saga has said it is “significantly ahead” of its long-term growth plans as it revealed a jump in profits.

The over-50s travel and insurance group saw shares jump higher in early trading as a result.

The company’s long-running turnaround programme gained further pace as sales grew for the past six months.

It said its positive performance over the half-year to July “increased profit and cash flow expectations for the full year”, with underlying pre-tax profits now set to be “materially higher” than last year, at between £65 million and £70 million.

The London-based firm said it expects to strike an underlying profit of £100 million before its original 2030 target.

The group’s transformation plan has seen Saga focus further on its cruise business, while shifting from underwriting insurance policies.

Saga sold its underwriting business to Belgian firm Ageas and agreed a 20-year partnership deal for its remaining motor and home insurance arm.

On Wednesday, the group said revenues increased by 12% to £367.5 million for the six months to July 31, compared with a year earlier.

Meanwhile, underlying pre-tax profits almost doubled to £46.6 million from £23.5 million a year earlier.

It said “strong” customer demand and lower promotional activity helped drive a 38% jump in profits in its ocean cruise business.

Mike Hazell, Saga’s group chief executive, said: “In April 2025, we laid out our medium-term targets, with plans to achieve underlying profits of £100 million by January 2030.

“Eighteen months on, we are significantly ahead of that trajectory.

“While conscious of potential economic headwinds and volatile global conditions, our performance this year further demonstrates the resilience of our business model and target customer group, increasing our confidence in achieving our medium-term targets ahead of plan.”

Mark Crouch, market analyst at EToro, said: “Saga is making its old reputation for debt and complexity look increasingly out of date.

“Profits have almost doubled, cash generation is strengthening and borrowings are falling faster than expected, giving substance to a turnaround investors have already backed enthusiastically.”

Shares in the firm rose by 15.6% to 741p on Wednesday morning.

News.content:

If you hadn’t got round to reading the independent commission’s 40-page report just yet, here are the headlines. From 2009 to 2018, Manchester City cheated, repeatedly and systematically, cooking the books to the tune of £900m. Abu Dhabi pumped money into the club in the form of “sham” sponsorship agreements to artificially inflate revenues. Club officials disguised payments to hide spending. They submitted false accounts, concealed the truth and lied to investigators.

During the nine-year period, City’s revenues swelled from £87m to £500m, an increase of 475%. By comparison, Arsenal’s revenues grew 73% and Manchester United’s grew 112%. It enabled City to transform from the Premier League’s middle reaches to assembling a world-class squad of players paid more than Real Madrid. Sergio Aguero, scorer of perhaps the most famous goal in Premier League history, earned around £16m a year.

Evidently, City didn’t much like the rules. They weren’t perfect, but they were agreed by all the clubs not only to align with Uefa but to encourage sensible spending, establish fairer competition, prevent hyperinflation of wages and stop clubs doing exactly what City did when they stripped rivals like Arsenal and Aston Villa of their best players, distorting the game into an even more extreme battle of financial muscle. City signed up to the rules, then deliberately broke them.

To use just one example from the commission’s report, take image rights. City set up a company called Fordham Sports Image Rights Ltd, which was “little more than a front for Abu Dhabi United Group”, the private equity company of City owner Sheikh Mansour. Fordham bought image rights from City for £24.5m, a hugely inflated fee against the market, which the club booked as revenue. Incredibly, City also used the Fordham vehicle to buy licences to sell the rights in the first place, so that they could be sold to… Fordham.

The commission wrote: “The closed-circle arrangement … was thus a) A further device by which ADUG funds could be paid into the Club in a manner that concealed their true origin, and which enabled the Club to pretend that such funds represented operating income in its financial statements and FFP returns, and b) A device by which ADUG funds were to be used to meet what were in reality Club liabilities, enabling the Club to remove operating expenses from its financial statements and FFP returns.”

open image in gallery City CEO Ferran Soriano and chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak ( PA )

Perhaps just as breathtaking as City’s cheating has been their response. Chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak strongly reiterated their innocence in a letter to fans. CEO Ferran Soriano told staff, during a bizarre video in which he didn’t blink for three minutes, that City are the subject of a “conspiracy” and would fight on. “I know this can be a bit of a distraction,” he told them, while Rome burned around him.

Statements from the club remain strangely defiant, despite the tranche of evidence and guilty verdicts that have now been made public. The club seems paranoid and unhinged from reality, and if this was someone you knew you’d stage an intervention. Manipulation, lying, lack of remorse, lack of empathy, a grandiose sense of self-worth: these characteristics were famously listed by the Canadian forensic psychologist Dr Robert Hare as the traits of a psychopath.

City will now appeal. They still insist they retain “a body of irrefutable evidence”, even though their evidence has been entirely refuted by an independent panel. They will be dogged to the very end, and as if we needed proof, there was even the detail that City tried to stop this report being published and that the commission had to go through an appeal process to do so.

In the loaded language there are clear hints as to City’s intentions. Repeatedly calling the report an “opinion”, describing the findings as “unsafe”, even calling the tribunal a “Premier League commission” rather than an independent one: it is all designed to paint a picture of an unfair process that has conspired against them. This is the tactic, to undermine the sense of impartiality, to question legitimacy, to sow seeds of suspicion.

There are dark undertones here. Journalists investigating the case have been abused online and harassed at stadiums in recent years. Lawyers doing their jobs at the Premier League have been subjected to threats and feared for their families’ safety. People involved in the case have had their names redacted, presumably for those reasons. City could now stand down, yet on it goes.

After years of hard work, those journalists deserve their flowers now. There are many but to take just two examples on these pages, chief football writer Miguel Delaney has been indefatigable in calling out the ills of state ownership in football, and former chief sports writer Ian Herbert was investigating the details of City’s image-rights scandal eight years ago, despite enormous pressure from the club not to do so.

The greatest credit, of course, goes to the whistleblowers. Portuguese activist Rui Pinto leaked the documents to Der Spiegel in 2018 and without him, none of this would have come to light. Pinto was convicted and is living under witness protection after sacrificing his freedom for the truth.

open image in gallery Portuguese whistleblower and founder of Football Leaks, Rui Pinto ( AFP/Getty )

City will continue down this warpath regardless. Part of the club’s confidence lies in the fact their lead lawyer, Lord Pannick, is an appeals specialist. They are prepared for the case to go to the High Court and this story will run and run. City have history here, having successfully overturned a Uefa ban in the Court of Arbitration for Sport in 2020.

But that was won on a technicality, and that will surely not do here. It will not satisfy the football world if City pick faults in Premier League procedure. They have been found guilty of more than 100 charges by an independent panel reviewing thousands of documents of evidence over two years, and it is hard to envisage any way the achievements of a stained era can be allowed to stand.

It is a cliche that you will hear a lot over the coming days, but no one wins from this case. Not Manchester City, of course, whose entire identity will be wrapped up in this saga for years to come. Not their rivals, who might enjoy some schadenfreude but have ultimately lost titles, players and prize money over nearly two decades of the City project. Not even the Premier League, where – contrary to belief at the Etihad – there is really no appetite to fight their own clubs, to use up vast energy and resources enforcing regulations. The ramifications for the league will be long lasting and could go far beyond City’s points tally.

But if anything is to be salvaged from the wreckage, let it be this. Nation states shouldn’t own football clubs. Neither should oligarchs or other nefarious actors. The Premier League shouldn’t be left exposed to anyone who fancies taking advantage of its cultural power. Clubs are historical artefacts to be preserved and owners are their curators. These values are why the Independent Football Regulator was established; now it must use its statutory powers to protect them.

News.title: Dolly Parton welcomes fans to new museum in touching posthumous video message
News.content:
Dolly Parton spoke to fans from beyond the grave for the opening of a new museum all about her life.

The country music star, who died last month at the age of 80, pre-recorded a video message welcoming visitors to the attraction in Nashville, Tennessee.

In the video posted on Tuesday (29 September) she says: “Hi, everybody. It’s Dolly, and I am so proud to invite you to my Life of Many Colours Museum, opening right here in the heart of Nashville at my Song Teller Hotel.

“It includes all of the things that have helped this little girl’s dream come true, and I can’t wait to share it with you.”

News.title: How vaccines and antibiotics can beat some cancers
News.content:
At least one in eight cancers worldwide are caused by viruses and bacteria, according to a new study published in The Lancet.

An estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases in 2024 – out of a total of 20 million recorded worldwide – were caused by common infections, almost all of which could have been prevented with treatments such as antibiotics or vaccines.

Almost half of infection-linked cancers, around 760,000 cases, were caused by H. pylori, a bacterium that infects the stomach, researchers from the International Agency for Research on Cancer found.

The pathogen, which is typically ingested through contaminated food and water and is carried by around 60 per cent of the world’s population at any given time, can remain relatively undetected in the gut for between 20 and 40 years without causing any symptoms.

If left untreated, it can trigger chronic inflammation in the stomach and cellular mutations that, in some cases, lead to gastric cancer.

Cases of stomach cancer linked to H. pylori are particularly common in East Asia, where roughly 80 per cent of the population carries the bacterium. This is due in part to the prevalence of a more aggressive strain of the pathogen, known as CagA, which is endemic to the region.

East Asian diets – which typically include salty, pickled or smoked foods – can also damage the stomach’s protective lining and accelerate the inflammatory processes that can contribute to stomach cancer, researchers have found.

While H. pylori infection is treatable with a course of antibiotics, its symptoms often mimic those of other digestive problems and can be difficult to distinguish without testing.

This means the infection can remain undetected for years, allowing inflammation and damage to progress.

News.title: ‘Pooled’ TB testing could save money and improve diagnosis, study finds
News.content:
Mixing phlegm samples from multiple patients in “pooled tests” for tuberculosis could halve costs and help find millions of missing cases, according to a major new study.

While most advances in fighting TB come with a large price tag, the shift in strategy could dramatically boost access to diagnosis and save money, experts said.

TB is the deadliest single infection globally, killing around 1.3m people every year, despite being both preventable and curable.

The gold standard in diagnosis is rapid molecular testing, which detects genetic material from the bacteria causing TB in patient sputum samples within hours. But each sample needs a specialist diagnostic cartridge that costs around US$8, beyond the budget of many poorer countries even before recent aid cuts.

In a pooled test, samples from multiple individuals are tested in one cartridge. If the result is negative then all of them are reported to be negative, but if the result is positive each is re-tested individually.

Results published in The Lancet Global Health found the strategy, with up to four patients in each pool, used half as many cartridges as individual testing – 7,028 compared to 14,362. It detected 84.9 per cent of people with TB compared with 88 per cent for individual testing.

The study involved more than 14,000 people whose symptoms suggested TB in Bangladesh, Brazil, Cameroon, Kenya, Malawi, Nigeria and Vietnam.

News.title: UK borrowing costs hit highest level since 2007
News.content:
Britain’s borrowing costs hit their highest level since 2007 after Middle East tensions pushed oil prices above $108.

Yields on 10-year gilts, which determine the price the treasury pays to borrow money, rose above 5.43pc on Monday, before edging back to 5.42pc.

These are levels not seen in almost two decades, underlining the challenge facing John Healey as he prepares for next month’s Budget.

The Chancellor is coming under pressure to slash spending or raise taxes to bring Britain’s borrowing costs under control, against a backdrop of growing debt and rising inflation.

The surge in 10-year gilt yields pushes them above the 19-year high of 5.41pc recorded earlier this month, threatening to put a dent in Mr Healey’s fiscal headroom – a self-imposed guardrail to guide public spending.

Economists said high costs reflect the scale of Britain’s near-£3tn national debt and the rise in inflation facing the country.

“The uncomfortable truth for the PM and his Chancellor, John Healey ... is that the wide spread of gilt yields over peers is fair, in our view, given the UK’s dire fiscal position and the inflationary pressures stemming from high energy prices,” said Elliott Jordan-Doak, at Pantheon Macroeconomics.

“Gilt yields will fall if energy prices drop, but investors will continue to be driven by the economics and the Government’s willingness to take tough fiscal decisions, both of which point to yields staying high.”

UK borrowing costs are growing amid a wider bond market sell-off after Donald Trump rejected a peace deal with Iran over the weekend, pushing oil prices higher.

Brent crude, the international benchmark, rose by 3pc to just over $108 a barrel on Monday, adding to global inflation pressures. Bond traders reacted by demanding higher yields from governments to lend them money.

The yield on 10-year US Treasury bonds rose to above 5.24pc, the highest level since 2007.

News.title: Taylor Swift becomes most-awarded artist in MTV history
News.content:
Taylor Swift broke records at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards (VMAs) on Sunday, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMA history.

The pop star, 36, was previously tied with Beyoncé for the title, with 30 VMAs each. However, Swift took home three awards at the ceremony, bringing her career total to an unmatched 33.

The Fate of Ophelia, ⁠Swift’s first single from her record-breaking The Life of a Showgirl album, claimed the top trophy – Video of the Year – and she dedicated the honour to the late country music legend Dolly Parton.

During her speech, Swift praised Parton as “the ultimate showgirl” who told stories that were “so vivid and so rich”.

“I think that we were all very lucky to share this planet with Dolly Parton for a time,” she said.

Parton, an award-winning country singer, died in August at the age of 80.

Swift also received the inaugural Artist Director Honors, a new award meant to recognise artists “whose work behind the camera has expanded the possibilities of music video and advanced the art of visual storytelling”.

The 36-year-old has written and directed 18 videos of her roughly 60 videos during her career. The ‌most recent, for ‌her new single Patient Zero, debuted during ⁠the ceremony.

News.title: Five reasons why Australia’s win over Boks was an all-time classic
News.content:
If the Wallabies play like this in their own backyard at their own World Cup next year, boy we are in for a treat. After years in the doldrums, this five-try victory over South Africa was the latest reminder of their transformation under the stewardship of Les Kiss.

Their gritty performance in Perth – the city where Australia will open rugby’s showpiece in 12 months’ time – was caveated by the fact they were facing a second-string Boks side. But there can be no denying they are on an upward trajectory, even if their discipline dramatically deserted them late on.

In a helter-skelter denouement, Australia played the majority of the final 10 minutes of the match with 11 men on the pitch as South Africa threatened to mount a late comeback. Tom Wright’s eye-catching intercept try looked to have secured a match-winning moment, but it was scratched off after Hunter Paisami joined Harry Wilson, Ryan Lonergan and Joseph Sua’ali’i in the bin.

Ox Nche’s 80th-minute score made it a four-point game with time left for the restart, but Australia had enough fight to secure a dramatic victory largely built on execution and patience.

Five tries by the hour mark, including a Len Ikitau first-half double, ultimately gave South Africa a mountain to climb. The Wallabies’ field coverage and industriousness in defence was far superior to that of the four-time world champions, while Max Jorgensen and Sua’ali’i were pillars of excellence out wide.

After clinching a 3-1 win over New Zealand in their historic “Greatest Rivalry” series, Rassie Erasmus had the luxury of resting several of his A-listers for this one-off Test in Western Australia. The changes ultimately had an adverse effect, with the visitors faulty at the set-piece and lacking their usual snarl and bite. They found themselves playing catch-up in a chaotic game that Australia, despite their discipline creaking in the dying moments, deserved to win.

Here, Telegraph Sport explores five reasons why this was one of the craziest Test matches in recent memory.

Wallabies outmuscle Boks over 60 emphatic minutes

The Wallabies front up impressively to earn a seven-point lead at the break after a quickfire Len Ikitau double cancels out tries from Johan Grobbelaar and Edwill van der Merwe, before Ben Donaldson finishes a sublime attacking set from the hosts.

News.title: England show ODI depth in thrashing of Sri Lanka
News.content:
England’s international summer comes to an end at the Oval with a series decider against Sri Lanka. After England won the first game in Durham, Sri Lanka bounced back to take a 16-run win at Headingley on Thursday to set up this winner-takes-all match today. Sri Lanka put up a much better fight in the second one-day international than they have throughout the rest of their white-ball tour. The tourists posted 321 for six, with their captain Kusal Mendis leading the way with 121 off 100 balls, his seventh ODI century.

England’s reply got off to the best possible start, with both openers Tom Banton and Ben Duckett hitting fifties. It appeared to be going well for England, with Jos Buttler and Will Jacks also registering half centuries, but Buttler’s hamstring injury in addition to the regular loss of wickets meant Sri Lanka were able to claim victory to take us to a series decider in London today.

“I am so happy winning and getting the hundred,” Mendis said. “The overall performance was very good. We started really well and the middle order batted really well. Nothing special, basic cricket and I was very happy with 320, we wanted more than 300 on this pitch. [Dunith] Wellalage bowled really well, the whole team, after the powerplay. The guys gave 100 per cent. Today [Thursday] is finished and now we have to focus on the next game and do the basics right.”

When Buttler retired hurt in the 38th over of England’s run chase, the hosts were 254 for four and were in a great position to chase the total down and claim a series victory. From the 37th over onwards, England were only able to score one four and one six.

“It was an outstanding game,” England captain Harry Brook said. “You can look back and dwell on some many different areas but that is not what this team does, we go back to the drawing board and get ready for the Oval. We put up a really good fight with the ball. To restrict them to 320 and have the chance to chase that down was a hell of an effort.

“The lads got the chase off to a flyer. You could not really ask for much more. We probably stalled in that middle period and lost a few too many wickets, but the fight we showed was great. We have got a great opportunity now to try and win this series, and a great opportunity for 12 months’ time. In pressure situations, like the one that awaits us at the Oval, it will be great to see where we are as a team.”

Buttler has been ruled out of this match due to a hamstring injury and has been replaced in the squad by Dan Lawrence, who had been playing for Surrey in the final round of the County Championship.

Play from the Oval will get under way at 10.30am.

News.title: Saracens storm Leicester to launch new Venter era in style
News.content:
Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this mouthwatering Gallagher Prem meeting as Leicester Tigers host Saracens at Welford Road.

Last season, Leicester reached the play-off semi-finals in Geoff Parling’s first full season at the club, before losing to arch-rivals Northampton Saints, who went on to win their third title in the competition.

In a new era for Leicester as they plot a route back to the very top, Aaron Wainwright and Mako Vunipola make their Prem debuts.

Leicester head coach Geoff Parling is brimming with excitement ahead of this tasty match and has talked about his side’s preparation for the new season.

“Firstly we are looking to evolve our game, we’re not looking to rip it up and completely restart,” he said. This team is built on being competitive and winning, we’ve got to be in the mix every year. For me it’s all about being consistently near the top and then getting in those big games and having the ability to perform in them.”

“I’m well aware that there’s lots of elements from the season and different circumstances but the main thing is that the league is designed to have a top four that go into the play-offs so the top four is the aim.”

Saracens finished one place below Leicester in the previous campaign and missed out on the play-offs after a 32-12 final round loss to Exeter Chiefs.

Boss Joe Shaw has handed debuts to Tomos Williams and Alfie Barbeary, and he’s raring to go ahead of this fixture.

“We’ve had a great pre-season, but we’re itching to get stuck into the league campaign now,” he said. “We have a really competitive squad who are driving standards and good habits across the pitch. We are confident in the squad we have put together and are excited to see what they can achieve this campaign.”

Sports.title: Owner of top flight football club shot dead as team release heartbreaking statement and police launch investigation

BULGARIAN football club owner Iliyan Filipov has been shot dead aged 53.

Filipov was a majority shareholder of Bulgarian top flight side Botev Plovdiv and founded a major transport firm in the country called PIMK.

The businessman was killed in a late night shooting at a property in Plovdiv, according to Bulgarian outlet BGNES.



Police have since launched an investigation and have cordoned off the area.



A statement from the Bulgarian interior ministry read: “At approximately 1:00am, a report was received concerning a man who had been shot at an address in a Plovdiv neighborhood.

“His death was confirmed at the scene, and an investigation into the serious crime has been launched.

“Teams from the Plovdiv Regional Directorate of the Ministry of Interior and the General Directorate ‘National Police’ are working on the case.



“The area around the crime scene has been cordoned off, and traffic on several streets has been restricted due to the investigation.”

Plovdiv district prosecutor Vanya Hristeva added: “We ​are ⁠actively pursuing all possible leads.”

The main entry and exit points have also been blocked off in Plovdiv, which is located just 90 miles from the capital of Sofia.

Filipov’s club Botev released an emotional statement after the tragic news and said his name would be “written in golden letters for generations to come”.



Filipov was an key figure in rescuing the club from financial woes last summer and helping towards the reconstruction of their Hristo Botev Stadium.

The club said: “Botev Plovdiv FC expresses its profound grief over the tragic death of the club’s president, Iliyan Filipov.

“The management, players and staff of the club extend their deepest condolences to his family, relatives and friends.

“Iliyan Filipov will forever remain a part of Botev Plovdiv’s history.

“His contribution to saving the club in the summer of 2025 and his dedication to the team’s cause will be remembered by everyone in our family.



“His name will remain written in golden letters for generations to come following the successful completion of the reconstruction of Hristo Botev Stadium, which has made it the most modern sports facility in Bulgaria.”

MANCHESTER CITY CEO Ferran Soriano has blasted the “Premier League conspiracy theory” after an independent commission found the club guilty on all charges of financial breaches of league rules.

On Tuesday the league confirmed City were guilty of all charges relating to serious breaches of the Prem’s financial rules and the majority of charges in terms of failure to co-operate with the investigation.



The commission’s verdict found City to have arranged “sham contracts” and make “sham agreements with others”, and misstating their accounts and true nature of their finances to the tune of over £900million between 2009 and 2018 as part of a disguised funding scheme.

However, City hit back in a statement of their own, claiming they have “irrefutable evidence” supporting their case.



And in a leaked video to staff, club CEO Soriano defended the club, saying the Prem case was based on “a single false accusation”.

In a three-and-a-half minute video, he said: “A document has been made public with an opinion of the Premier League commission which is negative to our interests. I want to explain exactly what this is.



“This has gone on for so long, but it’s important to remind ourselves the whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation.

“That the owners personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club from some sponsors in Abu Dhabi. This is not true.

“Irrefutable evidence has been provided to show it could not happen and it did not happen.

“This includes bank transfers, money transfers, witnesses and everything necessary to categorically demonstrate the money did not come from the owner.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

“Every other false charge that has been thrown at us, and aggressively marketed and promoted, comes from that simple, central and completely false accusation.

“To do so the opinion had to ignore the extensive evidence provided by the club in order to reach a conclusion that is clearly wrong.”

Soriano, 59, confirmed City would appeal the decision by setting out how the opinion contains “clear material errors of law, principle and fact and is unsafe”.

He added the club had “been here before” in 2020 when they appealed the decision to the Court of Arbitration for Sport and won.

“So how do I feel? I feel saddened, I feel angry, I feel a bit confused. I saw the interview (CEO) Ferran [Soriano] had and they say they have evidence to say they are innocent.”

Shearer, who is the league’s record goalscorer, took a wider view of the scandal, calling it a “mess” and adding: “Where does it stop? Where does the club stop? Where do individuals stop? Where do the accolades [stop]?

Former Match of the Day host Lineker argued it might be better for City to hold their hands up and take any punishment they might get now, drawing comparisons with his beloved Leicester.



The 65-year-old said: “Leicester are my team who got points deductions which proved costly and got things wrong and we accepted it, I just wonder if Man City – I saw Ferran’s statement saying they have ‘irrefutable evidence’ – but if it was irrefutable that would have shown before.

“I wonder if they would be better off saying we got it wrong, we apologise, we take the punishment, we take the sanctions and just move on…

“The ones who really suffer are the fans.”

Richards shared a joke with Shearer regarding the potential stripping away of honours, with Shearer saying: “We might be saying you haven’t won a league anymore.”

Former City defender Richards said: “No one’s taking my Premier League away.”



Lineker added: “I think taking away the titles is such a can of worms and is so cruel on the fans and the players.”

City CEO Soriano warned the legal case could drag on for years.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

The club have the right to appeal the initial decision until October 2.

All sanctions remain on the table, which could include points deductions, transfer bans, stripping of honours and potential expulsion.

Sports.title: Man City face ‘ultimate sanction’ that could see them expelled from Premier League, Government warns
Sports.content:
Next

MANCHESTER CITY face being thrown out of the Premier League after they were found guilty on all charges of financial breaches by an independent commission, according to Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy.

League chiefs confirmed last week’s reports on City breaching nearly all of their charges after they were found to have arranged “sham” commercial deals as part of a disguised funding scheme between 2009 and 2018.



The sums of money involved in the case amounts to around £900million.

City deny any wrongdoing and will appeal the decision, stating they believe they have “irrefutable evidence” in their corner.



However, Nandy has suggested that City, who won three league titles in the period covered in the unprecedented case, could face the “ultimate sanction” if their appeal is thrown out.

She told Channel 5: “I don’t want to pre-empt any kind of appeal process, and they are entitled to a fair hearing. But what I would say is that the ultimate sanction is very serious indeed.

“I mean, a club can be expelled from the Premier League if these sorts of allegations are upheld, with obviously huge repercussions for everybody.

“So there are very serious sanctions, and I think the bigger issue is how do we make sure that we have clearly understood rules that are upheld and applied consistently, and that we can move quickly when they’re breached.

“The Premier League is one of our greatest exports. It brings joy to millions of people, and we want to make sure that we protect it for the fans for the future.”

Former Manchester United star Roy Keane went as far as calling on City players who had won medals to throw them “in the bin”.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

He told ITV: “They knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they’ve still done it, and if I was a player I’d be 100 per cent sticking those medals in the bin.

“It’s cheating. You’re hearing nonsense about some ex-players saying ‘oh well they won on the pitch’. Because it was cheating! It was cheating going on.”

Former City chairman David Bernstein, who worked in the role for five years until 2003, said the “sanctions cannot just be financial” and called on the board “be suspended immediately”.

Football finance expert Kieran Maguire told BBC Radio 5 Live it had “gone far beyond the worst-case scenario that anybody initially envisaged” and called the almost £1BILLION in inflated deals a “staggering misstatement”.

He also spoke about how City, who said the decision “contains clear materials errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe,” could appeal the decision.



Maguire added: “I’ve spoken to some sports lawyers today, just in case this did arise, and the consensus that I had coming back was that it’s difficult but not impossible for Manchester City to say that ultimately this is some form of commercial dispute between two entities and therefore it should be taken away from the football authorities and dealt with (by) the standard legal courts in the country.”

Sports.title: Ireland make decision on boycotting second Israel Nations League match after protests
Sports.content:
Ireland make decision on boycotting second Israel Nations League match after protests

Heimir Hallgrimsson has spoken to the media regarding the Republic of Irelands upcoming Nations League reverse with Israel, following fan protests regarding the game

View Image Heimir Hallgrimsson has spoken about Ireland's match with Israel (Image: RTE Sport)

Heimir Hallgrimsson has explained that the Republic of Ireland will "fulfil" the FAI's (Football association of Ireland's) request that they play a second game against Israel in the Nations League on Sunday evening. That's despite national outrage regarding the fixture as a result of the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.

‌



Ireland ran out 3-0 winners over Israel in their second game of the competition at the weekend, thanks to goals from Troy Parrot, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan. However, it was far from a straightforward encounter.

‌



Not only did Gavin Bazunu pull out of the squad as a result of personal beliefs - defender Jimmy Dunne taking his place on the bench as a makeshift goalkeeper - but a number of demonstrations also took place before and during the game. Captains Dara O'Shea and Manor Solomon did not exchange pennants or niceties ahead of time, also snubbing the chance to shake hands after the referee's coin toss.

‌



Israel star Manor Solomon shares UEFA ban fears after pointing finger at Ireland players READ MORE :

Ireland players snub Israel handshakes and take action during national anthem before match READ MORE :

Meanwhile, Ireland players on the pitch and staff in the bench also bowed their heads as the Israeli national anthem rang out around the Nagyerdei Stadium in Hungary, while wearing black armbands in recognition of all of the lives lost in the Gaza conflict.

Moyland also kissed said armband in a pointed display after scoring his goal in the match. Fans in Ireland and further afield, meanwhile, refused to watch the showing and have promised to do the same again for this weekend's encounter, should it go ahead.

Reports suggest that thousands of fans have backed a boycott, while hundreds of pubs across Ireland who didn't show the initial match have pledged to do so once more. Now, head coach, Hallgrimsson, has spoken about where his teams heads are at headed into this weekend's reverse.

‌



Speaking during a press conference this week, he said: "Obviously, the FAI have said that we are playing both the games and we are going to fulfil that. That was our intention when we came into this camp, and it's still our intention.

"It's been tough, especially on the players, it's been really, really tough and everybody understands that. But we are trying to focus on the football game against Austria (on Thursday).

"What happens after, like all this camp, we need to almost take it day by day. But that is already decided, we are going to fulfil the games."

Sports.title: Micah Richards heartbroken and Jamie Carragher lashes out - Pundits weigh in on Man City charges
Sports.content:
Micah Richards heartbroken and Jamie Carragher lashes out - Pundits weigh in on Man City charges

Manchester City await their sanction as they plan to appeal the guilty verdict they have been handed over their Premier League charges

View 6 Images Micah Richards

Manchester City have been found guilty of breaking Premier League financial rules, and pundits have had their say. From anger to upset, the decision has sparked emotional reactions among former players.

‌



On Tuesday, the Premier League confirmed that the Independent Commission had found that City were guilty of all charges related to serious violations over a nine-season stretch and overstated their commercial income by more than £800million. They were found guilty of all but one breach in relation to their cooperation with the Premier League's investigation.

‌



Manchester City plan to appeal the decision and maintain their innocence. Sanctions for the club will be decided in a separate hearing and could take the form of a fine, points deduction or other sporting sanctions.

‌



Following the news, there have been calls for City to receive severe punishments. Some have called for the club to be relegated, while others have suggested the team's ownership can continue at the club.

City, meanwhile, suggest that 'irrefutable evidence' has been ignored and will look at all avenues to vindicate themselves. In a message to staff, CEO Ferran Soriano described the suggestion that commercial income came directly from their owner as a conspiracy theory.

‌



Mirror Football takes a look at some of the fallout from pundits since the findings were released.

Jamie Carragher

View 6 Images Jamie Carragher

"The club are going to get punished. For me, this is all about the owners. I don't know how the owners can continue in English football.

‌



"We talk about the fit and proper test for owners, what they have done over ten years now in the Premier League and this stain that will be there for the next ten years about 'did they win it really, was that fair?'

"This all starts with Manchester City and it starts because they do not like the word 'no'. When the rules came in, it's in the emails: 'We can do what we want'.

"And when you see the statements in the last couple of days, the one from Sorriano last night, it actually beggars belief what you are watching and hearing here. Until they move away from the club, I don't know how this stain is ever removed from the club."

‌



"I just don't see how the ownership can continue after what has happened here and the way they are actually reacting to it.

"How can they be surprised, and that they have got irrefutable evidence? Where is it? Put it out there, surely.

"If you have irrefutable evidence of something and you are getting charged by the police, you hand it to them because you want this over with as quickly as possible. City have almost dragged this on, kicking the can down the road."

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Micah Richards

View 6 Images Micah Richards' Premier League title has been cast into doubt (Image: GETTY )

"First of all, the reports were troubling. I saw the words that were used by the Premier League...'sham contracts'.

‌



"I felt absolutely devastated, as someone who loves Manchester City and I know we have a laugh and a joke about 'I supported Arsenal when I was young' but Man City is my club.

"I had been at that club since I was 14 years old, I would die for that club, all the rollercoaster from being in the academy, down at Platt Lane going all the way through, making it to the first team, I achieved my dream at Man City but then to hear these reports and not only me as an ex-player but the fans what they have to go through, absolutely devastated.

"My digs man, he rang me today, and he was literally in tears and asking me for information. I haven't got the answers to tell him, and that is someone who has supported the club for 60-odd years, and the uncertainty around it is just heartbreaking.

‌



"The word I use is heartbreaking, to have a headline of this nature for a club that I love so much, it's been difficult.

"If you listen to the reports that have been said, they are damning. How do I feel? I feel saddened, I feel angry, I feel a little bit confused because on the other side you have City's side of the story."

‌



Alan Shearer

View 6 Images Alan Shearer

"What a mess, what a complete and utter mess. I go back to what we said at the weekend, the ramifications go so far it is unbelievable because where does it stop?

"Where do the clubs stop? Where do individuals stop? Where do the accolades...there is so much at stake here for football, for the Premier League and Manchester City.

‌



"So yes, it's a complete and utter mess isn't it? I look at their success, clearly they have to wait for sanctions to come out, then do they appeal?

"If it is all comes out in terms of you're done, you're banged to rights, how do they get over...how do they look back?

"I know the fans have had their memories, but that Aguero moment...that is one of, if not, the greatest moment in Premier League history in terms of how it unfolded and what happened on the day.

‌



"That is blown apart now if that is what is going to happen, that is done. That memory, I am not a City fan and I don't really care but that for me was one of the iconic moments in Premier League history.

"When and if City are done, banged to rights, it's finished."

Man City rivals' private thoughts on vote to expel club from Premier League READ MORE :

Ian Wright

View 6 Images Ian Wright called for Manchester City to be given an 'unprecedented' punishment

‌



"It's cheating on an industrial scale. It's quite surreal seeing it written down like that. The amount of stick I've taken off that.

"Unprecedented punishment is required here. It's a massive day for the Premier League. They've taken on a whole country, massive.

"Very messy. It's a problem for them to be going to Liverpool (in their next fixture). In their real time, Liverpool were the team chasing them down. Look at what Jurgen Klopp went through to break them - it probably broke him. It's so sad. It's probably going to get very litigious."

‌



Roy Keane

View 6 Images Roy Keane (Image: ITV)

"Well, do you know what? They knew it would hurt a lot of people, and they still done it. And if I was a player with that bit of success and praise that we've given a lot of credit for - but if I was a player I'd be 100% sticking them medals in the bin."

When questioned if he'd feel betrayed by the club as a player, he responded: "Oh 100% of course, of course you would. It's cheating. You're hearing nonsense from ex-players saying 'oh well they won on the pitch'. Because there was cheating. There was cheating going on."

Article continues below

"I think it's going to be very difficult for the players, for the manager. The trust, the belief in whatever's gone on at the football club, what they stand for when you've got owners who are quite happy cheating.

"It's very difficult for these players going forward to try and maintain the level of excellence that they've been [displaying]."

Sports.content:
Man City players 'fear Premier League relegation' as agent leaks dressing room reaction

Manchester City have been found guilty of breaching the Premier League's financial rules, with relegation from the English top flight landing as a potential punishment

View 2 Images Manchester City players are said to be concerned (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City players are worried about points deductions and relegation from the Premier League as a result of the club's recent guilty verdict over breaching financial rules, as per reports. The Premier League confirmed on Wednesday that an independent panel had found the club guilty of the majorty of the charges they were slapped with in 2023, relating to a nine-year period between 2009 and 2018.

‌



A statement from the league read: "An independent Commission has found Manchester City FC guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League’s investigation."

‌



While City are expected to appeal the verdict, they must exercise their option to do so by Friday. If that appeal fails, however, City could be in for severe sanctions from top flight officials.

‌



While all potential punishments are purely speculative at present, City could be handed fines or transfer bans should the Premier League see fit. However, should officials choose to throw the book at the club, then they could also risk being stripped of titles won between 2009 and 2018, huge points deductions, or even relegation from the league.

It's the latter two scenarios which are proving particularly worrying for players in Enzo Maresca's dressing room, according to an agent who recently spoke with L'Equipe. The publication claims there is a feeling within the camp that a significant point deduction would inevitably lead to relegation to the Championship, in the event that the club don't automatically demote them.

It comes as football fans will have to wait a little while longer to learn City's fate, given the Premier League will not hand down any penalties until the case is concluded. An appeals process will extend the investigation further, although the league have vowed to work through matters as quickly as the possibly can.

‌



It comes as City released a statement of their own in the wake of the Premier League's announcement on Tuesday. It read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, that has been published today.

Sports.title: Man City ‘sham’ is worst disgrace in British sports history and forever taints the Premier League
Sports.content:
It was the greatest moment in the Premier League era.

Sergio Aguero’s dramatic winner against QPR to clinch Manchester City's first Premier League title in 2012 signalled the start of the club’s period of dominance.

It was fairytale stuff with “93.20 and Agueroooo!” lodged in our memories thanks to Martin Tyler’s unforgettable piece of commentary.

The highlights from that unforgettable day are still up on the Premier League website today under a headline of “Iconic.”

‌



And now, sadly, that word should no longer be used to describe it. It has gone. Forever tainted. The title will have an asterisk by it. No football fan will ever view it in the same way.

And now we are all questioning whether we can actually believe anything that we have seen. Not just from that sunny day on May 13, 2012, but every trophy, every parade and every goal since.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



It does not just destroy City’s legacy. It also takes a huge chunk out of the Premier League history books - and that is why every football fan should feel so angry. The best league in the world forever tainted. Nearly two decades called into question.

City will now be known as the “sham” club. That is guaranteed. The word sham was used EIGHT times in the 40 page redacted legal document which found guilty of breaching the Premier League’s spending rules between 2009/10 and 2017/18.

But it goes further than that. Because can we believe anything since? The four-in-a-row titles, the 2023 Champions League success and the 2019 Treble.

They absolutely dominated English football. And yet they cheated their way to success.

‌



View 4 Images Man City scandal taints everything that has followed at the Etihad (Image: Getty Images)

If they had not “systematically” broke the Premier League rules in the first place through fraudulent sponsorship deals then the club would not have been able to dominate English football for so long.

Let’s be clear: this is the biggest scandal in the history of British sport. The biggest disgrace in English football. It is shocking.

And it calls into question way beyond 2018 because would they have been able to recruit the best manager and the best players without previous success? Of course not.

‌



City’s hierarchy have to be stripped of the club, not allowed to run a club and the devastating series of documents also suggest State ownership and fraud which must run into criminal offences.

It is impossible to imagine the Abu Dhabi could carry on from this point and the legacy and history is already destroyed.

Pep Guardiola, in my opinion, is the greatest coach in the Premier League era - but now even his achievements are tainted by this scandal.

View 4 Images Even Pep Guardiola's stunning list of honours now comes with an asterisk attached (Image: Michael Regan/Getty Images)

‌



City have won eight Premier League titles - but should any of them count? What about those incredible memories and players?

The final day success in 2022 when they came from behind in dramatic fashion to beat Aston Villa 3-2. The records. The 100 points-plus season when they left everyone else trailing in their wake.

I was there for so many of those achievements and I always marvelled at their football and Guardiola’s successes. How naive was I?

What does it all mean now? They have cheated us all. What did the players know? What did Guardiola know?

‌



Furthermore, what about the clubs who finished second in all of those years. Liverpool were runners-up three times. Arsenal twice. How do they feel?

This scandal has torn the game apart. The sheer scale of the deception is mind-blowing. The language used puts it in perspective. Sham. Deceit.

The index of the evidence ran to more than 750 pages and the core bundle of documents ran to tens of thousands of pages.

View 4 Images Man City have continued to dominate English football thanks to the foundations laid in those years (Image: Getty Images)

‌



But this is key about the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development’s sponsorship and a “disguised funding scheme” in the Premier League statement.

“As part of the scheme, further ‘sham’ arrangements, funded by ADUG, were entered into to enable the club to record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred, as well as a ‘sham’ circular arrangement with Fordham, an entity that purchased the club’s players’ image rights, that was funded by ADUG.”

The breach of the rules “enabled” the club to put itself on a different level. That is why it is not just the Aguero moment which has been ruined. But every achievement since.

Without the foundation of “success” from 2009 to 2018, they would not have won so many trophies afterwards. It is unquestionable.

‌



It is shocking. Guardiola should be angry. Every City fan should be angry. The ownership has betrayed us all.

Every memory, every achievement and every trophy is ruined. It is almost stripping City of titles. Because they have done that to themselves already.

Sports.title: Ian Wright demands 'unprecedented' Man City punishment after Premier League statement
Sports.content:
Ian Wright demands 'unprecedented' Man City punishment after Premier League statement

Former Arsenal star Ian Wright has given his verdict on the charges that have been brought against Manchester City after the Premier League's statement

View Image Ian Wright has reacted to the latest updat on Manchester City (Image: ITV)

Ian Wright has called for Manchester City to receive an "unprecedented punishment" after the Premier League revealed the full extent of the club's financial breaches. News emerged last week that City had been found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges brought against the club, with the allegations dating back to between 2009 and 2018.

‌



The Premier League issued a statement outlining four areas explaining why City had been found guilty by an independent commission, including 'sham contracts' with some of the club's commercial partners.

‌



City, who maintain their innocence, responded to the statement from the Premier League by releasing their own official statement, expressing their "disappointment" and "surprise" at the announcement.

‌



Wright, who called for City to be punished after the news first emerged last week, has done so again following the announcement made by the Premier League.

Man City chief's secret message to staff after bombshell Premier League verdict emerges READ MORE :

Man City 115 charges delay explained as commission lay out Premier League timeline READ MORE :

"It's cheating on an industrial scale. It's quite surreal seeing it written down like that," Wright told ITV Sport.

"The amount of stick I've taken off that. Unprecedented punishment is required here. It's a massive day for the Premier League. They've taken on a whole country, massive.

‌



"Very messy. It's a problem for them to be going to Liverpool (in their next fixture). In their real time, Liverpool were the team chasing them down. Look at what Jurgen Klopp went through to break them - it probably broke him.

"It's so sad. It's probably going to get very litigious."

Manchester United legend Roy Keane was alongside Wright and stated why he thinks City deserve to be punished based on the independent commission’s findings.

‌

"It's bittersweet. You deserve to be punished, but it's not good for the league. What about the players who have been part of the problem, new players, what happens now going forward?"

City issued a statement on Tuesday evening which read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, that has been published today.

The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

Sports.title: Man City chief's secret message to staff after bombshell Premier League verdict emerges
Sports.content:
Man City chief's secret message to staff after bombshell Premier League verdict emerges

Manchester City have been found guilty of the Premier League charges and the eight-time champions have now hit out at the allegations ahead of a possible appeal over the coming days

View 2 Images Khaldoon Al Mubarak and Ferran Soriano (Image: Getty Images)

Manchester City's chief executive, Ferran Soriano, has sent a video message to staff members claiming that the club will continue fighting their guilty verdict.

‌



The Premier League confirmed on Tuesday that the club had been found guilty of all charges, with the process now moving towards an appeal. That is an avenue that City will take advantage of. Before that, CEO of the City Football Group Foriano has got in touch with club employees.

‌



He sent a three minute video message, obtained by the Manchester Evening News, to staff members and said that they will continue attempting to clear their name and suggested that the Premier League's verdict is based on a 'single false accusation'.

‌



"I want to share some information related to the ongoing disciplinary process between Manchester City and the Premier League. A document has been made public with an opinion of the Premier League commission that is negative to our interests. I want to explain exactly what this is, the next steps and how we are going to continue to defend the club, and finally be vindicated in this process.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"This has gone for so long that it is important to remind ourselves that the whole Premier League case against us is based on a single false accusation - that the owners' personal money was somehow and secretly put into the club via some sponsors from Abu Dhabi. This is just not true.

"Irrefutable evidence has been provided to the Premier League commission that shows that it could not happen and that it did not happen. This includes bank statements, money transfers, witnesses and everything necessary to categorically demonstrate that the money did not come from the owner. Every other false charge that has been thrown at us - and aggressively marketed and promoted - comes from the simple, central, and completely false accusation.

"Surprisingly for us, and for our lawyers, after nearly two years the Premier League Commission has introduced an opinion that supports the Premier League's conspiracy theory. To do so, the opinion had to ignore the extensive evidence provided by the club in order to reach a conclusion that is clearly wrong.

‌



View 2 Images Ferran Soriano has sent a message to Man City employees (Image: Getty Images)

"Our lawyers will now file an appeal that sets out the opinion contains clear material errors of law, principle and fact and it is unsafe. Remember we have been here before. In 2020 we were also wrongly ruled against for many of the same issues. We appealed to an independent body in CAS and we won.

"We will now be relentless in our work. We will focus on the independent appeal process and also all other legal avenues available to us in order to win the case, and we will take all necessary action to protect the club and seek compensation from any party that tries to damage it now, and in the future.

‌



"I know this can be a bit of a distraction but please remain focused on our business and take care of our extended City family as we always do. Please follow the normal protocols in referring to fan, partner and media enquiries. Very soon we will look back at this and recognise it is another time in our history when we dealt with adversity and overcame it together."

Soriano's message comes in the aftermath of a strong statement from City in response to the Premier League's verdict. It read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, that has been published today.

Man City 115 charges delay explained as commission lay out Premier League timeline READ MORE :

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.

‌



"The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City FC will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe.

"The Club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence. The Club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete."

Elsewhere, Premier League CEO Richard Masters has claimed that the Premier League are attempting to wrap up the proceedings as soon as possible. In a statement, he said:“The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

‌



“It also vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

“It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

“This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches. Now we have the Commission’s decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans.”

Sports.title: Man City 115 charges delay explained as commission lay out Premier League timeline
Sports.content:
Man City 115 charges delay explained as commission lay out Premier League timeline

Manchester City have been found guilty by the independent commission who have now explained the reason behind the delay

View 3 Images Manchester City have been found guilty by the independent commission following their legal battle with the Premier League. (Image: PA Wire)

The independent Commission has explained the reason behind the 20-month delay following the end of the 42-day hearing into the Premier League and Manchester City's 115 charges. The investigation into Man City began in December 2018, and a complaint was subsequently issued under Section W of the League’s rules in February 2023.

‌



The Premier League announced in a statement today (Wednesday) that City were found guilty of 'all charges related to serious breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules over a nine-season period, and the majority of charges in relation to its failure to co-operate with the League’s investigation.' The club still maintain their innocence.

‌



In a statement, the independent Commission explained the reason behind the lengthy delay and wrote: "It has taken us much longer than we would have wished, and much longer than we had anticipated would be the case when the hearing concluded, to produce our Decision. That is regrettable.

‌

"However, we were fortunate to have available to us throughout the period in which our Decision has been being prepared not only all of the documents that were used at the hearing but also (a) verbatim transcripts of the evidence given by each witness and expert at the hearing.

"Those transcripts ran to approximately 7,000 pages, and (b) extremely detailed written submissions from the parties (that they had supplemented orally over four days at the end of the hearing) on the evidence and each of the numerous issues that we were tasked with determining in the proceedings."

‌



Premier League chief executive Richard Masters also broke his silence on the investigation and said: "The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade.

View 3 Images Richard Masters, CEO of the Premier League, has released a statement on Manchester City's rule breaches. (Image: PA Wire)

"It also vindicates the Premier League’s decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently.

‌



"It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously.

"This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches.

"Now we have the Commission’s decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans."

City however, maintain their innocence and have until the end of this week, Friday, October 3 to lodge and appeal. They released a statement which read: "Manchester City FC is both disappointed and surprised by the opinion of the Premier League Commission, which has been published today.

"The Club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The Club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums.
