England moved clear with a late goal from Kane and are second in Group A3 after Spain’s 4-1 win over Croatia. Next up is a trip to ­Croatia on Saturday. Tuchel hopes that the ­Manchester City left-back Nico O’Reilly will return from injury.

Sports.title: Have any footballers ever scored with the first touch of their careers? | The Knowledge
Sports.content:
“Jamie Spencer, 17, made his first first-team appearance in a competitive match, for Huddersfield at Doncaster on 9 September in the prestigious EFL Trophy,” emails Richard Askham. “He came on as a substitute in the 66th minute and scored with his second touch of the ball, one to control it and the second to score. Has anyone scored with their very first touch, which is the only way to better young Spencer’s achievement?”

We covered a variation of this question back in 2021, with answers on players scoring with their first touch on debut for their new clubs. This week, though, goes a step further, covering players that score with the first touches of their professional careers, although there are a few answers from that 2021 piece that work here, too: Jack Aitchison for Celtic in 2016, Matt Hatch for Central Coast Mariners in 2021, England one-cap wonder Michael Ricketts for Walsall against Brighton in 1996, Maheta Molango (now the chief executive of the Professional Footballers’ Association) for Brighton against Reading in August 2004, and Yan Dhanda for Swansea City at Sheffield United in 2018.

“Back in 2007, Luke Medley, on his professional debut for Bradford, was aged 18 years and two months,” emails Ben McGowan. “In an early-season game against a Wrexham side who finished the season bottom of the fourth tier, he came on in the 76th minute. Two minutes later, he scored an absolutely stunning half-volley with his first touch in professional football.” What a strike!

“Back in September 1981, Raphael Meade came on as sub for Arsenal against Panathinaikos and scored with his very first touch,” flags Mukhtar Khan. Quite the feat, especially as it was in the Uefa Cup, and especially as it was a bicycle kick! “Kenny Samson provided the cross from the left and Meade, with his back to goal, beat keeper Konstantinou all ends up”, wrote the Daily Express.

View image in fullscreen Raphael Meade celebrates scoring for Arsenal v Manchester City in October 1981, a month after his first-touch goal on debut against Panathinaikos. Photograph: Colorsport/Shutterstock

“Ibra Sekajja scored with his first touch on his professional debut for Crystal Palace against Hull in 2011,” writes Bjørn Barang. Sekajja netted an 88th-minute equaliser to help Palace retain their Championship status.

Andy Brook and Robert Heath both correctly identify Alan Smith’s first touch as a professional footballer resulting in a goal for Leeds at Anfield. With Leeds 1-0 down, Smith came off the bench and equalised with his first touch in front of the Kop two minutes later, before Leeds went on to win a controversial match 3-1 (the state of that tackle from Nigel Martyn on Karl-Heinz Riedle!) – Gérard Houllier’s first game in sole charge of Liverpool.

Stadiums with low Google ratings (part II)

Last week’s lead question regarding football stadiums with high or low Google ratings proved very popular but the answers were just based upon English clubs (and four Welsh ones). Luckily, Mykola Kozlenko has since been in touch with a few more continental options:

“Great question about stadia with low rankings!” writes Mykola. “I tried to expand it to Europe and found a few interesting candidates.

1) Nyva Stadium, Vinnytsia, Ukraine, 2.7*, 12 reviews.

Home stadium of third-tier FC Nyva Vinnytsia (who recently received Dynamo Kyiv here in the national cup). This was rebuilt two years ago but it is proving to be unpopular because:

amateur athletes are unhappy because they can’t train here any more

locals are unhappy because the stands are literally 20 metres away from the nearest residential complex (ironically named Family Comfort).

fans are unhappy because it’s a small soulless stadium with an artificial pitch instead of the old 24,000-seat Central City Stadium.

2) Avanhard Stadium, Rivne, Ukraine, 3.4*, 142 reviews

Home stadium of top-tier NK Veres Rivne. The stadium was dilapidated for years, renovation has started but not completed yet, although two out of four stands are ready.

3) Dens Park, Dundee, Scotland, 3.7*, 804 reviews

This (probably) makes the home stadium of Dundee the lowest-rated top-tier stadium in the UK.

View image in fullscreen Dens Park, viewed from the grandstand, a peculiar V-shaped main stand in Dundee that angles away from the pitch. Photograph: David Young/Action Plus/Shutterstock

4) Almondvale, Livingston, Scotland, 3.7*, 432 reviews

The home stadium of Livingston does not seem to have a great reputation despite being relatively new.

5) Kampi Nacional Hajvali, Pristina, Kosovo, 3.7*, 7 reviews

This stadium somehow hosted Conference League qualifiers this year despite being half built.

6) The Oval, Belfast, Northern Ireland, 3.8*, 490 reviews

The home stadium of Glentoran is particularly dilapidated, especially its away end.

7) Stade Jos Nosbaum, Dudelange, Luxembourg, 3.8*, 135 reviews

This stadium has hosted Conference League and Europa League qualifiers and is the home of top-tier F91 Dudelange. Parking and payments are picked out as particular gripes of this pretty old stadium.”

Three in a crowd

“Brian Brobbey scored a hat-trick against Manchester City and ended up on the losing side. How often has that happened in the Premier League, and who has scored the most goals in a game their team lost?” asks Alejandro Solis.

We’ve covered the second part of your question in the past – click here for tales of futile netbusting – so let’s proceed straight to the players who have scored Premier League hat-tricks in vain. Brobbey’s was the sixth example and the first in almost 20 years. The last man to achieve this dubious feat was Blackburn’s Roque Santa Cruz in December 2007. He single-handedly dragged Blackburn back into the game from 3-0 down, only for Wigan’s Marcus Bent to score two more goals and complete his own hat-trick.

The first two were scored by Matt Le Tissier, on the final day of the inaugural season and the opening day of the 1995-96 season. The cruellest is probably Dion Dublin’s: he’s the only man to put his team in front on three different occasions and still lose. Here’s the full list.

Matt Le Tissier Oldham 4-3 Southampton, 1992-93

Matt Le Tissier Southampton 3-4 Nottingham Forest, 1995-96

Dion Dublin Sheffield Wednesday 4-3 Coventry City, 1995-96

Dwight Yorke Newcastle 4-3 Aston Villa, 1996-97

Roque Santa Cruz Wigan 5-3 Blackburn, 2007-08

Brian Brobbey Manchester City 5-3 Sunderland, 2026-27

Knowledge archive

“When was the last time Spain did not have more possession than the opposition in a full match?” enquired Sol O’Carroll back in 2012.

Sixty-one games ago, to be precise Sol. Incredibly, La Roja last lost out to an opponent in the possession stakes in the Euro 2008 final, when Germany edged them 52% to 48%, although they still won 1-0.

2026 update: Remarkably, there is only one competitive match since the Euro 2008 final in which Spain have not had the lion’s share of possession. That was the 3-0 victory over Croatia at Euro 2024. “For the first time in 137 games, Spain did not complete as many passes as their opponents, and they could not be happier,” began Sid Lowe’s intro at the Olympiastadion, Berlin. Spain, of course, would go on to be Euro 2024 champions, beating England 2-1 in the final (with 63% possession).

Can you help?

“Oli McBurnie is back in the Scotland squad,” notes John Cant. “With his record of 16 appearances and zero goals, he said in a recent interview, “a tap-in on Saturday or one that goes in off my backside would be lovely.” The backside comes up often when players talk of breaking a goal drought – but has it ever actually happened?”

“Manchester City claimed Scott Carson as a club legend in a recent LinkedIn post,” retches Michael Haddon. “He played one league game for them. So, who is the genuine club legend who played the fewest games for a side? It’s not Carson obviously, but I’m thinking someone like fellow keeper Jimmy Glass who scored the last-minute goal against Plymouth Argyle to keep Carlisle United in the Football League in 1999. He was on loan, so three league games and one goal from your glovesman, keeping you up in the process. That must be hard to beat?”

View image in fullscreen Scott Carson: legend. Photograph: Peter Powell/Reuters

“Crewe are currently on a run of four 1-1 draws in the league,” writes Sam Hurst. “How long do we have to keep this up before we can start thinking about the record for consecutive identical scores?”

“Olimpia Cluj won the 2010-11 Romanian Liga I women’s title, finishing the season with a goal difference of +242,” notes Graham Clayton. “Has there been an example of a team having a larger GD either during or at the end of the season?”

“When announced, Sweden’s 25-man squad for the current Nations League internationals contained just one player currently playing in the country’s top flight, the Allsvenskan: Hammarby’s Hampus Skoglund. Has a senior international squad ever contained fewer players from its own country’s top domestic division (excluding countries where there is no professional domestic league)?” asks Derek Robertson.

“Oxford United goalkeeper Simon Eastwood was sent off towards the end of United’s Football League Trophy (can’t remember the then sponsors) game at AFC Wimbledon on 9 January 2024, with the U’s losing 2-0 to be eliminated from the competition. With Oxford subsequently winning promotion to the Championship and remaining there for two seasons, that was the club’s last involvement in the trophy until they travel to Exeter City on 4 October this year. Because the red card is competition-specific, Eastwood’s suspension comes into play for this game. Is this the longest gap between a dismissal and subsequent punishment (999 days, or two years, eight months, 25 days)?” asks Martin Brodetsky.

Sports.title: Roy Keane tells Man City players to ‘stick Premier League medals in the bin’
Sports.content:
Manchester City's Premier League winners should throw their medals in the bin, according to former Manchester United midfielder Roy Keane.

City were found guilty of all charges over serious breaches of financial rules on Tuesday after inflating their financial position by more than £900million between 2008 and 2019.



3 Manchester City are going through the ringer after being found guilty of all charges Credit: Getty

While the club have denied all wrongdoing, with City chief executive Ferran Soriano stating that 'irrefutable evidence has been provided to the Premier League', Keane criticised the club after England's UEFA Nations League 2-0 win over Czechia.

What did Keane say?

"They knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they still done it," the Irishman said.

"And if I was a player with the success of the last few years - I’d 100 per cent be sticking those medals in the bin."



Presenter Mark Pougatch then asked if the players would feel let down by the club, Keane replied: "100 per cent you would. It’s cheating.

"You’re hearing nonsense from ex-players saying they won on the pitch. But it was cheating. There was cheating going on.



"It’s tough for the players, the manager. You’ve got owners who are quite happy cheating.

"It’s very difficult going forward for these players to maintain the level of excellence."



Fellow pundit Ian Wright added: "[City owners] have told them that nothing bad’s going on. If you’re a player, something’s not right there.

"It’s unprecedented what we’re seeing right now. But in respect to the owners and what they’ve done. Terrible."

talkSPORT verdict

Speaking on Breakfast on Wednesday morning, Alan Brazil referenced Keane's medals quotes.

3 City won three Premier League titles during the period in question Credit: AFP



"I don't agree with that. It's not their fault," Brazil said.

And Ally McCoist agreed with Brazil, adding: "I think the City players can be as angry with the owners as the fans can and as every other fan can, to be honest with you.

"Because the players aren't, you wouldn't think, complicit in it.

"I think they're going to get hammered. [The Premier League] said, misstated accounts, concealed the true state of their finances from their auditors and football regulators, made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the league's investigation and breach of their duties of cooperation and utmost good faith.

"See when you read it like that, it's... no, I disagree with Roy. Would the titles and cups not be tainted? Yes, definitely."

Brazil then continued: "It can't take the players' memories or the fans' memories away, can it?"



3 McCoist didn't agree with Keane's suggestion about binning the winners medals Credit: talkSPORT

"Absolutely, that's the thing," McCoist concluded.

Sports.title: Argentina duo blocked by club from attending Lionel Messi’s farewell match
Sports.content:
AS Roma have blocked Paulo Dybala and Nahuel Molina from travelling to Argentina to attend Lionel Messi's international farewell fixture.

The Inter Miami forward will play against Benin at the Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, in what will mark his final appearance on the international stage.

3 Dybala has repeatedly called Messi his idol throughout his career Credit: Getty

However, the Serie A club will not allow the pair to attend for 'sporting and logistical reasons', despite both players helping Messi win the 2022 World Cup in Qatar.

The Italian giants released a statement on Tuesday to clarify that both the Argentine internationals will remain at the Trigoria training base during the upcoming international window.

A statement said: "AS Roma announces that Paulo Dybala and Nahuel Molina will not participate in the event organised in Argentina for the match between Argentina and Benin on October 6.

"The club recognises the importance of this appointment for the two players, who are linked to Lionel Messi and played a key role in his victory at the 2022 World Cup.

"The club’s choice was based on sporting and logistical reasons, linked to the length of the intercontinental trip and the proximity of official commitments.

"AS Roma expresses its utmost respect for Lionel Messi and his extraordinary career, wishing him and the Argentine Federation a special evening."

World Cup winners together

Messi announced his retirement from international football following Argentina's defeat to Spain in the World Cup final, which coincided with the passing of his father.

For both Roma players, they were not named in Lionel Scaloni's squad for the friendlies; however, youngster Matias Soule has been allowed to travel after he was called up for his country.

The 23-year-old winger had stepped away from the camp after he was granted compassionate leave to welcome his newborn son, and has now returned to resume squad preparations.

However, it will be a tough pill to swallow for the Roma duo after Dybala has shared the pitch with Messi on 18 occasions, while Molina has played alongside the icon in 53 appearances.

3 Roma want the players to prepare for their match against Como after the international break Credit: Getty

End of an era

The match will mark Messi's final cap of an illustrious international career spanning over two decades.

The 39-year-old has scored 125 times in 207 caps, and he will be preparing for his final chapter in Buenos Aires on October 6 against Benin.

80,000 tickets sold out in just 90 minutes, and the Argentine Football Association is preparing a special celebration fit for its captain, including a shirt designed for the occasion.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner has won the 2022 World Cup with his country and two Copa America titles.

Despite his age, he has showed no signs of slowing down as he scored eight goals in North America this summer.

Before his farewell game on October 6, Argentina have fixtures against Bolivia and Burkina Faso.

3 Messi will officially call time on his Argentina career Credit: Getty

During the summer, Messi released a statement announcing his retirement. It read: "After the time that has passed since the final, and after giving it a lot of thought, I want to let everyone know that I am retiring from the Argentina national team.

"It was a decision that hurt – and still hurts deep down – but I understand that the time has come. I swear to you that I always gave it my all – not just in these last few years when we won everything, but before that too.

"I always fought and left everything on the field for this jersey, to bring you joy and make you, through football, feel proud to be Argentinian."

Sports.title: Unhappy Cristiano Ronaldo to have crisis talks with Portugal manager over broken promise
Sports.content:
Unhappy Cristiano Ronaldo to have crisis talks with Portugal manager over broken promise

Cristiano Ronaldo has been left angered by Portugal manager Jorge Jesus just two matches into his tenure.

The 41-year-old forward is set to meet with the head coach and Portuguese Football Federation president Pedro Proenca this week to resolve his unhappiness.



3 Ronaldo is set to hold crisis talks after being left on the bench against Norway on Sunday Credit: AFP

According to Record, Ronaldo is frustrated after he was an unused substitute for the first time in 18 years against Norway on Sunday.

Jesus' decision not to bring the five-time Ballon d'Or winner off the bench is said to have broken a pre-match promise made to Ronaldo.

Ronaldo set for talks

The Portugal boss revealed both in private and during his pre-match press conference that he planned to give him a 30-minute cameo in Oslo.



However, despite warming up on the touchline, Ronaldo did not feature in the 2-1 away victory.

Ronaldo is Portugal's all-time leading scorer and appearance maker with 146 goals in 234 caps for his country.



He is now set to hold talks with Jesus and Proenca on Wednesday, the report adds.

The trio will meet in Copenhagen ahead of their Nations League clash with Denmark the following day.



Portugal head into the match with a 100 per cent record in the competition after wins over Wales and Norway.

Ronaldo started their opener against the former last week, playing 67 minutes as captain.

He was subsequently replaced as skipper against Norway by Ruben Dias.

3 Jesus opted against bringing Ronaldo on despite promising to give him 30 minutes off the bench Credit: Getty

His side continue their campaign away to Denmark before the final match of the current international break at home to Norway in Porto on Sunday.



Ronaldo under Jesus

Ronaldo's tension with Jesus comes just months after the pair won the Saudi Pro League title together.

The veteran coach was in charge of Al Nassr last season as they finished two points clear of nearest challengers Al Hilal.

During his time as manager, Ronaldo scored 30 goals in 37 appearances.

Having left Al Nassr, Jesus succeeded Roberto Martinez as national team boss in July.



It came after Portugal were knocked out of the World Cup in the last 16 by eventual winners Spain.

3 Ronaldo will meet with Jesus and Proenca in Copenhagen on Wednesday Credit: Getty

Jesus has signed a four-year deal through to the end of the 2030 edition of the tournament.

He will also oversee the current Nations League campaign and Portugal's quest to reach Euro 2028.

Sports.title: Anthony Gordon quickly corrects himself on Trent Alexander-Arnold comment in live TV interview
Sports.content:
Anthony Gordon quickly corrects himself on Trent Alexander-Arnold comment in live TV interview

Anthony Gordon appeared to suggest Trent Alexander-Arnold should have played more for England, before quickly correcting himself.

Real Madrid defender Alexander-Arnold made his first appearance for the Three Lions since October 2024.

2 Gordon put England 1-0 up against Czech Republic thanks to an Alexander-Arnold assist Credit: Getty

It was also the first time the 27-year-old has played under Thomas Tuchel.

Alexander-Arnold was the ninth right-back used during Tuchel’s short tenure so far and came in with something of a point to prove.

He did just that by providing an assist for Gordon in the 2-0 win over Czech Republic on Tuesday night.

Speaking to ITV after the game, the Barcelona forward said: “I make that run time and time again and only a certain number of players have got that ability, technique and bravery to be willing to make the mistake trying that pass, so credit to Trent.

“That’s why he’s so good and I’ve been dying to play with him for that reason.”

He continued: “He’s had his own journey with England.

“Probably should’ve played… Would’ve liked to have played more than he has, sorry, but he’s been a great character during this camp, I’ve really enjoyed being around him.”

Thomas Tuchel’s reaction

Three Lions boss Tuchel told talkSPORT that he was happy with Alexander-Arnold’s performance on the night.

He said: “In the first half, I think he struggled a little bit with the position. We wanted a little bit more offensive actions, a bit more dynamic movements that he's used to from his characteristics.

2 Alexander-Arnold made his 35th England appearance on Tuesday Credit: Getty

“Second half, we put him a little bit deeper and had one change with Eberechi Eze for Myles Lewis-Skelly.

“We got in itself a bit more offensive [position] and that allowed Trent to be in a bit of a deeper position, which suits him more because he's strong on the ball and can deliver from half-field.

“This is exactly what he did, a half-field cross after a mistake from the opponent on point and Anthony had a beautiful goal.”

Alexander-Arnold himself was pleased to be back in the England fold after two years away.

He said: "It was amazing. It's always an honour to represent my country. It's been a long time, but I've always believed I can play for England.

“That belief has always been there and it was about proving it at club level.

"The manager gave me a chance, now hopefully he is happy with how I played."

England face Croatia on Saturday, before travelling back home to play Czech Republic at Wembley next Tuesday.

Both matches will be live on talkSPORT.

Sports.title: Scotland suffer two damning feats as new manager oversees unwanted 55-year first
Sports.content:
Scotland suffer two damning feats as new manager oversees unwanted 55-year first

Sebastien Pocognoli's start to his Scotland reign has gone from bad to worse after his side suffered a 3-0 defeat to Switzerland.

Following a 0-0 draw away at Slovenia over the weekend, Scotland once again disappointed in the Nations League.

3 Pocognoli has failed to win any of his opening two matches in charge of Scotland Credit: AFP

Pocognoli, who guided Monaco to seventh spot in Ligue 1 last season, was announced as Steve Clarke's successor in August.

Scotland fans were optimistic that the Belgian, who is the country's first foreign manager since Berti Vogts [2002-2004], would build on the feel-good factor following the World Cup.

But Pocognoli has endured a nightmare start, with his first home match at Hampden Park against Switzerland proving to be a horror show.

The hosts were reduced to ten man after Jack Hendry was sent off after just 11 minutes, with Ricardo Rodriguez proceeding to break the deadlock from the resulting free-kick.

And Murat Yakin's men compounded further misery on Scotland in the second half, with Nico Elvedi and Zeki Amdouni getting on the score sheet.

What unwanted history has Pocognoli overseen?

With no wins from his opening two games, Pocognoli is the first manager to suffer the unwanted feat since George Burley in May 2008.

Pocognoli is still searching for a first Scotland goal, with his side mustering just one attempt against Switzerland on Tuesday night.

It's now four games in a row that Scotland have failed to find the back of the net - the first time this has happened since 1971.

Meanwhile, Scotland have also now failed to keep a clean sheet in their last eight home matches.

That is their longest run since they conceded in ten consecutive home fixtures between October 2001 and September 2003.

3 Scotland will be looking to bounce back with a win in their next Nations League clash against North Macedonia on Saturday Credit: Getty

What has Pocognoli said about Scotland's defeat?

Despite the humbling loss, Pocognoli insists he remains proud of his side for how they fought, despite being a man down for the majority of the game.

The 39-year-old also stressed his pride that Scotland didn't concede five or six goals in their match as he looks ahead to Saturday's clash away at North Macedonia.

He told BBC Scotland: "They [the players] worked with ten men for 80 minutes, maybe more, they showed great character to stick together for that time.

"It's not easy against a good team to be with ten men, it will be more about the reaction because we were so excited to start this first page of the book at home.

"We were ready to deliver the game we wanted from the first minute. We had an unlucky red card, punished with the free-kick, that's the worst scenario.

"We could probably manage the situation better, that's a fact, we create a press where we get the ball back, but from a transition we concede another transition.

3 Scotland are on the cusp of failing to score in five successive games for the first time in their history Credit: Getty

"We could probably defend better, we have to fight with ten men, the guys did the best they could and hopefully we will remember this night differently later on, we have to move on and get a good result in Macedonia.

"We feel sorry for Kieron [Bowie], it's not something we wanted to do [substitute him early] but we had to be smart to keep us alive as long as possible in the game.

"I'm proud because you can collapse in that moment and maybe lose two or three more goals, because they are a team that don't give the ball away cheaply.

"We didn't have a lot of set pieces to maybe have a bit of luck.

"I had a good welcome, it's just frustrating because I said before the game I want to have a good game.

"Hopefully this will be a nice night to remember in the future as part of the process."

Sports.title: Man City board must go and club kicked out of Premier League if appeal fails, says former chairman
Sports.content:
Man City board must go and club kicked out of Premier League if appeal fails, says former chairman

Ex-Manchester City chairman David Bernstein has called for the removal of the current board in the wake of the club’s guilty verdict.

City were found guilty of all Premier League financial breaches against them by an independent commission on Tuesday.

3 Man City chiefs Khaldoon Al-Mubarak and Ferran Soriano must find a way to overturn the charges levelled at the club in an upcoming appeal Credit: Getty

The club were found to have arranged ‘sham’ contracts with a host of their commercial partners to artificially inflate the club's revenues by around £900m.

City also failed to co-operate in good faith with the Premier League during the investigation.

Club chiefs insist they are innocent and are ‘surprised’ at the panel’s decision. They have until Friday to appeal the decision.

It is understood that the Premier League are eager to conclude the case at the earliest opportunity.

Should they fail in their appeal, then City are facing unprecedented sanctions that could result in a heavy points deduction or even expulsion from the Premier League.

Bernstein, a boyhood Manchester City fan who acted as chairman from 1998 to 2003, has slammed the club’s dealings over the nine-year period in question and says the position of the current board is now untenable.

Bernstein: Throw the book at Man City board

"I can't think of a penalty strong enough for this, really. I mean, this is absolutely terrible,” Bernstein told talkSPORT Drive.

“I want to raise another question, and that is the position of the board of directors. Because the directors of the club, including the chief executive, who's been there for years and went through this through this period, are responsible for the running of the club in every respect.

“And again, if this was a public company of some sort, I think the directors with something as serious as this, would have to stand down or be suspended pending the outcome of all this... appeal or no appeal.

“I don't think the present management can credibly continue. Now, I doubt if the Abu Dhabi owners would be very happy with that possibility.”

3 Ex-City chairman David Bernstein has called for harsh punishments if the club are unable to overturn the verdict Credit: Getty

Manchester City CEO Ferran Soriano sent a video message to Manchester City staff on Tuesday evening defending the club’s innocence in the face of the damning verdict.

He went on to describe the outcome as a conspiracy theory created by the Premier League.

Bernstein doubled down on his criticism of the board, accusing them of ‘abuse’ while sparing a thought for the club’s supporters.

“What credibility can a board of directors have who've been involved in systematic abuse over a long period?,” Bernstein added.

"You feel sorry for the City fans. I am a City fan of 70 years. I've supported the club. So this is, you know, I find this really doubly hard.

“I don't know the answer,” he continued. “And part of the reason is that until we understand where we are with the appeal process, you know, we don't know whether something's going to be imposed quickly or what.”

3 Ferran Soriano, now engaged in a huge legal battle with the Premier League, insists the club are innocent Credit: Getty

Bernstein then proposed a major sanction for the club in the event that they fail in their upcoming appeal against the charges.

Time to go

“If this got settled now, you could see one source scenario and set of penalties,” he said.

“But if it drags on for a year or two, heaven forbid, that would be the worst thing for everybody. But if it did, then you'd have a different situation. So it's a little difficult to predict. But all I would say is that money is not sufficient now.

“But if this, if these charges stand now and let's say the appeal does not happen or fails, then I'm afraid for the club I love that they've got to come out of the Premier League. This is beyond awful."

Sports.title: Eight England stars handed 8/10 ratings but one player ‘missed an opportunity’ in Czechia win
Sports.content:
Eight England stars handed 8/10 ratings but one player ‘missed an opportunity’ in Czechia win

England returned to winning ways following Saturday's defeat to Spain by easing to a 2-0 win away at ten-man Czechia.

The Three Lions threw away a 2-1 lead to lose 3-2 against the World Cup champions in their Nations League opener.

6 England beat Czechia in Prague thanks to goals from Harry Kane and Anthony Gordon Credit: Getty

But they have now registered their first points of the tournament ahead of this weekend's trip to Croatia, live on talkSPORT.

Following a first half lacking in quality, England finally made their extra man advantage count just two minutes after the break.

The hosts were reduced to ten men in the 25th minute following a horror tackle from Pavel Sulc on Elliot Anderson.

And it was Anthony Gordon who made the breakthrough, with the Barcelona winger getting on the end of Trent Alexander-Arnold's whipped in delivery to head home into the far bottom right corner.

Captain Harry Kane then doubled the visitors' lead in the 69th minute to bring up his 87th goal on the international stage.

The Bayern Munich marksman, who will equal Peter Shilton's record appearances [125] if he plays in England's remaining two matches this break, reacted quickest to a loose ball in the box.

His first-time left-footed strike nestled into the bottom corner as he put his missed penalty against Spain behind him.

What did Adrian Durham say about England?

Reacting to England's performance live on air, legendary talkSPORT broadcaster Adrian Durham said: "There are a lot of things that need to improve for England if they are to win a major tournament, there's no doubt about that.

"But they were taken by surprise with Czechia going down to ten men in the first half, they couldn't really negotiate that properly until after half-time.

"So what I'm going to do, is give Thomas Tuchel a lot of credit for his half-time team talk, a change of [Eberechi] Eze coming on for Myles Lewis-Skelly, a really attacking change, I think it worked.

6 Gordon opened the scoring with a deft header back across goal Credit: Getty

6 Kane put the Three Lions two goals to the good with a clinical finish into the bottom corner Credit: Getty

"All the subs in the second half [Eze, Alex Scott, Jude Bellingham, Rio Ngumoha and Morgan Gibbs-White] really impressed.

"So if you take the second half in isolation, and yes it was against ten men, but those ten men were defending - or trying to defend resolutely - that was their game plan.

"And England beat the ten men, so I don't think we have any complaints about that second half whatsoever."

Here is how Durham rated and slated England's stars from Prague...

Flash Gordon

The ex-Newcastle star is quickly becoming England's man for the big occasions having now scored in three international matches in a row.

Firing in the opener in the World Cup semi-final against Argentina, before grabbing England's equaliser against Spain last time out, Gordon is enjoying his best spell for the Three Lions.

Incredibly, nine of the forward's 11 goal contributions for England have come in 2026 alone.

Gordon has either register a goal or assist in each of his last six matches under Tuchel's tutelage.

A constant threat, Gordon was awarded an 8/10 rating by Durham.

Waxing lyrical over the 25-year-old, he simply stated: "Excellent again."

6 Gordon has scored three goals and supplied four assists in his last six England matches Credit: Getty

Took his chance

Featuring for the first time for England since a 1-0 win over Andorra in June 2025, Alexander-Arnold showed why he is deserving of a spot in the squad.

The Real Madrid right-back was overlooked by Tuchel against Spain, with the German insisting Jarell Quansah was preferred due to his speed and defending.

But the ex-Liverpool man boasts a trait unlike any defender in the squad: his passing.

That was on show throughout the match, producing a moment of magic to set up Gordon with his inch-perfect cross.

While he may have been booed by Real fans over his plays this term, he was one of England's stars players on his return to international action.

Awarded an 8/10 rating, Durham said: "Good runs forward, terrific passing and an assist."

6 Alexander-Arnold could now keep his place for England against Croatia on Saturday Credit: Getty

Needed Mor from him

While Alexander-Arnold took his chance in the line-up, the same can't be said for Chelsea's Morgan Rogers.

The versatile Blues star, who can play as an attacking midfielder or on the left wing, featured in the No.10 slot in place of Jude Bellingham.

But despite hitting the post in the first half, Durham believes that Rogers lacked a cutting edge in the final third.

Given a 6/10 rating, only Lewis-Skelly, who was awarded a 5/10, was rated lower.

Durham said of Rogers: "Missed an opportunity in the No.10 position."

6 Here is how Durham rated England's starters against Czechia

There were also 8/10 ratings for substitutes Eze, debutant Scott, Ngumoha, Bellingham and Gibbs-White.

Mewanhile, manager Thomas Tuchel was handed a 7/10.

Sports.title: Tragic footballer Courtney Meppen-Walter became a father two months before death aged 32
Sports.content:
Tragic footballer Courtney Meppen-Walter became a father two months before death aged 32

Tragic former England youth captain Courtney Meppen-Walter became a father for the third time just months before his death aged 32.

Ex-Manchester City star Meppen-Walter's passing was announced by his current club, Bury, on Tuesday. No details have been announced regarding the circumstances of the defender's death.

'We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of former player Courtney Meppen-Walter, at the age of 32,' a Bury statement read.

'The thoughts and condolences of everyone at Bury FC are with his family and friends at this incredibly difficult time.'

The 32-year-old leaves behind two daughters and a son - having become a father again in July when he welcomed his second girl.

A candle light vigil was held for Meppen-Walter on Tuesday night, with family and friends releasing balloons and fireworks in honour of the 32-year-old.

We are deeply saddened to learn of the passing of former player Courtney Meppen-Walter, at the age of 32.



The thoughts and condolences of everyone at #buryfc are with his family and friends at this incredibly difficult time. pic.twitter.com/v4Qlu2Twhn — Bury Football Club (@buryfcofficial) September 29, 2026

Courtney Meppen-Walter, who played for Man City and England at youth level, has died at the age of 32. He became a father for the third time in July. Pictured in 2010

Meppen-Walter had been part of Manchester City's youth set-up and captained England's Under-18 side. He was released by Man City in 2013 after he was jailed for 16 months for causing the death of two people by careless driving.

Kulwant Singh, 32, and his sister Ravel Kaur, 37, were both pronounced dead at the scene following a high-speed crash in Manchester.

Meppen-Walter was released after serving half of that sentence.

The defender joined Carlisle United following his release from prison and spent two seasons at the Cumbrian side.

Meppen-Walter later had spells at Ashton United, Stockport County, Glossop North End, Chorley, AFC Telford United, Radcliffe, Guiseley, Nantwich Town, Bury and Stalybridge Celtic.

Meppen-Walter was released by Bury in the summer of 2025 after a loan spell at Stalybridge Celtic.

In 2019, when Meppen-Walter was playing for Chorley, he was banned from being behind the wheel for 22 months after he was caught drink-driving.

Meppen-Walter had been found to have been more than twice the legal limit when he was stopped in his vehicle by police in Manchester city centre.

The footballer had been arrested and taken to a police station where he gave a positive reading of 85 microgrammes of alcohol in 100 millilitres of breath – the legal limit being 35mcg.

Meppen-Walter was jailed in 2013 for causing the death of two people by dangerous driving

Brother and sister Kulwant Singh and Ravel-Kaur died following the high-speed crash in Manchester

Meppen-Walter, right, was released by Manchester City following the verdict in 2013

Meppen-Walter played for Carlisle United between 2013 and 2015, before a career in non-league football

Meppen-Walter was also ordered to serve a 12-month community order, as well as completing 80 hours of unpaid work.

'I know what you are probably thinking and what everyone else is thinking,’ Meppen-Walter said in court.

‘I will probably get called every name under the sun and I deserve it. I'm just embarrassed.'

The court had heard that alcohol played no part in the deaths of Mr Singh and Ms Kaur who had come to the UK from Afghanistan in 2001 to start a new life after fleeing persecution by the Taliban.

A pre-sentence probation report noted his drink-driving reflected 'poor judgment' when considering his previous conviction and that 'again he has failed to consider the consequences of his actions'.

Caitriona McLaughlin, defending, said: 'The most significant mitigation in this case is his genuine remorse which has been reflected throughout. He is truly sorry for his actions.

'It was a mistake and it is the one and only drink mistake on his record.'

Chairwoman of the bench Margaret Hutchinson said: 'We hope this will be a lesson to you and we will not see you in court again.

'Drink-driving is a very serious matter and the consequences could have been much graver than today.'

Sports.title: Man City's appeal will FAIL, warns club's former adviser, as scale of cheating is laid bare by scathing Premier League statement revealing their £900m 'sham' after being found guilty of most serious of 115 charges
Sports.content:
Manchester City's appeal against their guilty verdict in their battle with the Premier League will fail, their former financial adviser has said. The Premier League condemned City for 'sham' deals in an excoriating statement which confirmed they are guilty of the most severe financial rule breaches. City fiddled with their books for around £900million, repeatedly misleading the league about their financial situation, and now people are calling for the harshest response. City's former financial adviser, Stefan Borson, said: 'Absolutely scathing announcement from the Premier League. Shams, misleading auditors, conspiracy. All difficult to prove. Now proved, it is very difficult to unwind on appeal.' Manchester United legend Rio Ferdinand posted some embarrassed face emojis on X and said: 'The wording “sham”'. The Premier League have confirmed that Manchester City are guilty of the most serious financial rule breaches Former Man City financial adviser Stefan Borson says any appeal they make will fail Former Liverpool star Stan Collymore called for extreme sanctions, writing: 'This now is the biggest football scandal in British football history. Nothing comes close. 'Expulsion from the Prem and EFL a bare minimum, several billion in fines, Abu Dhabi struck off global football ownership, selling all clubs, an independent commission into all Premier League clubs' financial conduct, and where applicable, criminal fraud charges.' Meanwhile, Piers Morgan wrote: 'It's official: The Premier League confirms Manchester City are the biggest cheats in British football history. 'Punishment must hurt: Relegate them, strip them of their fraudulently won titles + dock them 25pts for first 5 seasons if/when they get back in the Premier League.' Popular football streamer Mark Goldbridge said: 'So the Premier League announce City are guilty on all financial breach charges with nearly a billion put through the club wrongly. City come out and say they have evidence they are innocent. 'Whatever happens from here, City aren't ever shaking these allegations.' On Friday, Daily Mail Sport reported how City had been found guilty of a series of breaches over a nine-year, glittering period in its history, in a verdict which sent shockwaves through football and opened the door to huge penalties including possible expulsion. However, there had been no official comment from the Premier League on the findings of an independent panel who oversaw a hearing that concluded in December 2024. That has now dramatically changed. In a lengthy statement, the Premier League say City arranged 'sham contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on "sham" agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs'. It also says the club falsely altered the financial picture at the Etihad to the tune of £900m. The club had agreed exorbitant sponsorship deals with a number of companies, but those sponsors only paid part of the fee. The rest was propped up by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club. Premier League CEO Richard Masters claimed that the commission's verdict had 'vindicated' the league's decision to pursue the charges

Your browser does not support iframes.

As the Premier League note, this allowed the City to 'artificially inflate the club’s revenues' and therefore spend more under Premier League rules. The higher the revenue a club records, the more they are permitted to spend. Moreover, further 'sham' deals, funded by ADUG, allowed the club to 'record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred'. The Premier League say that revenues were inflated and costs reduced to the tune of £900m in an attempt to comply with spending rules. The result was that the club 'filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators'. It added that the club was 'significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits' during the time period in question, 2009-2018 when it won eight major trophies. Had City reported accurately 'it would have been in breach of both the League's and UEFA's spending limits by a very substantial amount'. The panel also found that City committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and good faith in that it failed to assist the Premier League's four-year investigation, triggered by the emergence of club emails obtained by a hacker. Indeed, City had 'made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the PL investigation'. Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, said: 'The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade. 'It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently. 'It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously. 'This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches. Now we have the Commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans.' Manchester City have insisted on their innocence throughout the saga (Pep Guardiola pictured with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak) In a statement released a short time later, City said it was ‘disappointed and surprised’ and referred to the ‘opinion of the Premier League Commission’. It added: ‘The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums. ‘The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe. ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence. ‘The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete.’ City have until Friday to appeal. Man City were first charged with the 115 breaches in February 2023. While that totemic number stuck, the figure – as they subsequently corrected – was actually 130. Of those, 54 were charges of ‘failure to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information’ while there were 14 charges of ‘failure to provide accurate financial reports for player and manager compensation’. Both sets related to alleged offences between 2009 and 2018 (2009-2018), an eight-year period which saw the club win four Premier League titles, the FA Cup, and three League Cup competitions. There were also five charges of ‘failure to comply with UEFA’s regulations, including Financial Fair Play Regulations’ and seven charges of breaching the Premier League’s profit and sustainability regulations (PSR) between 2015 and 2018. There were also 35 counts of failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations between 2018 and 2023. The hearing into the 130 breaches began last September at London’s International Dispute Resolution Centre, with the Premier League sparing no expense and enlisting KCs Adam Lewis and Andrew Hunter to take its case.

Sports.title: Historic speedway trophy to go on public display after years in storage thanks to Daily Mail chairman Lord Rothermere
Sports.content:
Historic speedway trophy to go on public display after years in storage thanks to Daily Mail chairman Lord Rothermere

One of the world’s great sporting trophies is to be put on public display after it was loaned to the National Speedway Museum in Broxbourne, Hertfordshire.

Lord Rothermere, the Daily Mail chairman, presented the Daily Mail National Speedway Trophy to Bert Harkins, the chairman of the World Speedway Riders’ Association, at the company’s London offices on Tuesday afternoon.

The trophy, which features a rider, modelled out of silver and pewter, taking a corner, his left foot dragging in the dirt, was contested by the leading teams in the sport between 1931 and 1964, when Oxford were its final winners.

It used to be on display in the reception area of the company’s former printworks at Surrey Quays and has been kept in storage.

‘It does not belong in my cupboard,’ Lord Rothermere said. ‘It belongs to speedway and to people who compete in the sport and love the sport.’

Speedway enthusiast and Plymouth Gladiators fund-raiser Graham Read said he hoped the re-emergence of the trophy could act as the catalyst for a Champions League-style competition with the trophy as the prize.

Lord Rothermere presents Bert Harkins (left) and Graham Read (centre) with the Daily Mail National Speedway Trophy as the iconic trophy prepares to be put on public display

The speedway trophy was contested by the leading teams in the sport between 1931 and 1964

Sports.title: 'Heartbroken' Micah Richards says Man City verdict has left him 'ANGRY' after Premier League found club guilty of benefiting from £900m sham deals - with his 2012 title now shrouded in doubt
Sports.content:
'Heartbroken' Micah Richards says Man City verdict has left him 'ANGRY' after Premier League found club guilty of benefiting from £900m sham deals - with his 2012 title now shrouded in doubt

Former Manchester City defender Micah Richards says the Premier League’s damning verdict on the club has left him devastated and heartbroken.

City were found to have engaged in a £900million scheme to either inflate revenues or reduce costs through a series of 'sham' arrangements between 2009 and 2018 in order to avoid breaching league and UEFA financial regulations.

The eight-time Premier League champions face severe sanctions, although City remain defiant and immediately declared their intention to appeal.

Speaking on The Rest is Football podcast, Richards – who lifted the Premier League title with City in 2012 – said: 'The reports were troubling. I saw the words which were used by the Premier League in sham contracts and I felt absolutely devastated.

'I’ve been at that club since I was 14 years old, I would die for that club. I achieved my dream at Manchester City, but then to hear these reports, and not only me as an ex-player, but the fans, what they have to go through, absolutely devastating.'

Richards described speaking to the fan he used to live with as a young player at the club, adding: 'My digs man, he rang me and he was literally in tears and asking me about information, which I don’t know, I haven’t got the answers to tell him.

Richards is rarely spotted without a smile but will struggle to manage one in the near future

The former England international won the 2011/12 Premier League title with Manchester City but is under threat of having the accolade stripped from him

'And that’s someone who’s supported the club for 60-odd years, and the uncertainty around it is just heartbreaking.

'To have a headline of this nature for a club that I love so much, it’s been difficult. If you listen to the reports, they are damning. I feel saddened, I feel angry, I feel a little bit confused because, on the other side, you have City’s side of the story.'

What City’s punishment will be remains to be seen, but the implications are likely to spread far and wide – with the possibility that they could be kicked out of the Premier League and also stripped of the titles they won in that period.

'There are no winners in this,' added Richards. 'If Man City do the appeal and they get off, it’s still going to be tarnished. And, if they’re found guilty after the appeal, what happens then?

'And it’s not just Man City fans or Man City players, it’s the whole of the Premier League comes into question. This could be something that goes on for years and years and years.'

Former Manchester United captain Roy Keane said, if he was a City player, he would throw all the medals in the bin - referencing Brian Clough's famous words to his Leeds players during an ill-fated 44-day spell at Elland Road.

Speaking on ITV, Keane said: 'They knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they’ve still done it, and, if I was a player, I’d be 100 per cent sticking those medals in the bin.

'It’s cheating. You’re hearing nonsense about some ex-players saying, ‘Oh well, they won on the pitch’. Because it was cheating! It was cheating going on.'

Sports.title: Cristiano Ronaldo set for showdown meeting with manager and head of Portuguese FA today after 41-year-old skipped training following furious reaction to sub snub
Sports.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo set for showdown meeting with manager and head of Portuguese FA today after 41-year-old skipped training following furious reaction to sub snub

Cristiano Ronaldo is set for an emergency meeting today with national boss Jorge Jesus and the head of the Portuguese FA.

A row is brewing after the 41-year-old captain - who skipped training on Wednesday - was left on the bench for his side's 2-1 win over Norway. It was the first time in 18 years that Ronaldo has not featured at all for Portugal - aside from injury or suspension absences.

At full-time on Sunday, Ronaldo stormed straight down the tunnel and did not return to thank the travelling fans alongside his team-mates.

Jesus had originally planned to bring on the veteran striker for a 30-minute cameo but then decided to leave him on the bench.

The decision was validated by Portugal holding on to win the Nations League clash but Ronaldo's anger has led to FA chief Pedro Proenca hurriedly changing his travel plans to sit down for a three-way meeting today, according to Record.

Proenca was due to fly to the Azores for an Under-21s match but dealing with Ronaldo's discontent has now become the priority.

Cristiano Ronaldo was angry at being an unused substitute for Portugal's win over Norway

Portugal face Denmark on Thursday but Ronaldo did not take part in team training today, along with Joao Felix and Francisco Conceicao.

According to A Bola, he briefly spoke to Jesus and left Malmo's training facilities due to the Swedish club not having the right equipment.

It is an inauspicious start to the relationship between Jesus and Ronaldo, who opted not to retire from international duty after the World Cup.

Only a week ago, Ronaldo reiterated his commitment to the cause, saying: 'I had a conversation with our president, with our coach (about his future).

'I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I'm not doing anything here.

'I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

'This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.'

Ronaldo will turn 42 in February and has scored three goals in five games for Al-Nassr so far in the Saudi Pro League this season.

Jesus and Ronaldo worked together successfully for a year when the 71-year-old was in charge of Al-Nassr but they could be on a collision course if the forward's playing time remains limited.

Roberto Martinez stepped down after Portugal's 1-0 World Cup defeat by Spain and when Jesus was announced as his successor, he was asked the Ronaldo question.

Jesus insisted: 'As long as he's playing and is in a condition to be selected, I will pick him, within certain limits and under the conditions that I consider best for the national team.'

Goncalo Ramos, 25, scored the winner against Norway on Sunday and is considered by many to be the natural evolution up front for Portugal.

But it seems as long as Ronaldo is around the national side, the five-time Ballon d'Or winner's playing demands will continue to be an issue for the new boss.

Sports.title: Czech Republic 0-2 England PLAYER RATINGS: How did Trent Alexander-Arnold fare on his return? Who was almost embarrassed by an early error? Who proved he belongs at international level?
Sports.content:
Czech Republic 0-2 England PLAYER RATINGS: How did Trent Alexander-Arnold fare on his return? Who was almost embarrassed by an early error? Who proved he belongs at international level?

Thomas Tuchel alleviated some of the pressure off his back as England overcame Czech Republic to win 2-0 in the Nations League.

It was a frustrating start against a solid rearguard action from the hosts, but the sending-off of Pavel Sulc after 25 minutes saw England start to pick apart their opponents more.

Anthony Gordon broke the deadlock just after the restart as he met a cross from Trent Alexander-Arnold on the Real Madrid man's return to the starting line-up.

Harry Kane then doubled the lead with a first-time strike for the 87th goal of his Three Lions career.

KIERAN GILL brings you our player ratings.

England beat the Czech Republic 2-0 in the Nations League thanks to goals from Anthony Gordon (pictured) and Harry Kane

ENGLAND (4-2-3-1)

James Trafford – 6

Quick in charging forward when Czechia got behind England early on. When the hosts went down to 10 men after 25 minutes, his evening quietened.

Trent Alexander-Arnold – 7

Nice having him back, isn't it? This was his first England appearance since June 2025, and it was a classic cross which allowed Anthony Gordon to finally crack Czechia.

Trevoh Chalobah – 6

Strong block to deny Pavel Sulc, who was popping up in dangerous positions before his dismissal. Usually the deepest man as everyone else pushed forward.

Marc Guehi – 6

No error inside two minutes this time mercifully. A much more composed performance and encouraged to push up the pitch as Czechia sat back.

Trent Alexander-Arnold bagged an assist on his return to the England starting line-up

Lewis Hall – 7

Enjoyed his aggression and attacking. Hall & Gordon sounds a little like a solicitors firm, but actually, they were a lovely left-sided combination for England.

Elliot Anderson – 6

Early error allowed Sulc to break behind but Trafford covered by bravely smothering the ball. Sulc was then red-carded for a nasty foul on Anderson.

Myles Lewis-Skelly – 5

Cautioned for a late challenge on Lukas Cerv. Replaced at half-time owing to carrying that risk and with England craving more creativity by Anderson.

Bukayo Saka – 5

The Czech Republic goal appeared at his mercy until Jiri Slama produced the block à la John Terry. Not his most creative night for club or country.

Bukayo Saka could have scored a sitter and did not have his most creative night overall

Morgan Rogers – 6

Started ahead of Jude Bellingham at No 10. Good touch and turn before striking the post at 0-0. Run helped create England's second goal.

Anthony Gordon – 8

The Real Madrid right back produced the cross. Then the Barcelona left winger headed it in. Just like that, England led via their two talented Scousers.

Harry Kane – 7

Scored the clincher, doubling England’s lead when the ball sat nicely for him inside the Czechia box. Only ever needs one chance.

Harry Kane only ever needs once chance and bagged his 87th England goal in Prague

SUBS USED

Eberechi Eze (for Lewis-Skelly 45) – 6

Introduced to add extra creativity for England after a first half spent struggling to break through the Czech block.

Alex Scott (for Anderson 70) – 6

Now a senior England international. Deservedly so. Nice one-two which led to a 20-yard chance, fired wide.

Jude Bellingham (for Kane 70) – 6

Kane scored, then was replaced by Bellingham, who could have an easy runaround for 20 minutes or so. Denied making it 3-0.

Rio Ngumoha (for Saka 70) – 6

Replaced Saka to try to add a little invention from the right-hand side.

Morgan Gibbs-White (for Gordon, 81) – N/A

MANAGER: Thomas Tuchel – 7

Czechia were already sitting in a defensive shape. Then they went down to 10 men and dropped even deeper. But Gordon finally found the breakthrough. Phew.

CZECH REPUBLIC (4-3-3):

Kovar 6; Chaloupek 6, Hranac 5, Krejci 5, Slama 5; Cerv 5, Sulc 3, Sadilek 5 (Kral 56, 6); Radosta 5 (Ambros 57, 6), Hlozek 5, Karabec 5 (Lingr 45, 5)

Subs (not used): Kinsky, Kricfalusi, Zmrzly, Vasulin, Vitik, Hornicek, Bucha, Macek, Sacek

Manager: Santi Denia 5

REFEREE: Halil Meler – 6

Even Sulc didn’t sulk when he dismissed him for sending studs into Anderson.

Sports.title: Roy Keane claims Man City stars should BIN their medals won during period of 'cheating' and hits out at owners after club found guilty of £900m 'sham' in seismic Premier League verdict
Sports.content:
Roy Keane says he would bin his medals if he was a Manchester City player after they were found guilty of breaking the Premier League's financial rules for nine seasons. The Manchester United legend fears it will be hard for the current crop under Enzo Maresca to maintain their elite levels of performance under the cloud of 'cheating owners'. The Premier League has condemned City for making 'sham' agreements to manipulate their financial accounts to the tune of £900million over a nine-season period which saw them win eight trophies. 'They knew it would hurt a lot of people but they've still done it,' Keane told ITV Sport after England's 2-0 win over Czech Republic in the Nations League. 'If I was a player, I'd be 100 per cent sticking those medals in the bin. Of course you would, it's cheating. 'They won it on the pitch because cheating was going on. Roy Keane has claimed he would throw away his medals if he was a Manchester City player The Premier League have confirmed that Manchester City are guilty of the most serious financial rule breaches

Your browser does not support iframes.

'I think it's going to be very difficult for the players and the manager, the club, what they stand for, when you've got owners who are happy cheating. It's hard to maintain a level of excellence.' Ian Wright added: 'They told them nothing bad is going on. If you're a player, something is not right. 'It's very unprecedented and sad for everybody. The owners and what they've done, terrible.' Before the match, Wright had said: 'Unprecedented punishment is required here. It's a massive day for the Premier League. 'Very messy. It's a problem for them to be going to Liverpool (in their next fixture). In their real time, Liverpool were the team chasing them down. Look at what Jurgen Klopp went through to break them - it probably broke him.' On Friday, Daily Mail Sport reported how City had been found guilty of 114 of 115 charges against them. However, there had been no official comment from the Premier League on the findings of an independent panel who oversaw a hearing that concluded in December 2024. That has now dramatically changed. In a lengthy statement, the Premier League say City arranged 'sham contracts (which misrepresented the true agreement between the parties) with a number of its commercial partners, as well as relying on "sham" agreements with others, to artificially inflate the club's revenues and reduce its costs'. It also says the club falsely altered the financial picture at the Etihad to the tune of £900m. The club had agreed exorbitant sponsorship deals with a number of companies, but those sponsors only paid part of the fee. The rest was propped up by the Abu Dhabi United Group Investment & Development Ltd (ADUG), which owned the club. Premier League CEO Richard Masters claimed that the commission's verdict had 'vindicated' the league's decision to pursue the charges As the Premier League note, this allowed City to 'artificially inflate the club’s revenues' and therefore spend more under Premier League rules. The higher the revenue a club records, the more they are permitted to spend. Moreover, further 'sham' deals, funded by ADUG, allowed the club to 'record lower operating expenses than it actually incurred'. The Premier League say that revenues were inflated and costs reduced to the tune of £900m in an attempt to comply with spending rules. The result was that the club 'filed misstated accounts and concealed the true state of its finances from its auditors and football regulators'. It added that the club was 'significantly in breach of both the Premier League's and UEFA's spending limits' during the time period in question, 2009-2018 when it won eight major trophies. Had City reported accurately 'it would have been in breach of both the League's and UEFA's spending limits by a very substantial amount'. The panel also found that City committed multiple breaches of its duties of co-operation and good faith in that it failed to assist the Premier League's four-year investigation, triggered by the emergence of club emails obtained by a hacker. Indeed, City had 'made concerted efforts to stop and frustrate the PL investigation'. Richard Masters, Chief Executive of the Premier League, said: 'The core decision establishes the facts of what happened at Manchester City during this period. It details how the club systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade. 'It also vindicates the Premier League's decision to pursue this case against Manchester City. While the process to date has been both long and difficult, the League has remained determined that the facts be established independently. 'It is a key responsibility of the Premier League to ensure that the Rules, approved by the clubs themselves, are upheld to protect the integrity of the competition. It is paramount that the League remains competitive and fair for all clubs and for the fans. We take that role extremely seriously. 'This disciplinary case, and this decision, are the most significant in Premier League history. There are elements of the case that remain to be decided, including, importantly, what sanction must follow for these breaches. Now we have the Commission's decision, we are committed to moving swiftly through the remainder of the process, to provide certainty for the League, our clubs and fans.' Manchester City have insisted on their innocence throughout the saga (Pep Guardiola pictured with chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak) In a statement released a short time later, City said it was ‘disappointed and surprised’ and referred to the ‘opinion of the Premier League Commission’. It added: ‘The club is innocent of the accusations made by the Premier League and a comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence exists in support of all of its positions, relating to this case. The club will therefore be relentless, and where necessary proactive, in any and all appropriate regulatory and legal forums. ‘The Premier League process remains ongoing, with significant elements uncompleted. Manchester City will now pursue the appeal avenues open to it, on the basis that the opinion contains clear material errors, of law, principle and fact, and is unsafe. ‘The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League Board and Executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence. ‘The club is obviously restricted in what it can say further until all future proceedings are complete.’ City have until Friday to appeal. Man City were first charged with the 115 breaches in February 2023. While that totemic number stuck, the figure – as they subsequently corrected – was actually 130. Of those, 54 were charges of ‘failure to provide accurate and up-to-date financial information’ while there were 14 charges of ‘failure to provide accurate financial reports for player and manager compensation’. Both sets related to alleged offences between 2009 and 2018 (2009-2018), an eight-year period which saw the club win four Premier League titles, the FA Cup, and three League Cup competitions. There were also five charges of ‘failure to comply with UEFA’s regulations, including Financial Fair Play Regulations’ and seven charges of breaching the Premier League’s profit and sustainability regulations (PSR) between 2015 and 2018. There were also 35 counts of failure to co-operate with Premier League investigations between 2018 and 2023. The hearing into the 130 breaches began last September at London’s International Dispute Resolution Centre, with the Premier League sparing no expense and enlisting KCs Adam Lewis and Andrew Hunter to take its case.

Sports.title: Thomas Tuchel admits he has a 'bad conscience' for not checking on England's Man City stars amid guilty verdict on financial 'sham' - and suggests why Jude Bellingham could be his next England captain
Sports.content:
Thomas Tuchel admits he has a 'bad conscience' for not checking on England's Man City stars amid guilty verdict on financial 'sham' - and suggests why Jude Bellingham could be his next England captain

Thomas Tuchel admitted that he regretted not checking in with the Manchester City players in his England squad before kick-off against Czech Republic, just hours after the Premier League confirmed a guilty verdict against the club for serious financial breaches.

Daily Mail Sport reported on Friday that the top-flight side had been found to have committed significant breaches of financial regulations between 2009 and 2018, with the Premier League's official confirmation released alongside a bombshell statement on Tuesday.

But despite the seismic news likely rocking players including starters in Prague Elliot Anderson and Marc Guehi, and Nico O'Reilly, who travelled with the squad, Tuchel revealed after the whistle that the over 115 charges had not been on his mind.

'I have a bad conscience now,' he told BBC Radio 5 Live when asked if he had spoken to Guehi, Anderson, and O'Reilly. 'I did not actually because I am just focused on everything we have to deal with here and to prepare the team.'

Supporters wondered what had captured the attention of Guehi and O'Reilly in particular after they were snapped at the Fortuna Stadium listening to audio on one of their mobile phones.

While it has not been confirmed what the players were listening to - if anything - club chief executive Ferran Soriano released a video shared with the organisation's 1,000-strong staff doubling down on the club's innocence amid a Premier League 'conspiracy theory'.

Thomas Tuchel admitted that he had a 'bad conscience' for focusing solely on England's Nations League tie

His squad contains a number of Man City stars including Marc Guehi and Nico O'Reilly

Premier League CEO Richard Masters claimed Man City's breaches, which included over £900m-worth of 'sham' deals and deliberate attempts to frustrate the league's investigations, showed the club had ‘systematically broken Premier League rules for nearly a decade’.

After the final whistle in Prague, Tuchel also suggested that Jude Bellingham might follow Harry Kane as England's next captain.

Bellingham took the armband when he replaced skipper Kane 20 minutes from the end of last night's 2-0 Nations League win over the Czech Republic in Prague.

Asked afterwards if that was a glimpse into the future, the England manager said: 'If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can for sure be the permanent captain.

'It's a reward. It's good. I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That's what I feel.

'We had a small talk today about his role and said maybe 30 minutes is enough because he hasn't played in this quick turnaround throughout this season.

'He has done it before, but not in this season, so we didn't want to be the first ones to try that.

'But even in this little encounter you can see that he's confident and happy to even help from the bench.'

Tuchel also revealed that Bellingham reported a slight niggle at the end of the game. England play in Croatia on Saturday and then at home to last night's opponent next Tuesday.

'Hopefully it's nothing serious and he's available for selection,' said Tuchel.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury begins drug testing hours before Anthony Joshua face-off
Sports.content:
Tyson Fury begins drug testing hours before Anthony Joshua face-off

Anthony Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn were concerned that Tyson Fury had not been tested ahead of their press conference this evening

View Image Tyson Fury and Anthony Joshua

Tyson Fury was drug tested this morning ahead of his face-off with Anthony Joshua - removing one of the last remaining hurdles to their British super-fight.

‌



Fury and Joshua will face the media this evening for the first time since their fight was officially announced for December 11 in Cardiff. They will then face off officially for the first time in their decade-long rivalry. But despite last week's announcement, there were fears today's event would not take place.

‌



Joshua and promoter Eddie Hearn were adamant Fury should have been drug-tested by VADA seamlessly since his win over Arslanbek Makhmudov. But Fury's team believed he only had to start when his fight with British rival Joshua was announced. Fury enrolled in testing in time for both men to make their way to London from their training camps - and Mirror Fighting understands Fury was woken in his hotel this morning to be tested.

‌



What time is Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury press conference today? READ MORE :

How to buy tickets for Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua fight READ MORE :

This evening's press conference will also go ahead without UFC chief Dana White whose involvement in the fight had caused problems with Hearn and Joshua. White is the frontman for his Zuffa Boxing promotion and Saudi ringmaster Turki Alalshikh wants him to promote the fight.

But Joshua's contract forbids his involvement and he will at least be absent today. "I would have been there if I didn't have The Contender series," he said. Asked why there is confusion over his involvement, White said: "There's no confusion whatsoever. If you look at everything from the network to the guy who's actually f***ing paying for it, and to me saying what I've said. I mean, I've been saying it now, feels like for f***ing years, but it's probably been weeks, but I've been saying the same thing.

Article continues below

"Everything that I've been saying is the truth, and why would I say it and double down, and triple down, and f***ing quadruple down if it wasn't the case? This isn't a hesitation; this is an ego thing; a total ego thing. Boxing has taken a hit in the United States. It's not as big as it was here 20 years ago. It has become a very British sport, and all the s*** you're hearing, and the crying, and the bitching is all coming from the UK."

Sports.title: Dana White explains why he won't be at Fury vs Joshua face-off
Sports.content:
Dana White explains why he won't be at Fury vs Joshua face-off

Fury and Joshua will be present at a press conference in London this evening to ignite the build-up to their seismic heavyweight clash

View Image Dana White won't be flying to London (Image: Zuffa LLC)

Dana White has confirmed he won't attend the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference tonight.

‌



Barring any late developments, the fierce British rivals will be present at a press conference in London to ignite the build-up to their seismic heavyweight clash at Cardiff’s Principality Stadium. Fury and Zuffa Boxing boss White stated over the weekend that the fight was in jeopardy because of an ongoing feud between White and Eddie Hearn of Matchroom Sport, who has been Joshua’s long-standing promoter.

‌



Hearn disputed White’s involvement after the American boss of UFC was officially named as a promoter alongside The Ring, which is owned by Saudi Arabian powerbroker Turki Alalshikh. And while Hearn appears to have got his way, White insists he will only be absent because he was busy with his UFC Contender series.

‌

Anthony Joshua vs Tyson Fury fight date and venue finally announced READ MORE :

"I would have been there if I didn't have The Contender series," he said. Asked why there is confusion over his involvement, White said: "There's no confusion whatsoever. If you look at everything from the network to the guy who's actually f***ing paying for it, and to me saying what I've said. I mean, I've been saying it now, feels like for f***ing years, but it's probably been weeks, but I've been saying the same thing.

"Everything that I've been saying is the truth, and why would I say it and double down, and triple down, and f***ing quadruple down if it wasn't the case? This isn't a hesitation; this is an ego thing; a total ego thing. Boxing has taken a hit in the United States. It's not as big as it was here 20 years ago. It has become a very British sport, and all the s*** you're hearing, and the crying, and the bitching is all coming from the UK."
