World.title: India news: Key opposition leaders meet to discuss poll body row
World.content:
09/30/2026 September 30, 2026 India opposition leaders push back against voter roll review

A meeting of the INDIA bloc, the Congress-led alliance of opposition parties, is underway at the Constitution Club in New Delhi on Wednesday, where opposition leaders are expected to discuss the Election Commission of India's (ECI) Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of voter lists and the furor surrounding India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, that has gripped the nation in recent days.

Mallikarjun Kharge, the president of India's main opposition Congress party, called for the roll back of the SIR, a hotly debated exercise to verify hundreds of millions of Indian voters, that began last year.

Kharge said that the "ballot belongs to the people" and the principle of "one, person, one vote, one value" in Indian democracy was under a "serious threat."

"It is shocking that as many as 13.3 Crore (133 million) voters have blatantly been removed from voter list. Their power to take part in a DEMOCRACY has been snatched. It is ordinary voters who should be deciding who comes to power rather than those who are in power," he said.

Why India's poll body chief is under scrutiny

Wednesday's meeting comes after an investigative report by the Indian Express published last week said that there were differences within the Election Commission of India over decisions related to the SIR.

The report stirred a political storm, with protests calling for the resignation of the poll body's chief, Gyanesh Kumar, for allegedly undermining the ECI's credibility.

According to the Indian Express, Kumar's fellow election commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, raised at least 14 formal objections over 10 months regarding voter registrations, deletions and restorations, as well as control of electoral-roll data, but those concerns were not taken into consideration.

The report said that in one objection, one of the commissioners complained that the ECI acted against the written advice of two commissioners and claimed its action was "unauthorized and illegal."

The ECI has deemed all its decisions lawful, saying that differing views were a routine "part of decision-making."

The three-member commission, comprising Kumar, Sandhu and Joshi, oversees the SIR, which the poll body says removes deceased, relocated and duplicate voters and also prevents the inclusion of "foreign illegal immigrants."

However, opposition parties and critics allege that the exercise has gone beyond that remit and removed millions of eligible voters to the benefit of Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP).

Congress demands CEC Kumar's resignation

On Wednesday, Kharge also called for the removal or resignation of Kumar, saying that there could be no credible election without an "independent and impartial" election body.

He said that the ECI head's "very integrity" and "intentions" were under question.

Last week, Congress carried out demonstrations across the country demanding Kumar's resignation.

Pressure group Cockroach Janata Party (CJP), which claims millions of supporters, said that it would launch nationwide protests on October 2 if Kumar does not step down.

World.title: Germany news: Cabinet approves care reform bill
World.content:
Many women in the Bundeswehr have been victims of sexual offenses Image: Marcus Brandt/dpa/picture alliance

The German armed forces are doing too little to crack down on instances of sexual offenses against women in their ranks, according to public service broadcaster ARD.

This comes as the Bundeswehr is actively seeking to recruit women.

Witnesses and victims of such offenses told the ARD's news magazine REPORT MAINZ that many personnel were scared to report what had happened to them for fear of negative career consequences.

The number of suspected cases of sexual harassment has been rising every year, with 413 reported in 2024 and 472 in 2025, but the number of unreported cases is likely high, according to the ARD.

A spokeswoman from the Defense Ministry told REPORT MAINZ that there had been an "disproportionate rise" in reports of sexual offenses this year.

Women have been permitted to join the Bundeswehr in all capacities for 25 years but still make up just 13.6% of personnel.

The Defense Ministry has, however, rejected the claim by a military historian in the program that the integration of women in the Bundeswehr had so far failed.

Women in the Bundeswehr were "accepted and respected," and there was no "value and rights free space for any group of people" in the German armed forces, it said.

World.title: El Nino is a 'postcard from the future' — and could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths
World.content:
The current El Nino could cause 451,000 excess heat deaths. Researchers warn it offers a glimpse of temperatures that may become normal within 20 years.

Peruvian fishermen gave El Nino its name — "the little boy" or Christ Child — after noticing unusually warm Pacific waters around Christmas that caused the fish they depended on to suddenly become scarce.

But what those fishermen observed locally can have consequences thousands of kilometers away. El Nino can shift temperature and rainfall patterns around the world, bringing extreme heat and drought to some regions and heavy rain and flooding to others.

Researchers now estimate that the unusually high temperatures linked to the current El Nino could cause around 451,000 excess deaths worldwide from June 2026 to February 2027.

The event is a "postcard from the future," Tamma Carleton, head of research at the University of Chicago's Climate Impact Lab, told DW. Land temperatures over the coming months are forecast to run about 1.2 degrees C (2.1 F) above normal.

"For the average person, that's roughly the warming climate change is projected to bring about 20 years from now, arriving all at once," Carleton said.

How does El Nino affect weather worldwide?

Normally, winds blowing west across the Pacific push warm surface water towards Asia and Australia, allowing colder water to rise near South America. During El Nino, which occurs erratically every two to seven years, those winds weaken. Less cold water then rises, and much more of the Pacific stays unusually warm.

The warmer water heats the air above it and fuels rainfall over the central and eastern Pacific. The rising air spreads high in the atmosphere, sending waves that disrupt weather worldwide.

"It is like throwing a stone into a lake," climate researcher Fred Kucharski told DW. "Initially the surface perturbation is local, but then the energy spreads all over the lake through wave propagation."

Kucharski said the effects can cross the tropics within one week and reach higher latitudes in about two. Where the waves travel determines whether a region becomes hotter, cooler, wetter or drier.

The current El Nino developed in June and has strengthened rapidly since. It is now on course to become an exceptionally strong — sometimes called "super" — El Nino.

The Climate Impact Lab says its estimate covers only the first nine months of El Nino, as far as the current seasonal forecasts allow. The event is expected to continue into Northern Hemisphere spring, and its effect on global temperatures could last longer.

"We expect the final number to be meaningfully higher than what we are currently reporting here," Carleton said.

Why can El Nino be so deadly?

The estimate of 451,000 excess deaths covers deaths linked to the direct health effects of unusually high temperatures associated with El Nino.

Extreme heat strains the heart and kidneys, makes it harder for the body to maintain a safe temperature and can worsen cardiovascular, respiratory and other illnesses. As a result, the underlying condition is often recorded as the cause of death rather than the heat that aggravated it.

"Most heat deaths never show up in official statistics as heat deaths," Carleton said.

Could El Nino cause half a million heat-related deaths? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

El Nino can also alter rainfall, contributing to drought in some regions and heavy rain and flooding in others.

Floods can kill, contaminate drinking water and spread disease. Drought can damage harvests and cause water and food shortages.

Deaths from these other indirect effects are not included in the 451,000 projection.

Where will the toll be greatest?

The Climate Impact Lab expects some of the largest increases in deaths in the Sahel, South and Southeast Asia and parts of Latin America. The highest numbers of fatalities are predicted for Nigeria, Sudan, Niger, Chad, India, Indonesia and Brazil.

Many are projected to occur between December and February, meaning much of the expected toll still lies ahead.

"Heat headlines usually focus on Europe and North America," Carleton said. "This event's toll is overwhelmingly in lower-income, already-hot countries, where people have the fewest ways to adapt and where these deaths are least likely to be counted."

Are these lives being significantly shortened?

Some people who die during extreme heat are already frail. This raises an important question: Is the heat cutting their lives substantially short, or merely bringing forward deaths that would have occurred days or weeks later — an effect known as mortality displacement?

What happens when El Nino meets climate change? To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The underlying research uses annual rather than daily death rates, which largely filters out deaths brought forward by only days or weeks.

Ben Armstrong, an emeritus professor at the London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine, said he could not verify the 451,000 figure. But because the estimate is based on annual mortality data, it largely excludes deaths brought forward by only days or weeks. If the figure is correct, he said, most of those counted "would have lived at least six months longer."

Why predict deaths before they happen?

Scientists have long estimated the death toll from extreme temperatures retrospectively. Better seasonal forecasting is increasingly allowing researchers to look ahead instead.

To produce the estimate, researchers used earlier work showing how death rates change during hot weather in different parts of the world. They combined it with seasonal forecasts showing how hot each place is expected to become.

El Nino, regional wars fuel global food crisis To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"Putting the two together lets us estimate the human cost of this event while there's still time to do something about it, rather than counting the deaths after the fact," Carleton said.

Heat warnings, cooling centers and hydration stations, home visits to vulnerable people, protections for outdoor workers and additional health care capacity could all reduce mortality.

The researchers believe targeted interventions could save tens of thousands of lives.

For Carleton, the forecast is a warning to prepare now for the heat that climate change could make commonplace.

"This El Nino gives us a look at future weather in the 2040s," Carleton said. "These temperatures will become normal in 20 years, giving us time and reason to begin investing in adaptive capacity now."

Edited: Carla Bleiker

World.title: El casero tendrá que indemnizar con 12 mensualidades al inquilino si decide no renovar el alquiler
World.content:
El segundo decreto de vivienda, que incluye una extensión indefinida de todos los contratos de alquiler y que el Gobierno prevé publicar este jueves en el BOE, obligará al casero a indemnizar con al menos 12 mensualidades de renta al inquilino si decide romper la relación. El texto, al que ha tenido acceso este diario, incorpora el nuevo régimen de renovación automática de los arrendamientos y permite al propietario romper con el contrato al vencimiento de cada plazo, de cinco o siete años en función de si es una persona física o jurídica. Sin embargo, el texto establece una compensación económica, equivalente a una renta anual, si el arrendador no alega alguna de las causas justificadas recogidas en el decreto.

Todo parte de la modificación del artículo 10 de la Ley de Arrendamientos Urbanos (LAU). El cambio establece que, una vez cumplido el periodo mínimo obligatorio ―cinco años cuando el arrendador es un particular y dos más cuando es una empresa―, el contrato se prorrogará por periodos sucesivos de la misma duración si ninguna de las partes transmite su voluntad de no renovarlo. En caso de querer finalizar el contrato, el propietario deberá comunicarlo con al menos seis meses de antelación, frente a los dos meses del inquilino.

Si el arrendador decide no renovar, no tendrá que alegar ningún motivo concreto para hacerlo siempre que abone la indemnización. La compensación será de al menos 12 mensualidades de la renta correspondiente a una vivienda de características análogas, calculada conforme al sistema estatal de referencia de precios de alquiler, y no podrá ser inferior a una mensualidad por cada año que el inquilino haya permanecido en la vivienda.

La norma contempla determinados supuestos en los que el propietario podrá evitar el pago de esta contrapartida. Entre ellos figuran la necesidad de la vivienda para el propio arrendador, su cónyuge o familiares de hasta segundo grado; que el inquilino no habite efectivamente la casa durante más de seis meses al año sin causa justificada; que disponga de otra residencia apta en el mismo municipio; o que se formalice un nuevo contrato de cinco o siete años a precio regulado. También se contempla la situación de vulnerabilidad acreditada del arrendador. Estas causas deberán quedar justificadas en la comunicación de no renovación.

El Gobierno ha pospuesto un día la publicación en el Boletín Oficial del Estado del decreto que incorpora esta prórroga automática, uno de los puntos más calientes de la negociación y una de las principales exigencias que el Sindicato de Inquilinas reclama desde la acampada de la Puerta del Sol en Madrid. El Ejecutivo, no obstante, explica que la decisión se debe únicamente a motivos técnicos y jurídicos, ya que el texto está ya redactado.

El Consejo de Ministros de este martes se retrasó más de una hora y forzó una negociación contra reloj para que el paquete de vivienda incluyera, de alguna manera, la extensión indefinida de los contratos. El Gobierno, escudándose en que no había tenido tiempo de negociar un punto tan ambicioso con los socios de la investidura de los que depende la posterior convalidación ―en referencia a Junts y PNV―, decidió trocear el decreto en dos e incluir esta extensión automática en una segunda orden.

La razón del retraso de la publicación es eminentemente jurídica. Ambos textos están conectados y la segunda norma modifica un artículo de la primera. El primer decreto establece una renovación de los contratos de alquiler de hasta dos años que puede solicitar el inquilino y a la que el casero está obligado ―con algunas excepciones―, mientras que el segundo introduce la prórroga automática. Por ello, insisten en el Gobierno, no tendría sentido que la segunda norma modificase una disposición que todavía no ha entrado en vigor al no haberse publicado previamente en el BOE.

La idea del Gobierno es que el Congreso vote por separado la convalidación de los dos textos el viernes, en un pleno extraordinario, aprovechando además el creciente respaldo de la calle a las protestas para presionar a los socios más escépticos. El martes, tras conocer la fórmula ideada por la coalición, Valeria Racu y Alicia del Río, portavoces del Sindicato de Inquilinas de Madrid, cargaron contra la decisión de haber troceado los decretos, algo que, aseguran, abre la puerta a que el segundo sea rechazado.

La diferencia entre una prórroga limitada a dos años y un sistema de renovación automática de los contratos ha concentrado buena parte de la discusión durante las negociaciones que se precipitaron tras el desahucio de Maricarmen a manos de Urbagestión. El Sindicato de Inquilinas, que capitanea las movilizaciones y mantiene la presión desde el centro de Madrid, reclama contratos indefinidos en los que el inquilino pueda continuar en la vivienda mientras cumpla con los pagos y no concurra una causa justificada y acreditada para poner fin al arrendamiento. Sumar y el resto de las formaciones de izquierdas incorporaron esa reivindicación en las negociaciones, mientras que el PSOE trató de hacer encaje de bolillos para no perder el apoyo de PNV y Junts, con otras prioridades en materia de vivienda.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Humanizar la educación ‘online’, o por qué los docentes son más importantes que nunca
World.content:
La formación virtual pivota sobre el profesorado para lograr una mayor oferta de recursos, exprimir las posibilidades de las plataformas y estimular la interacción y la autonomía del alumno

Cuando se habla de educación online, la atención se bifurca habitualmente en dos direcciones íntimamente relacionadas: hacia las posibilidades de la plataforma digital educativa y hacia las posibles dificultades que el alumno afrontará a lo largo de su aprendizaje, desde mantener la atención hasta la frialdad de aprender sin estar rodeado físicamente de otras personas. Sin embargo, todas estas cuestiones dependen, en gran medida, de la capacidad del profesorado en conseguir que la experiencia, de principio a fin, se humanice lo suficiente como para no echar de menos la presencialidad continuada.

Y esa humanización pasa, desde el principio, por intentar que el alumno no se sienta solo ante el contenido. Hay formas: con tutorías telefónicas, videollamadas, mensajes de voz, vídeos personalizados, clases en directo... Como explica la docente Ana Belén Salinas, en esas conversaciones se estrecha la relación y, “de ese modo, conoces a los alumnos un poco más, sabes de dónde partes y cómo puedes ayudarles”.

Ana Belén Salinas, psicopedagoga y profesora en el grupo tecnológico-educativo Educa Edtech. Mónica Martínez Aguilar

Para establecer ese vínculo, el docente tiene que hacer un esfuerzo mucho mayor que en un aula presencial, reconoce Salinas. De hecho, su inteligencia emocional y su empatía son fundamentales para transformar una plataforma en un espacio seguro de aprendizaje. Así lo afirma Ramón Sánchez, compañero de Salinas en el grupo tecnológico-educativo Educa Edtech: “Damos un toque humano y real. Si no, es muy difícil convencer al alumno de la autoridad de los conocimientos”.

Los grandes retos para el docente

Salinas es psicopedagoga y profesora e imparte formaciones relacionadas precisamente con la docencia. Esta granadina de 47 años comenzó en el oficio hace 21, cuando la educación a distancia consistía en enviar por correo libros físicos y cuestionarios que el alumno devolvía por sobre franqueado. “Yo no llevaba portátil a la facultad, vengo de un mundo analógico”, recuerda.

Hoy, es ella la primera que debe seguir aprendiendo para adaptarse a la tecnología que luego servirá para la educación online. Su adaptación pasa por distintas formaciones pero, también, por lo que ha absorbido de compañeros “mucho más jóvenes que nacieron en la época tecnológica”, asevera. “No queda otra: la gente trabaja, tiene que conciliar y quiere seguir aprendiendo. Las clases online son una buena opción y, por suerte, los docentes podemos actualizarnos”.

No todos lo ven así: la resistencia de los docentes al cambio es uno de los principales desafíos en España a los que se enfrentan las instituciones que quieren ofrecer una formación online de calidad, según se puede ver en el siguiente gráfico.

Desafíos de las instituciones educativas para ofrecer formación 'online' de calidad

Una vez que el docente se adecúa al formato y a las plataformas, es él quien debe adaptar las clases a partir de lo aprendido. Y el principal error es pensar que esto consiste simplemente en trasladarlo a la pantalla, como indica Andrea Carolina Rojas, pedagoga infantil y docente en Educa Edtech. “Dar clases en línea tiene su propia metodología: no basta con grabarla o con subir unos contenidos”. Para Rojas, se deben diseñar experiencias de aprendizaje adecuadas para el entorno digital: “Es importante utilizar un lenguaje cercano, facilitar espacios de interacción, dar una retroalimentación personalizada y mostrar disponibilidad para orientar al estudiante”, recomienda.

Andrea Carolina Rojas, pedagoga infantil y docente en Educa Edtech. Mónica Martínez Aguilar

Por toda esta mano humana, insiste en que la tecnología no puede sustituir a un docente: “Al contrario, se valorará todavía más aquello que aporta el profesional, como su capacidad para interpretar contextos, acompañar y tomar decisiones pedagógicas”.

Consejos para aprender ‘online’

Aunque sus virtudes son la flexibilidad, el alumno tiene que conseguir ser constante y continuar motivado para aprovechar al máximo este tipo de formación. Sánchez, docente en la Facultad de Actividad Física y Deporte de la misma institución, ofrece una serie de pautas fundamentales. La primera es crear un horario: “Tienen que organizar qué tiempos tienen disponibles para el aprendizaje y que sean innegociables”. El espacio también ha de ser adecuado, sobre todo, libre de distracciones.

Para facilitar la adherencia a la formación, el alumno debe implicarse y utilizar todas las herramientas a su alcance. Los docentes insisten en que no debe ser un ejercicio pasivo; no se puede considerar que ha habido un aprendizaje real si un alumno se limita a pasar páginas o liquidar un curso en un fin de semana. Requiere tiempo de maduración y reflexión. Además, Sánchez subraya como fundamental que encuentren una vía para aplicar lo teórico en el ámbito práctico o profesional.

Ramón Sánchez, docente en la facultad de Actividad Física y Deporte en Educa Edtech. Mónica Martínez Aguilar

Por último, la comunicación directa: no estancarse ante dudas complejas y utilizar el contacto con el docente para recibir pautas claras que permitan seguir avanzando. “La clave es ese contacto humano, esa capacidad de tranquilizar, de alumbrar los conocimientos”, reflexiona Sánchez. Los docentes de Educa Edtech también se relacionan entre sí. Desarrollan su trabajo en el Edificio Educa Edtech, en Granada, equipados con micrófonos y auriculares. En ese mismo espacio cuentan con cabinas insonorizadas, y es allí donde se recluyen cuando deben impartir una masterclass o realizar una videollamada.

Lo que las empresas valoran

La formación virtual es una alternativa ideal para todo tipo de personas y profesionales, explica Elísabeth San Juan, quien cuenta con más de seis años de experiencia en el área de Business tutorizando formaciones de Recursos Humanos y gestión del talento de Educa Edtech. Sobre todo, para profesionales en activo que necesitan conciliar la vida laboral y personal, para personas que no tienen un acceso fácil a los centros educativos o para quienes quieran libertad. “Son los propios alumnos quienes marcan su ritmo de estudio, adaptando y ajustando el aprendizaje a sus verdaderos intereses”, describe San Juan.

A su vez, responde a una demanda de los empleadores. “Hoy en día las empresas buscan perfiles interesados en aprender de forma continua”, señala esta experta: “Haber realizado formación online demuestra autodisciplina, buena gestión del tiempo, autonomía y competencias digitales, que son cualidades clave en el mercado laboral actual”, insiste. Porque algunas compañías, una vez que el candidato es contratado, implementan itinerarios formativos online que permiten a sus empleados la escalabilidad del aprendizaje y la actualización inmediata de competencias.

“Cursar una formación ‘online’ demuestra autodisciplina, buena gestión del tiempo, autonomía y competencias digitales, cualidades clave en el mercado laboral actual” Elísabeth San Juan Docente en la Facultad de Recursos Humanos en Educa Edtech

Por todo, la formación online no debe entenderse como una alternativa de menor valor a la presencial, como señala Rojas: “Se trata de una modalidad con unas posibilidades propias que, cuando está bien diseñada y acompañada, puede ofrecer una experiencia educativa de gran calidad”.

World.title: ‘Larry’, un viajero más rumbo a Barcelona
World.content:
Una mezcla de ternura y curiosidad: esto es lo que despierta la presencia de un perro grande en un tren de Iryo

Parece que nadie nos esperaba aquí. Por las miradas que acaparamos, por los dedos que nos señalan, diría que este jueves de mediados de septiembre nos hemos convertido en la gran atracción de la zona de embarque para la alta velocidad en la estación de Atocha de Madrid: el periodista que escribe estas líneas y un simpático labrador mestizo. “¿Harry?”, pregunta un grupo de aficionados futboleros, interesándose por el nombre de mi acompañante. “No, Larry como Larry David, el cómico”, respondo. “¡He is so cuuuute! (¡Es tan mono!)”, exclama en inglés una niña rubísima, de ojos azules, alucinada con la textura aterciopelada de sus orejas.

¿Se convierte uno en el centro de atención cuando viaja acompañado de una mascota? A priori, mientras esperamos el tren de Iryo con destino Barcelona, constato que el desplazamiento está diseñado para que entorpezcamos lo menos posible, para que no molestemos a los otros pasajeros. Con este propósito entiendo que nos han asignado billetes en una última fila, los dos solos, sin asientos a nuestra izquierda, y también por este motivo nos han ubicado ahora junto a dos familias con bebés para embarcar por separado.

‘Larry’, un perro viajero Edad 7 años Raza Mezcla de labrador con una raza indeterminada Aficiones La comida, sea la que sea, a la hora que sea; los paseos por la Casa de Campo de Madrid; robar pelotas a los otros perros; echarse panza arriba para que le acaricien el pecho. Viajes El de septiembre de 2026 fue el primero de Larry en tren por España; antes, ya había cruzado varias veces Francia en ferrocarril y alcanzado las costas italianas en barco. Su primer viaje fue en 2019, en un coche que le llevó desde Sevilla, donde fue rescatado, hasta Tarragona, en las instalaciones de la protectora SOS Golden.

Pero el magnetismo de Larry –¿será suyo en particular?, ¿será el de los perros en general?– desvanece cualquier barrera entre nosotros y el resto de los viajeros: aún estamos esperando para bajar al andén número cuatro y ya he perdido la cuenta de las veces que se han acercado a pedir si podían acariciarlo, que le han llamado guapo o que sencillamente se han quedado observándolo desde la distancia, con ternura o con curiosidad.

El asombro de algunos rostros me dice que pocos intuyen que este será el viaje número 3.835 de un perro de más de 10 kilos a bordo de uno de los trenes de Iryo, como detalla Javier Abadía, su director comercial. La compañía siempre permitió llevar a perros pequeños, gatos y hurones en trasportín y empezó a admitir a perros grandes en el verano de 2024. Una decisión en consonancia con el signo de los tiempos, cuando en ciudades como Madrid ya hay más canes censados (cerca de 310.000) que niños de hasta nueve años (unos 267.000), según los últimos datos del ayuntamiento de la capital y del Instituto Nacional de Estadística (INE).

Guía para viajar en Iryo con un perro de más de 10 kilos Consulte la disponibilidad Los perros de más de 10 kilos pueden viajar en los trenes que tienen como origen las estaciones de Madrid Puerta de Atocha-Almudena Grandes y Madrid Chamartín-Clara Campoamor, Barcelona-Sants, Valencia-Joaquín Sorolla, Sevilla-Santa Justa, Málaga-María Zambrano, Córdoba-Julio Anguita y Zaragoza-Delicias. Además, debe tener en cuenta que no se permite viajar con un perro de menos de un año, con una perra en celo o un perro de raza potencialmente peligrosa de acuerdo con la normativa vigente. Gestione la reserva La reserva del billete del animal se debe gestionar siempre por teléfono con el Servicio de Atención al Cliente, en el 910 150 000. El billete tiene un coste de 40 euros y lo puede comprar a través de la web de Iryo o a través del Servicio de Atención al Cliente, en el que le informarán de la disponibilidad de plazas para viajar con su mascota: solo hay dos plazas para perro grande en cada tren. Prepare la documentación y la bolsa de viaje Para poder viajar necesita rellenar y firmar una declaración responsable (lo puede descargar en este enlace), disponer de un seguro de mascotas vigente y llevar la cartilla de vacunación actualizada. Por otro lado, también deberá llevar utensilios de limpieza (bolsitas, toallitas higiénicas y espray desinfectante y anti-olor). Acuda a la estación con tiempo El día del viaje deberá ir a la oficina de Iryo de la estación una hora y media antes de la hora de salida y presentar la documentación anteriormente mencionada. La compañía pide que el pasajero y el perro sean los últimos en realizar el embarque. Por contra, serán los primeros en bajar del tren a la llegada al destino.

“El valor de nuestra propuesta reside en nuestra capacidad para adaptarnos a las necesidades de cada uno de nuestros clientes”, incide Abadía. “Para quienes comparten su día a día con una mascota, estas son compañeras de vida, y por ello consideramos esencial facilitar la posibilidad de trasladarse de forma sencilla junto a ellas”.

Una plaza propia para el animal por 40 euros

La logística del trayecto ha consistido en una llamada telefónica para reservar una plaza para el animal, con un coste de 40 euros, y en avanzar un poco la salida de casa. La compañía pide llegar a la estación con una hora y media de antelación para revisar la documentación del animal y presentar una declaración responsable. Y luego, una vez pasado el control de equipajes, aplica un protocolo de reminiscencias bíblicas: los viajeros con mascotas serán los últimos en subir al convoy para luego ser los primeros en bajar.

Instalados ya en los asientos 19C y 19D del sexto coche, y equipados con una funda protectora para la butaca y una alfombrilla para el suelo que nos han entregado, Larry se acomoda para comenzar un viaje que pasa en gran medida echado debajo del asiento. Dormita, a veces cambia de postura, cruzando las piernas con elegancia, sin darse cuenta de que sigue maravillando a los pasajeros que van y vienen. “¿Cuántos años tiene?”, “¿De qué raza es?”.

¿Qué otros animales pueden viajar con Iryo? Además de perros, grandes o pequeños, también pueden viajar gatos y hurones con un coste adicional de 10 euros. Estos dos últimos, junto con los perros de menos de 10 kilos, deben viajar en un transportín que no supere las medidas de 60x35x35 cm. Todas las mascotas tendrán que ir identificadas con su chip correspondiente y debidamente documentadas, además de estar vacunadas y desparasitadas según la normativa de origen y destino del viaje. El transporte de la mascota tendrá un coste adicional y deberá contratarse de manera previa al viaje.

Estas son las preguntas que voy respondiendo a medida que avanzamos hacia Barcelona, interrumpiendo a ratos la lectura de Sobre la muerte de un perro (Periférica). Un texto de los años cincuenta en el que el filósofo francés Jean Grenier, entre otras cosas, narra algunos episodios de sus periplos por Europa a bordo de barcos, trenes, taxis y góndolas venecianas junto a su mascota y en el que se queja de las “prohibiciones” y la falta de espacio que sufre Taïaut, quien muchas veces “no sabía dónde meterse”.

Con el tren a punto de llegar a la estación de Sants cierro el libro y pienso, observando la respiración calmada de Larry a mis pies, que Grenier ya no podría volver a escribir este lamento: “¡Qué difíciles los viajes con perros!”.

World.title: He pagado una derrama de 5.000 euros para arreglar las filtraciones, pero la comunidad no inicia las obras. ¿Cómo reclamo?
World.content:
Pregunta. Tengo un inmueble en Tacoronte (Tenerife), donde residen mi hija y su familia. El edificio, dada su antigüedad y proximidad al mar, presenta serios problemas de revestimiento, filtraciones y riesgo de daños estructurales. Mi apartamento, en particular, padece filtraciones y humedades. La junta de propietarios aprobó una derrama destinada a financiar las obras y los honorarios profesionales. Hasta la fecha, he abonado una cantidad superior a 5.000 euros. Sin embargo, los trabajos aún no se han iniciado y ni el presidente ni la administración del edificio responden a mis correos o mensajes. ¿Qué pasos legales debo seguir para reclamar la ejecución de las obras o la solución a esta problemática? A. Gómez

Respuesta. Según el artículo 10.1.a) de la Ley 49/1960, de 21 de julio, de Propiedad Horizontal, la comunidad de propietarios está obligada a realizar las obras y actuaciones necesarias para el adecuado mantenimiento y conservación de los elementos comunes del edificio.

El hecho de que la presidencia y la administración de la finca no hayan llevado a cabo ninguna actuación, pese a haber aprobado y recaudado una derrama superior a 5.000 euros, supone un incumplimiento de las obligaciones inherentes a sus cargos dentro de la comunidad. En particular, la falta de gestión y ejecución de los acuerdos adoptados resulta contraria al artículo 20.1.c) de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, que impone al administrador la obligación de velar por la conservación de la finca.

Dado que sus comunicaciones informales no han obtenido respuesta, el siguiente paso sería enviar un burofax con acuse de recibo y certificación de contenido dirigido tanto al presidente como al administrador. En dicho escrito, puede concederles un plazo de diez días para que inicien las gestiones necesarias para ejecutar las obras o acrediten que ya han contratado los trabajos de reparación, indicando la fecha prevista de inicio, advirtiéndoles de que, en caso contrario, se ejercitarán las acciones legales oportunas.

Si transcurrido ese plazo continúan sin actuar, se podrá interponer una demanda por la vía civil solicitando al juez que requiera a la comunidad, representada por su presidente conforme al artículo 13.3 de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, para que ejecute de forma inmediata las obras previamente aprobadas.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Porto Ercole, el pueblo de Italia donde la ‘dolce vita’ sigue mirando al mar
World.content:
Entre barcos de madera, terrazas frente al puerto y hoteles que forman parte de la historia del Mediterráneo y de la visión del fotógrafo Slim Aarons, en este enclave al sur de la Toscana la vida cotidiana sigue marcando el ritmo

Cuando llega la última hora de la tarde, la italiana Porto Ercole recupera su mejor versión. Los barcos regresan al puerto, las terrazas se llenan lentamente y la luz suaviza las fachadas de color ocre que trepan por la colina. Una Vespa atraviesa el paseo. Alguien recoge la ropa del balcón. Los camareros se mueven entre las mesas cuando llega la hora del aperitivo. En realidad nada parece extraordinario, y ahí está parte del encanto de este enclave en la costa del Argentario. La escena podría repetirse hoy o dentro de una década.

Este es uno de los lugares a los que la gente regresa. Las familias romanas que llevan generaciones pasando los veranos aquí. Los navegantes que conocen cada cala y quienes buscan un Mediterráneo que conserva su ritmo. Argentario no se parece demasiado a la Toscana que se suele imaginar. En vez de los campos infinitos de cipreses, aquí aparecen pinares que descienden hacia el mar y acantilados esculpidos por el viento.

Una callejuela en el casco antiguo de Porto Ercole. Atlantide Phototravel / GETTY IMAGES

Apenas a una hora y media en coche desde el aeropuerto de Roma (o en tren hasta Orbetello-Monte Argentario, a 10 kilómetros del pueblo), y a poco más de dos horas desde Pisa, los casi 3.000 vecinos de Porto Ercole han conseguido preservar algo cada vez más difícil de encontrar en el Mediterráneo: la sensación de estar en un lugar donde la vida cotidiana parece seguir marcando el ritmo.

Antes de que llegara Instagram, el fotógrafo estadounidense Slim Aarons (1916-2006) convirtió esta costa en uno de sus escenarios favoritos. Sus fotografías ayudaron a construir el imaginario de la dolce vita, retratando comidas interminables, barcos de madera, piscinas frente al mar y una elegancia que parecía surgir sin esfuerzo. Por delante de su cámara pasaron Gianni Agnelli, Lee Radziwill, los Getty o la familia Missoni… y muchas de aquellas escenas inmortalizadas siguen pareciendo posibles.

El encantador pueblo de Porto Ercole se encuentra en la costa del Argentario. Roberto Nencini ( GETTY IMAGES )

Las mañanas transcurren despacio en Porto Ercole; hay quienes comienzan el día con un expresso mirando al mar y los que prefieren perderse por las calles que rodean el puerto, donde se suceden pequeñas boutiques. Fue en una de esas tiendas donde empecé a entender mejor el pueblo. Había llegado la noche anterior y, después de descubrir que durante las noches aquí a veces corre un poco de fresco (aunque durante el verano son muy calientes, con temperaturas que suelen rondar los 30 grados de día y 25 grados de noche o más), entré en Ester Gi en busca de una capa ligera. Mientras me la probaba, Ornella, la encargada, empezó a hablar de Porto Ercole como solo hablan los italianos de los lugares que quieren. La Sirena para cenar pescado. O la Hosteria Alicina. O Il Gambero Rosso. Una recomendación llevaba a la siguiente y, antes de darme cuenta, ya no hablábamos de restaurantes, sino del pueblo. Ornella lo conoce bien, porque durante 14 años trabajó en la boutique del Hotel Il Pellicano y ha visto pasar generaciones de familias que repiten cada temporada. “Es como una pequeña joya”, dice al hablar del pueblo. “La gente vuelve porque aquí se sienten como en casa”.

Escuchándola, es fácil entender por qué, tarde o temprano, cualquier conversación sobre Porto Ercole acaba desembocando en el hotel Il Pellicano. “En realidad, toda su historia es una historia de amor”, explica. Y es difícil encontrar una mejor prueba de ello. Patricia Daszel, una socialité estadounidense, quedó fascinada por el piloto británico de guerra Michael Graham después de verlo fotografiado en un periódico como superviviente de un accidente aéreo. Años después se conocieron en Pelican Point, en California, se enamoraron y encontraron en unos terrenos de la familia Borghese, suspendidos sobre una cala de aguas cristalinas de Argentario, el lugar perfecto para construir una casa e invitar a sus amigos. Aquella residencia acabaría convirtiéndose en el hotel, que inauguraron en 1965.

Vista aérea del hotel Il Pellicano, en Porto Ercole. Pellicano Hotels

Ahora, 60 años después, Il Pellicano parece haber conservado una manera de entender el verano. Una buena parte de las fotografías más conocidas de Slim Aarons se tomaron aquí. El embarcadero, las plataformas junto al mar y las icónicas toallas de rayas amarillas y blancas siguen formando parte del paisaje. También la forma de vivirlo: un baño antes de comer, una sobremesa que se alarga y, al caer la tarde, el Bar Roberto, donde Federico Morosi lleva 18 años detrás de la barra.

La familia Sciò ha sido clave para conservar el carácter del alojamiento. Roberto Sciò llegó primero como huésped, se enamoró del lugar y lo hizo suyo en 1979. Desde entonces, el hotel ha mantenido esa combinación de elegancia relajada y discreción, hoy bajo la dirección de su hija Marie-Louise, y que también se percibe en La Posta Vecchia, la histórica propiedad familiar cerca de Roma.

Terraza junto al Mediterráneo de Il Pellicano. Pellicano Hotels

El espíritu de Il Pelicano también se percibe fuera del hotel. Ornella me insistió varias veces en que pasara por Medusa a la hora del aperitivo, un pequeño local abierto por Stefano y Alin, dos antiguos miembros del equipo que decidieron emprender su propio proyecto. Pedí una bruschetta de tomate y mozzarella mientras observaba la escena. Solo se escuchaba hablar italiano y sentí nostalgia de ese Mediterráneo de antes, con más veraneantes que turistas.

Cuando le pregunté a Ornella qué explicaba mejor Porto Ercole, no mencionó los hoteles ni los famosos. Habló de quienes crecieron veraneando aquí y siguen regresando cada año. Aunque esa fidelidad de la que hablaba no ha impedido que el pueblo empiece a escribir un nuevo capítulo. LA ROQQA es probablemente el mejor ejemplo. Inaugurado en 2023, hacía años que la apertura de un hotel no generaba tanta conversación en el pueblo. Mientras que Il Pellicano está más escondido sobre el acantilado, aquí el hotel forma parte de la vida cotidiana. Al cruzar la puerta, una puede mezclarse con las calles del centro o improvisar un aperitivo antes de regresar. Desde la entrada, donde suele descansar un pequeño Fiat descapotable que parece sacado de una fotografía de los años sesenta, LA ROQQA deja clara su personalidad. El interiorismo combina referencias retro, diseño contemporáneo y una paleta inspirada en los colores del puerto.

La mejor hora para subir a su rooftop Scirocco quizá no sea la cena, sino ese momento previo en el que el sol empieza a caer sobre Porto Ercole y el puerto cambia de color. La barra rinde homenaje a Caravaggio, con creaciones inspiradas en algunas de sus obras más célebres y reinterpretaciones del clásico Negroni. En la cocina también manda el producto local. Pescados del Tirreno, pasta fresca preparada a mano, verduras de temporada y vinos de la Toscana dan forma a la carta. Uno de los platos preferidos de la casa es su spaghetto otto pomodori, preparado con distintas variedades de tomate cultivadas en los alrededores de Porto Ercole.

La terraza Scirocco del hotel LA ROQQA, en Porto Ercole.

Explorando los alrededores

Quienes tienen algunos días más encuentran motivos de sobra para seguir explorando Argentario. A pocos minutos a pie desde Porto Ercole está la cala Le Viste. Hacia el norte, La Feniglia es una playa de arena bordeada por un pinar protegido perfecta para pasar la mañana, mientras que Spiaggia Lunga es más tranquila y salvaje.

Vista de la playa de La Feniglia. Andrea Pistolesi ( GETTY IMAGES )

La historia aparece donde menos se la espera. En Forte Filippo, fortaleza que los españoles levantaron en el siglo XVI para proteger la ruta marítima entre sus territorios italianos, y que sigue dominando la bahía a lo alto de las colinas. O en el último viaje de Caravaggio, que pasó aquí sus últimos días y murió en 1610 mientras intentaba regresar a Roma. A pocos kilómetros, Porto Santo Stefano es el punto de partida de los ferris hacia las islas de Giglio y Giannutri. Están integradas en el parque nacional del Archipiélago Toscano, el mayor parque marino protegido de Europa.

Porto Ercole conserva algo que resulta cada vez más difícil de encontrar, porque aquí las tardes siguen midiendo el tiempo en baños, aperitivos y conversaciones que se alargan sin mirar el reloj. Quizá por eso la dolce vita, más que una promesa, sigue pareciendo una forma de vivir.

World.title: Most major Dutch data centres keep energy usage secret: report
World.content:
Most data centres in the Netherlands do not make their environmental impact public, which conceals water and electricity usage, according to an investigation by Trouw and Lighthouse Reports.

The Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), which collects data on behalf of the EU, lists only 104 data centres but the industry body Dutch Datacenter Association (DDA) says there were 186 commercial data centres at the end of 2025.

These figures cover data centres with at least 500 kW of installed IT capacity, which are required to report their energy and water use, among other things, under the EU’s Energy Efficiency Directive.

The RVO’s list is missing almost half the centres counted by the DDA, and that count does not include the many data centres run in-house by banks, hospitals and other companies. Trouw estimates that public data is available for only around a quarter of large data centres.

Dutch data centre energy

Data centres used 5.1 billion kWh of electricity in 2024, or 4.6% of the national total, according to statistics from CBS – a 37% rise on 2021. Figures for 2025 are not yet available.

RVO figures published this summer showed that Microsoft’s largest Dutch data centre alone uses 1% of national electricity, though the power is said to come from renewable sources. Google, which runs two large data centres in the Netherlands, does not publish its figures.

Grid operator TenneT expects data centres to account for 10% to 15% of Dutch electricity use by 2030. Water use is lower, at an estimated 0.1% of the national total.

Aarhus Convention

Reporters working with Lighthouse Reports spent a year filing freedom of information requests in all 27 EU member states and with the European Commission. Most were refused, with some countries saying they did not have the data, and others citing commercial confidentiality.

The group has now filed a complaint under the Aarhus Convention, a treaty signed by the EU and all its member states that guarantees public access to environmental information. The complaint is before the convention’s compliance committee, which meets four times a year.

Lighthouse Reports says the Netherlands discloses more than most other EU countries, where reporters met what they called a “wall of silence”.

World.title: Two more suspects arrested in Overasselt shooting inquiry
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Two men have been arrested in Amsterdam during the investigation into a fatal shooting at a farmhouse in Gelderland.

Police said they had also recovered guns, including an automatic weapon, during searches of houses in the capital, Diemen and Hoofddorp on Tuesday.

A group of armed men descended on the small village of Overasselt in the early hours of September 1 and opened fire on a farmhouse, killing a security guard and injuring two police officers.

The man living in the house, 28-year-old Jan G., was arrested in Germany two weeks ago on suspicion of trying to smuggle cocaine through the port of Dunkirk.

He is believed to have been targeted as retribution for a stolen drugs shipment, according to a video that police obtained in the days afterwards.

Bolle Jos

The Telegraaf reported that the 1,283kg shipment belonged to “Bolle Jos” Leijdekkers, Europe’s most wanted criminal, who is believed to be living in Sierra Leone.

The arrest of the two suspects, aged 24 and 25, takes the total number of arrests to 36. Most of the others have appeared in court charged with murder or manslaughter.

Two of the suspects are minors aged 16 and 17, the rest are men from France, Netherlands, Algeria, Libya, Belgium and Ukraine – all aged between 18 and 32.

A third man, aged 19, was arrested at one of the houses raided by police. His connection to the gang is being investigated.

World.title: Education cuts loom if talks with unions on welfare reforms fail
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The education budget could be cut by €1.2 billion if talks to reform social security fail to deliver enough savings, according to documents seen by NOS.

The coalition parties have agreed to scrap €6.5 billion of welfare cuts in order to get the support they need from the opposition for next year’s budget.

Some of the gap has been plugged by raising more from savers and investors, but the cabinet expects to be left with a €3 billion shortfall.

Prime minister Rob Jetten and finance minister Eelco Heinen are due to meet trade unions to discuss cost-saving reforms to the long-term sickness benefit WIA. “If the savings are less than we expect, the cabinet will identify additional measures,” Jetten said.

As a last resort the government could save €1.2 billion by not raising the education department’s budget in line with inflation, which would force it to make savings.

The move would be unpopular with Jetten’s own party D66, which campaigned to reverse the previous cabinet’s €2 billion cuts package and sees higher education as one of its flagship policy areas.

NOS reported that the prospect of having to make cuts in education was intended to put pressure on D66’s base to demand concessions from trade unions on social security.

Parliament is due to begin a two-day debate on the detailed budget plans on Wednesday.

World.title: Rail union demands action on violence against train staff
World.content:
Violence against train staff is getting out of control, rail union VVMC has said in a call to politicians. The union says conductors and other employees of national rail company NS are increasingly being assaulted, threatened, and spat at by passengers.

In a letter reported by NOS, the union cites NS figures showing that reports of aggression and violence against staff more than doubled from 2,672 in 2023 to 6,442 in 2025. According to those figures, there have been 5,088 reports so far this year, including 1,368 involving physical violence and 105 threats with a weapon.

“These are no longer unpleasant situations,” the union wrote, according to NOS. “These are serious incidents of violence against people carrying out their public duty.”

The letter lists several recent attacks. In February, a conductor at Rotterdam Blaak station was beaten unconscious. The same happened to a conductor at Den Dolder station 6 months later.

On August 6, several NS staff and police officers were injured during the arrest of an aggressive passenger at Almere Centrum station. According to the union, one NS employee lost part of his thumb after being bitten, and a colleague suffered a broken wrist and torn tendons.

Lost powers

The union also complained that senior conductors lost their enforcement powers in 2022. Since then, they can no longer write up offenders themselves or check personal details in the national population register.

Senior conductors were given bodycams this year, but the union says that does not make up for the powers they lost.

A VVMC spokesperson told news agency ANP that the union wants more NS security and service staff on trains.

“Politicians can no longer make do with stating that aggression is unacceptable. Action is needed now,” the letter says, according to NOS.

Licence register

The letter follows the cabinet’s announcement on Tuesday that public transport enforcement officers will get access to the driving licence register. From Thursday, employers can apply to vehicle authority RDW for access.

Officers will then be able to use licence photos to identify fare dodgers and troublemakers who carry no ID, instead of waiting for the police.

World.title: Peak birthday season: more NL celebrations today than any other
World.content:
More people in the Netherlands are celebrating their birthday on Wednesday than on any other day of the year, with some 44,000 sharing September 30, according to national statistics office CBS.

On average, 41,000 people in the Netherlands have a birthday every day. The number peaks in late September and early May.

The figures are taken from over 15 million people who were born in the country and whose birth is officially registered with a local council. Those born abroad are not included.

Apart from leap day, New Year’s Day is the least common birthday. Christmas, Sinterklaas, and Liberation Day also have relatively few. The CBS said this may be because planned births, such as caesarean sections, are less often scheduled on holidays.

Birth patterns have also shifted over time. People born between 1940 and 1980 were more often born in spring, while summer and late-summer birthdays are more common among those born since 1980.

The CBS said the arrival of the contraceptive pill in the 1960s, which made pregnancies easier to plan, may explain the change.

World.title: Hundreds of thousands more to pay tax on savings, NOS says
World.content:
Hundreds of thousands more people in the Netherlands are set to pay tax on their savings and investments from 2028 under a revised plan for box 3, the tax on wealth, according to leaked details of the cabinet’s deliberations with opposition parties.

Box 3 covers savings, shares, crypto and second homes, and around 2.5 million people currently pay it, according to broadcaster NOS. At present the tax rate is 36% on an assumed return on those assets, with a tax-free allowance of €59,357 per person.

Under a new law on box 3 rules approved by MPs in February, people were to pay tax on unrealised returns on most assets every year, meaning they would pay tax on increased asset values regardless of whether they have sold the assets and made any money.

This plan is set to be dropped for shares, according to NOS, and people will only pay tax on gains from shares once they sell them. This was a demand by right-wing parties such as far-right JA21.

Initially, the new system was to allow a tax-free return of €1,800 per person a year. That has reportedly been cut to €1,000, helping offset the losses anticipated by moving to a realised gains system.

Businesses affected

People who run their own private limited company (bv) will also be affected. The amount they can borrow from their own company on favourable tax terms is set to fall from €500,000 to €100,000. The rules on borrowing from a company to buy a home will stay the same.

At the same time, tax on profits that owners pay out to themselves will be cut for 4 years. The aim is to encourage them to take money out of the company, which would bring in extra tax revenue in the short term.

The measures are expected to raise almost €500 million more than needed. The cabinet wants to use that to cut income tax, but has not yet said how.

Welfare cuts dropped

The leaked plans also confirm that planned cuts to social security are off the table, as left-wing Pro and pan-European party Volt said this week. Hans Spekman, chairman of the country’s largest trade union FNV, said on Monday evening that the unions would return to talks with the cabinet if the cuts were scrapped. Political sources told NOS that could happen as soon as next week.

JA21 said part of the funding for the box 3 changes was “unacceptable” because it hits small investors. Jan Struijs, parliamentary leader of pensioners’ party 50PLUS, said he wanted a “stress test” to show what the plans would mean for police officers, nurses and pensioners.

Finance minister Eelco Heinenis expected to set out the details in a letter to parliament ahead of this week’s budget debate. The minority cabinet needs opposition votes to get its budget through both houses of parliament.

World.title: Netherlands “blocked” Machado’s efforts to return to Venezuela
World.content:
The Dutch government has been accused of blocking the return of Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado after two flights to Curaçao and Aruba were cancelled on the same day.

Both flights were cancelled at short notice last Tuesday because of administrative “technicalities” that arose after Machado had booked to travel from her current home in Panama, according to a Spanish journalist who was embedded with her to document the trip.

The Nobel peace prize winner had hoped to slip into Venezuela via the Caribbean islands while the country’s interim president, Delcy Rodriguez, was in New York for the United Nations general assembly last week.

Officially the Netherlands supports Machado’s return so that free democratic elections can be held, something that has not happened since former president Nicolas Maduro was captured by US forces in January and replaced by Rodriguez, who was vice-president in Maduro’s regime.

Prime minister Rob Jetten said at his weekly press conference on Friday: “If Venezuela is serious about working towards a future where relations with the Netherlands and Europe are normalised, one of our conditions is that progress is made towards free and fair elections.

“Those elections are only possible if opposition leaders can participate in them.”

Trump oil deal

But behind the scenes, the Trump administration appears to be concerned that Machado’s return could destabilise the interim regime, which has struck a deal with Washington giving the US control of 65 billion barrels of crude oil reserves.

Leiden university professor Wouter Veenendaal, who specialises in relations between the nations in the Kingdom of the Netherlands, told Dutch News: “I can’t prove it, but it sounds to me like The Hague has been put under pressure by the Americans.

“Although the Americans formally take a positive view of Machado, her arrival is seen as potentially threatening the relative stability that they’ve been able to create with the interim president.”

Machado has made seven attempts to reach Venezuela by land, sea and air in recent months, including twice from Curaçao and once from Aruba, but every time her efforts have been thwarted by administrative or technical problems.

Last Tuesday a ferry trip from Panama City, where she is currently living, was cancelled hours before the boat was due to leave port after the operator claimed to have discovered a serious defect with the engine.

Paperwork problem

David Alandete, a journalist with the Spanish newspaper ABC who was invited to travel with Machado, said it was clear that the Dutch government, which controls the Caribbean islands’ foreign policy, “had a hand in preventing Machado from reaching Aruba, Curaçao or Bonaire”.

“This was not simply a paperwork problem. A European government was part of the chain of decisions that kept her from moving closer to Venezuela,” he wrote on social media site X.

Is María Corina Machado a prisoner in Panama? Why has the Nobel Peace Prize winner been prevented from returning to her own country seven times? I have the facts firsthand from Panama. I was with her team this weekend and witnessed the latest attempts—and the refusals. The full… pic.twitter.com/Jk4iBuop3m — David Alandete (@alandete) September 23, 2026

“Clearly there is something that is preventing Maria Corina Machado from returning,” Alandete said. “She has tried to enter and she’s been unable to do it.”

Jetten would neither confirm nor deny at his press conference whether the Netherlands was behind the decision to cancel Machado’s flights.

“It’s not in the interests of the co-operation we have with the [Venezuelan] opposition and the responsibility we feel for its members to say any more about it,” he said.

Caribbean journalists who asked Eric van der Burg, junior minister for kingdom relations, about the episode last week were redirected to the foreign affairs ministry in The Hague. “I can say extremely little about it,” he said, according to the Antilliaans Dagblad.

Jetten also hinted that he had been unable to persuade Rodriguez to guarantee Machado’s safe return to her country when he spoke to the interim president at the UN last week.

“It’s important that Machado and others are able to travel freely to Venezuela, and that’s why I brought it to the interim president’s attention.”

Veenendaal said the episode was typical of the way the Dutch govern Aruba, Bonaire and Curaçao, which are semi-autonomous nations within the kingdom, and the “democratic deficit” in their administration.

Colonial history

The islands are represented by Van der Burg at the cabinet table in The Hague, but have no say in which issues are raised. Their parliaments have no powers to question cabinet ministers about foreign policy or defence.

“A lot of decisions are taken over their heads, which is a sensitive point given the colonial history,” Veenendaal said.

“In the past the Americans have exerted a lot of pressure on The Hague behind the scenes, for example to prevent the islands becoming independent, but also because they have air bases on the islands so that they can keep an eye on Venezuela.”

“I can see Jetten’s government thinking: ‘choose your battles’. Let the Americans get their way here so that the Americans give them an easier ride on other issues such as the International Criminal Court or Ukraine.”

World.title: Five arrested after luggage left unattended at railway stations
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Five people have been arrested after four railway stations had to be partly evacuated on Tuesday morning when luggage was left unattended.

Haarlem station and surrounding buildings were closed and cleared after two stray bags were reported at around 10.15am. Some trains were unable to stop at the station.

Luggage was also left standing in Rotterdam, Utrecht and Dordrecht. Police said there was no evidence that the incidents were linked, but they described the situation as “highly unusual”.

Three people were arrested at Haarlem station, while two others were detained at Utrecht Centraal after camera footage showed them acting suspiciously just before they dumped the bags.

In Rotterdam a pedestrian tunnel was evacuated while police checked two abandoned suitcases for possible explosives.

A woman in Rotterdam later came forward to say she had left the bags while she went into the city centre. She was not arrested.

Spokesman Jan Martijn Stout told NOS the incidents appeared to be unconnected, but the suspects were be questioned about why they had left the bags behind.

“Their role is being investigated because it was a significant disruption to public order,” he said.

World.title: EU court rejects Poland’s request to suspend implementation of Mercosur trade deal

The Court of Justice of the European Union has rejected a request from Poland to suspend the implementation of the EU’s recently launched free trade agreement with the Mercosur bloc of South American countries. The CJEU found that the Polish government had failed to prove its claims that the trade deal would cause serious harm to European farmers, consumers or the environment. #ECJ: Order in Case C-460/26 R Poland v Council: should the implementation of the Council’s decision authorising the provisional application of the EU-Mercosur interim trade agreement be suspended pending the Court’s ruling?#CJEU #Mercosur pic.twitter.com/ocb4I4PsE8 — EU Court of Justice (@EUCourtPress) September 29, 2026 Poland has long been critical of the agreement, in particular over the potential negative impact that imports of agricultural products from Mercosur, which includes Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, could have on Polish farmers, who have repeatedly protested against the deal. In January, Poland failed in a bid to block the agreement at the European Council, where 21 of the EU’s 27 member states voted in favour of the deal. Although the agreement has not yet received final ratification – still requiring approval from the European Parliament and national parliaments – it nevertheless went into provisional force on 1 May. Shortly afterwards, Poland submitted a complaint to the CJEU, calling for implementation of the agreement to be suspended. It argued, first of all, that the process through which the deal had been provisionally implemented violated the EU’s treaties. Second, it claimed that liberalising trade in agricultural products without imposing the same production standards in both the EU and Mercosur created a risk of harm to human and animal health, the environment, the income of farmers, and the functioning of the market in the EU. Poland has filed a complaint to the European Court of Justice against the EU's free-trade deal with the South American Mercosur bloc that recently went into provisional force. It wants the agreement to be suspended until the court issues a ruling https://t.co/wE7DIbDazU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 However, on Tuesday, the CJEU announced that it had dismissed the application to suspend the agreement, finding that “Poland has not provided any concrete evidence to establish the likelihood and imminence of serious and irreparable damage”. The court pointed out that agricultural products from Mercosur could already be imported to the EU before the free-trade deal, and that they were and continue to be subject to food safety and health regulations similar to those for products manufactured in the EU. It also noted that the new trade deal includes tools allowing the EU to bar products that do not meet standards, including emergency measures in the case of a serious threat to human, animal or plant life. Finally, the CJEU said that Poland’s “general and abstract claims” regarding potential harm to farmers and markets did not include “any evidence capable of establishing, with a sufficient degree of probability, that the implementation [of the agreement]…will cause disruption”. In response to the court’s decision, the Polish government’s spokesman, Adam Szłapka, immediately blamed the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) administration, which was in power in Poland from 2015 to 2023. Szłapka said that the details of the Mercosur deal had been agreed during that period and that PiS had “failed to secure Polish interests in any way”. He argued that it was the current government which secured the addition of last-minute safeguards intended to protect farmers. The spokesman also noted that Polish agricultural exports to the Mercosur bloc have actually increased under the new agreement while imports from there have fallen, showing that “Polish farmers are profiting from this”. Rząd i Premier Tusk najpierw mówili, że umowa UE-Mercosur będzie „bezpieczna dla polskich rolników”. Potem nie potrafili zbudować koalicji blokującej w Radzie Europejskiej – choć polityka europejska jest domeną rządu. Politycy KO, PSL i Lewicy nie potrafili nikogo przekonać.… https://t.co/EqOJr4sneP — Marcin Przydacz (@marcin_przydacz) September 29, 2026 However, Marcin Przydacz, the head of the foreign policy office of President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, argued that the CJEU’s decision showed the impotence of the current pro-EU government. “The government and Prime Minister Tusk first said that the EU-Mercosur agreement would be ‘safe for Polish farmers’. Then they failed to build a blocking coalition in the European Council,” wrote Przydacz. “In the end, under pressure from public opinion in Poland, they filed a complaint with the ECJ. [It was] so weak that they lost the request for interim relief,” he added. “Ineffective policy and ineffective government.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Poland recovers looted painting that once hung in SS officers’ club in occupied Warsaw
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Polish painting looted by Nazi Germany during World War Two, and which once hung in an SS officers’ club, has been returned by its owner, who donated it to the National Museum in Warsaw. “History is coming home,” said culture minister Marta Cienkowska, celebrating the return of Alfred Wierusz-Kowalski’s Winter – Napoleon’s Retreat from Moscow, which she described as “one of the most significant wartime losses in Polish painting”. Her ministry is responsible for seeking the return of tens of thousands of artworks and other cultural items that were looted during the war and remain missing. Kolejny sukces restytucyjny! Odzyskaliśmy jedną z cenniejszych i najbardziej znanych strat wojennych malarstwa polskiego. Obraz „Zima – Odwrót Napoleona spod Moskwy” Alfreda Wierusza-Kowalskiego trafił dziś do zbiorów Muzeum Narodowego w Warszawie. To efekt naszej współpracy z… pic.twitter.com/Y0wDIBgIGG — Ministerstwo Kultury i Dziedzictwa Narodowego (@kultura_gov_pl) September 28, 2026 Wierusz-Kowalski, who was active in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, was a renowned realist painter whose work often featured animals alongside people. His Winter – Napoleon’s Retreat from Moscow had, by the 1930s, become part of the collection of Andrzej Rotwand, a wealthy banker and industrialist. In June 1939, it was featured in an exhibition organised by the Society for the Encouragement of Fine Arts in Warsaw, which occupied the building that is now the famous Zachęta National Gallery of Art. However, the exhibition was brought to an abrupt end when Nazi Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. The works on display, along with other items from the gallery, were seized by the occupiers, with many used to decorate the offices and apartments of German officials. Winter – Napoleon’s Retreat from Moscow was displayed in a club for high-ranking SS and police officers located in Warsaw’s Blanka Palace. The same building also housed Warsaw’s German-installed commissioner, Helmut Otto, and mayor, Ludwig Leist. No information has been released as to the fate of the painting in the immediate aftermath of the war. However, it eventually came into the possession of Ewa Tsonis, who has now handed it back. Speaking at a ceremony in the National Museum in Warsaw, Tsonis said that her late father, Michał Stefan Koryzna, had purchased the painting in the 1960s from Desa, a major gallery and auction house, in the city of Kraków. “I grew up with this painting. It was greatly appreciated and loved in our family,” she said. However, after recently conducting research into the painting’s history, she became aware of its provenance and notified the culture ministry. Experts from the National Museum in Warsaw confirmed the identity of the painting, which remains in good condition and in its original frame. Tsonis then donated the work to the museum. “Restitution is not possible without the cooperation of many people and institutions – both on the side of the state and on the part of the owners of the works,” said Cienkowska, who thanked Tsonis for her “incredibly responsible and civic-minded attitude”. “Such attitudes are still rare but, because we constantly talk about restitution – we search for lost works and strive to recover them – we are increasingly approached by people who own lost objects and feel a sense of responsibility for cultural heritage.” Cienkowska noted that the culture ministry has so far secured the return of over 920 works, with around 200 more restitution cases currently underway in 18 countries. Germany has agreed to return to Poland a collection of 73 medieval documents that were looted during WWII. The culture minister has hailed it as "the most important and valuable return of stolen cultural heritage in modern Polish history" https://t.co/GxHQ8A0jyr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 1, 2025 However, that is still just a small fraction of the over 60,000 missing items listed in the ministry’s database of missing works, which includes seven further paintings by Wierusz-Kowalski. Two other works from Rotwand’s collection – Italian Woman by Anna Bilińska and Mother with Children by Kazimierz Alchimowicz – were also hung in the SS officers’ club during the war and today remain missing. Poland has in recent years stepped up efforts to secure the return of historical and cultural items looted during the German and Soviet occupations. In 2022, it appealed to UNESCO for help in securing the return of cultural items that remain missing after being looted by Nazi Germany. It also launched a campaign seeking the return of thousands of items that ended up in Russia after the war. World.title: Poland changes rules of engagement for firing on foreign aircraft amid growing Russia threat
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland is changing the procedures under which its military can fire upon foreign aircraft, citing the “growing threat from Russia”. Visual identification of targets will no longer be required, with other forms of data to be used instead. The move follows a series of violations of Polish airspace over the last year by Russian drones, a missile and a helicopter, as well as Russia’s increasing use of jet-powered drones to attack targets in Ukraine close to the Polish border. Polska zmienia procedury użycia uzbrojenia dla lotnictwa w przypadku zwalczania obcych statków powietrznych. To wnioski Dowódcy Operacyjnego generała Ireneusza Nowaka z ostatnich tygodni. To także odpowiedź na rosnące zagrożenie ze strony Rosji, doświadczenia wojny w Ukrainie… — Cezary Tomczyk (@CTomczyk) September 28, 2026 “In the coming days, the defence minister will change the procedures for firing by Polish planes and helicopters at objects flying to us from the direction of Russia,” announced deputy defence minister Cezary Tomczyk on Monday, quoted by news service Defence24. The change, as Tomczyk explained in a statement later issued on social media, will shift requirements away from requiring visual identification of foreign aerial objects and towards so-called “positive identification”. The latter involves identifying an object based on a combination of several other, non-visual sources of information, such as using radar and other sensors to determine its speed, altitude, trajectory and flight parameters, as well as a lack of IFF (identification friend or foe) from an object. Tomczyk said that the change was being made based on the “conclusions from recent weeks” made by the operational commander of Poland’s armed forces, General Ireneusz Nowak. It is a “response to the growing threat from Russia, experiences from the war in Ukraine, and the emergence of new air attack means – primarily fast jet drones and cruise missiles in the case of which the time for reaction is very brief”, added Tomczyk. The minister said that positive identification would only be issued when there is a “sufficiently high degree of certainty in determining what we are dealing with”. He noted that accurate target identification is particularly crucial in peacetime, when there are civilian aircraft in Polish airspace. The change will mean “not less identification, but a different way of conducting it: faster and based on data from multiple sources”. Poland's government has issued public guidance on how to act in the case of airborne attacks, amid growing concerns over the threat from Russia. It is also preparing evacuation plans and clearer markings for 85,000 shelters across the countryhttps://t.co/vMEMU6mlRx — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 25, 2026 Defence24 reports that the government, military and many experts have found current rules of engagement to be overly restrictive and not suited to meeting the scale and type of threat facing Poland today. It points to last week’s violation of Polish airspace by a Russian helicopter, which crossed the border from Kaliningrad and spent around 42 seconds in Poland before returning. The website also notes that Russia’s growing use of jet-powered drones, which are able to travel much faster than traditional unmanned aerial vehicles, is a further threat. Such drones have recently been used to attack targets along the Ukrainian side of the border with Poland, including a passenger train travelling between Kyiv and Warsaw. A drone has struck a passenger train travelling between Kyiv and Warsaw, around 2 km from the Polish border, amid the latest mass Russian attacks on Ukraine. Separately, a truck around 800 metres from a border crossing with Poland was also hit last night https://t.co/ZbfE2iDLOk — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 13, 2026 “Until now, we have not utilised these [non-visual identification] capabilities because they are typically reserved for a state of war or martial law,” said Tomczyk. “However, given the threat, and the fact that Poland today struggles daily with the possibility of drones entering our country, we must implement these changes for the benefit of both pilots and national security.” In July this year, a Russian Kh-101 cruise missile also entered Polish airspace before landing in a field. On one night last year, around 20 Russian drones crossed Poland’s eastern borders. Some were shot down but many struck the ground. Earlier this month, Prime Minister Donald Tusk warned that, according to intelligence sources, Russia is planning drone and missile strikes on eastern NATO countries, which it would present as accidental. Russia is planning drone and missile strikes on eastern NATO countries, which it would present as accidental, says Polish Prime Minister @donaldtusk, citing intelligence sources. The aim would be to create a sense of "NATO's helplessness", he says https://t.co/9MFPiEEkIV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) September 18, 2026 Poland has invested heavily in its air defences in recent years, including buying Patriot batteries and fighter aircraft from the United States, as well as developing a new anti-drone system with Norway’s Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace. The government has also recently moved to expand the network of warning sirens along the Ukrainian border, launched a campaign informing the public how to respond to aerial threats, and started more clearly marking bomb shelters.
