“Abukhba was sentenced to nine years for raping a Russian tourist, robbery and causing grievous bodily harm. The case then went through several levels of court. Because of the way sentences are enforced in Abkhazia, he was actually released on 2 February 2024, after serving about 4½ years.

The nine-year sentence itself was not formally reduced. But that is not really the main question.

What happened to him after he was released?

Abkhazia has a law providing for administrative supervision of people released from prison. And this is where I have questions.

Were any monitoring or preventive measures put in place after Abukhba’s release? Who is responsible for assessing the risk that someone who has committed such a violent crime could do it again, and how is that risk assessed?

I am not saying that administrative supervision would necessarily have saved Amina. No one can know that. But when someone who has committed such a crime returns to society, the work should not end on the day of his release.

A systemic reform of the security system is needed: reviewing certain provisions of criminal law, tighter controls on firearms, and strengthening the Interior Ministry in terms of personnel and technical capacity. […]

And then there are the comments directed at Amina.

Yes, it can be said that you should not go to the home of someone you barely know. But a risky decision does not make someone responsible for their own murder.

Amina may not have known who she was dealing with or what was in his past. The authorities did.

At the same time, I disagree with attempts to attribute the crime of one individual to all of Abkhazia. After the family reported her disappearance, law enforcement identified and detained a suspect and found the woman’s body. The investigation is continuing.

But good police work after a killing does not remove the main question: could something have been done before it happened?

And here I would like to see not a search for one guilty agency or one particular person, but an honest examination of what needs to change in the law and across the security system to prevent similar cases from happening again.”

The terminology, place names and views expressed in this article are those of the author and do not necessarily reflect the editorial position of this website.

World.title: ‘Which neighbouring country would you visit?’ Tbilisi street poll – VIDEO
World.content:
Travel poll in Georgia

We asked people on the streets of Tbilisi which of Georgia’s neighbouring countries they would like to visit and why.

We also asked whether they had previously travelled to any countries in the region, why they chose those destinations and what impressions they came away with.

The answers vary widely. Turkey is mentioned most often, with respondents drawn by its picturesque coastline and the Bosphorus. Many also say they would be happy to visit Armenia or Azerbaijan, while some look further afield and name more distant countries in the region.

Russia is rarely mentioned in a positive context. Instead, it is named by almost every respondent when asked which neighbouring country they would not like to visit.

Through this survey, we sought to find out how well people in Georgia know the countries of the South Caucasus and their other neighbours, what interests them about these countries and what stereotypes they hold about them.

World.title: SOCAR, ExxonMobil sign deal to explore for oil and gas in Azerbaijan’s Middle Kura Basin
World.content:
Oil and gas investment in Azerbaijan

At the second Azerbaijan International Investment Forum in Baku, SOCAR and ExxonMobil signed a production-sharing agreement for the exploration and development of unconventional hydrocarbon resources in the Middle Kura Basin. A final investment decision was also made on the full-field development of the Absheron gas field.

Speaking on 26 September about investment priorities for the coming decade, Ilham Aliyev said the oil and gas sector would retain a leading role.

What will ExxonMobil look for in the Middle Kura Basin?

The agreement provides for the exploration, development and production of unconventional hydrocarbon resources in the Middle Kura Basin. According to SOCAR, the companies will each hold a 50% stake in the project through their subsidiaries, with ExxonMobil acting as operator.

The project does not involve the development of an existing offshore field in the Caspian Sea, but rather the exploration of the oil and gas potential of an onshore basin. Bloomberg has linked the project to shale oil and gas production. It has also been reported that the project is awaiting parliamentary approval.

Aliyev said successful exploration “could lead to another oil and gas boom in Azerbaijan”.

Published information does not specify when commercial production could begin, targeted annual production levels, confirmed recoverable reserves or the project’s overall budget. The precise size and boundaries of the contract area have also not been disclosed.

For Azerbaijan, the significance of the agreement lies in bringing ExxonMobil’s technology and expertise in developing unconventional hydrocarbon resources into the search for new reserves. However, the basin’s resource potential and the commercial viability of development will have to be established before its possible economic impact can be assessed.

Absheron: annual gas production set to quadruple

SOCAR, TotalEnergies and XRG have taken a final investment decision on the full-field development of the Absheron gas and condensate field. According to TotalEnergies, which operates the project, the company holds a 35% stake. SOCAR also owns 35%, while XRG holds 30%.

Under the company’s plan, annual gas production will increase from 1.5bn to 6bn cubic metres, while daily condensate production will rise from 12,000 to 47,000 barrels. The new phase of development is expected to begin in 2029.

In his speech, Aliyev spoke of an additional 5bn cubic metres of gas within three to four years. However, the figures presented by the company imply an increase in annual production of 4.5bn cubic metres.

TotalEnergies says the gas produced will be supplied to the domestic market and Turkey.

GDP diversifying, but energy still dominates exports

Discussing the country’s future economic model, Aliyev said “oil and gas will retain a leading role in our economy”, adding that the revenues generated would be reinvested in the economy.

The president said the non-oil sector accounted for more than 70% of GDP, while, according to him, oil and gas still made up more than 90% of exports.

According to calculations by Marja based on State Customs Committee statistics, oil and gas products accounted for 71.22% of goods exports in January-August 2026.

Electricity, data centres and logistics

Aliyev linked the development of renewable energy to efforts to reduce domestic gas consumption and free up additional volumes for export. He also referred to the expansion of power transmission lines for electricity exports and projects to lay submarine cables across the Caspian and Black seas.

The president identified supplying electricity to data centres and artificial intelligence systems as a priority and said an Azerbaijan-Kazakhstan fibre-optic cable would become operational by the end of the year. Documents relating to the Oracle Alloy project were also exchanged at the forum. According to SOCAR, Caspian Mind AI will serve as the local operator.

In transport, the government aims to increase transit freight volumes from an expected 16m tonnes in 2026 to at least 25m tonnes by 2030. Discussing food and water security, Aliyev highlighted water shortages and the need to reduce dependence on food imports, while also calling for investment in agriculture.

What does the $10.8bn package actually represent?

According to the Economy Ministry, 23 documents covering projects worth a combined $10.8bn were signed at the forum. The ministry says these projects are planned for implementation.

However, the documents represent projects at different stages of development. A final investment decision has been taken on Absheron. The ExxonMobil agreement establishes the contractual framework for exploration and subsequent development. A framework agreement with Comstock provides for studying opportunities to liquefy US gas and sell it on international markets. A memorandum with Apollo concerns assessing potential investments, conducting due diligence and preparing final agreements.

Published information does not provide a full breakdown of the $10.8bn figure among individual projects, a financing timetable or details of how much has already been formalised as binding financial commitments. There is therefore no basis for treating the entire amount as a guaranteed inflow of foreign investment.

Aliyev described the government’s approach to investment policy as follows:

“All we have to do is create favourable conditions.”

The economic results of the forum will ultimately depend on the actual investment made in the announced projects, as well as growth in production and non-oil exports.

World.title: Uzbekistan's UTK pitches Turkmenbashi-Baku feeder service at TCTC forum
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 30. Today, Uzbekistan’s Uztemiryolkonteyner proposed a regular feeder shipping service between Turkmenbashi and Baku across the Caspian Sea as part of efforts to expand multimodal transport links between Uzbekistan and Europe, during the TCTC Conference in Tashkent.

This was reflected in the statement by UTK, following the initiative presented by M.K. Mirhamidov, chairman of the board of Uztemiryolkonteyner, on Sept. 30 at the second national conference on the development of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor in Uzbekistan, held in Tashkent under the Global Gateway framework.

The proposed Turkmenbashi–Baku service is intended to create an additional maritime link for Uzbek cargo moving toward European markets and reduce delivery times by strengthening the Caspian segment of the Trans-Caspian route.

“The organization of regular feeder services between Turkmenbashi and Baku will create additional opportunities to accelerate cargo delivery, expand multimodal transportation and strengthen Uzbekistan’s connectivity with European markets,” Uztemiryolkonteyner said during the presentation.

Additionally, the company presented preliminary investment projects to modernize logistics centers in Raustan, Margilan, Jizzakh, Ulugbek and Termez, aimed at increasing their capacity to handle international cargo.

The proposed maritime connection would link Uzbekistan’s rail and logistics network with Turkmenbashi International Seaport in Turkmenistan and the Port of Baku in Azerbaijan, strengthening the Caspian section of the Trans-Caspian Transport Corridor.

The company announced that the projects are intended to expand international freight transportation and create opportunities for cooperation with international partners in developing Uzbekistan’s transport and logistics infrastructure.

World.title: Turkish CANİK M3 anti-aircraft weapon takes spotlight at ADEX 2026 (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 30. The “CANİK M3” anti-aircraft weapon, developed by the Turkish arms manufacturer “CANİK,” is on display at the “ADEX” exhibition, Trend’s correspondent reports from the exhibition venue.

CANİK has integrated the “M3 FALCON” machine gun with the “FALCON FLEX 50” modular mounting system onto the Azerbaijani Air Force’s Mi-17 helicopters.

The 6th Azerbaijan International Defense Exhibition “ADEX-2026” and the 15th anniversary International Exhibition of Equipment for Internal Security, Protection, and Rescue Operations “Securex Caspian” have begun.

In total, more than 270 companies from 29 countries have confirmed their participation in the “ADEX” and “Securex Caspian” exhibitions. To date, 45 foreign delegations from 33 countries have registered to participate in the exhibitions.

Among the countries represented by delegations are the U.S., Belarus, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, the UK, South Korea, the Czech Republic, Afghanistan, Georgia, Jordan, Iraq, Israel, Italy, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Malaysia, Morocco, Montenegro, Nigeria, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, Russia, Serbia, Saudi Arabia, Slovakia, Sudan, Northern Cyprus, Türkiye, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uganda, and Vietnam.

In addition, 14 countries are represented at the exhibitions with national pavilions: the U.S., Azerbaijan, Belarus, the UK, the Czech Republic, China, Israel, Italy, Pakistan, Romania, Russia, Slovakia, Türkiye, and Uzbekistan.

One of the main new features of “ADEX-2026” is that Pavilion 4 of the Baku Expo Center has been designated for national pavilions for the first time.

World.title: Iran views Strait of Hormuz security as key to regional stability – Pezeshkian
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 30. Iran’s approach to the Strait of Hormuz is based on a strategic and responsible commitment to protecting the security, stability and interests of countries in the region.

According to the Iranian president’s information portal, Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said this in a message marking World Maritime Day on September 30.

“The Strait of Hormuz, as one of the world’s important maritime passages, has a special role in the economy and security of the region and the world. Iran believes that sustainable security in the Persian Gulf and its waterways depends largely on cooperation among regional countries,” he said.

Pezeshkian added that, with long coastlines to the north and south and its location along major regional routes, Iran is among the world’s key centers of maritime activity, the maritime economy and trade.

He said security and development along the region’s major routes are two inseparable issues. The security of maritime routes, ports and communication lines creates conditions for trade and economic activity, he added.

The Iranian president said that beyond the economy and security, the sea should also be viewed as an important area for scientific research and environmental protection.

The latest escalation in U.S.-Iran tensions began on July 8. On that day, U.S. forces carried out several waves of strikes on Iranian territory, saying they were in response to an attack on a commercial vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. The strikes followed a memorandum signed between Washington and Tehran.

U.S. President Donald Trump announced the same day that the ceasefire with Iran had ended. In response, Tehran began striking U.S. facilities in Bahrain, Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE and Oman.

The conflict severely disrupted maritime trade through the Strait of Hormuz.

World.title: Iran receives U.S. proposal to resume negotiations, official says
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 30. The Iranian side has received a proposal from the U.S. to resume negotiations.

This was reported by Iranian government spokesperson Fatemeh Mohajerani on her social media account on “X.”

“Iranian Foreign Minister Seyyed Abbas Araghchi has received a proposal from the U.S. addressed to Iran,” she wrote.

Mohajerani stated that today’s meeting of the Iranian Cabinet addressed issues related to the Iranian foreign minister’s visit to New York, the meetings held there, and Iran’s proposal, put forward through intermediaries, regarding the opening of the Strait of Hormuz.

The government spokesperson noted that, despite the other side’s efforts to isolate Iran, the Iranian delegation remained the center of attention. Numerous meetings were held with officials from European countries, Gulf states, and other nations, while diplomatic efforts to find a solution in the realm of foreign policy remained a key focus.

Meanwhile, the latest escalation in relations between the U.S. and Iran began on July 8. On that day, for the first time since the signing of the memorandum between Washington and Tehran, the U.S. military launched several waves of strikes against Iranian territory, stating that they were in response to an attack on a merchant ship in the Strait of Hormuz. On the same day, U.S. President Donald Trump announced the end of the ceasefire with Iran. In response, Tehran began striking U.S. targets located in Bahrain, Jordan, Qatar, Kuwait, the UAE, and Oman.

World.title: Uzbekistan, Egypt target 20,000 hectares for new agricultural projects
World.content:
Photo: The Ministry of Economy and Finance of Uzbekistan

BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 30. Uzbekistan and Egypt prepared pilot projects covering 20,000 hectares to improve water management, restore pastures and unused land, and introduce modern agricultural technologies, following a meeting on Sept. 29 in Tashkent.

This was reflected in the statement by the Ministry of Economy and Finance of Uzbekistan, following a meeting between First Deputy Minister of Economy and Finance Ilhom Norqulov and Egypt’s Ambassador to Uzbekistan Tamer Fathi Abdelsalam Hammad to discuss expanding bilateral economic cooperation, with a focus on agriculture, water resources management, irrigation, desert and pasture development, and scientific research.

“The implementation of previously reached agreements and the launch of pilot projects will help translate the accumulated experience of Uzbekistan and Egypt into practical results, particularly in efficient water use and agricultural development,” the Uzbek side said.

Particular attention was given to the Uzbek delegation’s visit to Egypt on Sept. 15–20, during which officials studied Egypt’s experience in water management, land development, modern irrigation technologies, seed production, livestock breeding and the productive use of desert areas.

Additionally, the two sides discussed expanding cooperation between Uzbek and Egyptian research institutions. Proposed areas include water-saving technologies, hydrology and modeling, geographic information systems (GIS), remote sensing, climate change and water reuse.

Uzbekistan and Egypt are also considering reciprocal visits by specialists and researchers and the involvement of experts from leading Egyptian research institutions in projects in Uzbekistan.

The planned pilot projects are expected to focus on pasture restoration, the development of unused land, modern irrigation solutions, seed production and livestock breeding, drawing on Egypt’s practical experience.

The parties agreed to develop concrete joint projects, strengthen contacts between experts and advance scientific and practical cooperation in the identified areas.

World.title: Azerbaijan’s new “KASIRGA” UAV takes center stage at ADEX (PHOTO)
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 30. The “KASIRGA” unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV), developed by Azerbaijani engineers and technicians, was unveiled for the first time at the ADEX exhibition, according to a Trend correspondent reporting from the event.

Meanwhile, this UAV was developed by Bayraktar Teknoloji Azerbaijan.

In addition, it is noted that “KASIRGA,” which is capable of vertical takeoff and landing, autonomous flight supported by artificial intelligence, and performing two types of missions, will make a significant contribution to the development of Azerbaijan’s technological capabilities.

The platform uses four electric motors during hover and horizontal flight and can operate in both kamikaze mode (circular flight) and reconnaissance missions.

The platform, which is equipped with a return-to-base function during reconnaissance operations, has a maximum takeoff weight of 33 kilograms and a payload capacity of 6 kilograms.

Equipped with a 5-kilogram warhead and an AI-supported electro-optical (EO) camera system, “KASIRGA” is capable of high-precision targeting. The platform, which has a communication range of over 80 kilometers, can conduct operations by utilizing the communication relay capabilities of the “Bayraktar TB2,” “Bayraktar TB3,” or “AKINCI” UAVs.

Equipped with anti-jamming systems (signal interference resistance), visual positioning, and autonomous flight systems based on sensor data fusion, “KASIRGA” is capable of conducting operations within a 60-kilometer radius for kamikaze missions and a 90-kilometer radius for reconnaissance operations.

The 6th Azerbaijan International Defense Exhibition “ADEX-2026” and the 15th anniversary International Exhibition of Equipment for Internal Security, Protection, and Rescue Operations “Securex Caspian” have begun.

In total, more than 270 companies from 29 countries have confirmed their participation in the “ADEX” and “Securex Caspian” exhibitions. To date, 45 foreign delegations from 33 countries have registered to participate in the exhibitions.

Among the countries represented by delegations are the US, Belarus, Bahrain, the United Arab Emirates, the UK, South Korea, the Czech Republic, Afghanistan, Georgia, Jordan, Iraq, Israel, Italy, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Latvia, Malaysia, Morocco, Montenegro, Nigeria, Uzbekistan, Pakistan, Russia, Serbia, Saudi Arabia, Slovakia, Sudan, Northern Cyprus, Türkiye, Turkmenistan, Ukraine, Uganda, and Vietnam.

In addition, the exhibition features national pavilions from 14 countries, including the US, Azerbaijan, Belarus, the United Kingdom, the Czech Republic, China, Israel, Italy, Pakistan, Romania, Russia, Slovakia, Türkiye, and Uzbekistan.

One of the main innovations of “ADEX” 2026 is that, for the first time, the 4th exhibition hall of the Baku Expo Center has been designated for the national exhibition.

World.title: RWS KZ signs agreement with Deutsche Bahn to prepare rail wheels for EU market
World.content:
BAKU, Azerbaijan, September 30. Kazakhstan’s RWS KZ holding and RWS Prommashkomplekt, part of RWS KZ, signed a memorandum of understanding with Deutsche Bahn on September 29 to prepare solid-rolled railway wheels manufactured by RWS Prommashkomplekt for supplies to the European market, RWS KZ said.

The next stage will include certification of BA 318 wheels under the agreement with Deutsche Bahn, as well as BA 319 wheels for freight and passenger rolling stock, the company said.

The agreement provides for the manufacturer qualification procedure required for admission of the products to supplies, including a production audit, qualification and operational testing of the wheels in line with Deutsche Bahn’s internal requirements and European standards for solid-rolled railway wheels.

According to RWS KZ, the company is developing production of solid-rolled wheels for the European railway market in 920-mm sizes, including BA 303, BA 004, BA 318 and BA 319.

The company is undergoing TSI WAG certification in accordance with European requirements for freight and passenger rolling stock. Testing is being completed to obtain certificates of conformity with EU requirements for BA 303 and BA 004 wheels.

After the certification and qualification procedures are completed, the parties will be able to discuss specific orders, including technical requirements, production and supply volumes and delivery timelines. Cooperation with Deutsche Bahn represents another step by the company toward realizing its export potential, RWS KZ said.

Testing is being conducted at accredited testing laboratories on specialized equipment and includes, among other procedures, thermomechanical and fatigue tests in accordance with European standards. The tests are designed to assess the reliability and durability of the wheels under operational loads.

“Obtaining EU Certificates of Conformity will enable the company to supply products to customers in EU countries and move toward signing its first commercial contracts. The company is already negotiating with potential European partners and receiving requests for technical information,” RWS KZ Holding CEO Sergey Pavlinger said.

At the initial stage, the company will focus on wheels for freight and passenger railway rolling stock. Further expansion of the product range will depend on the needs of the European market and potential customers.

The company uses modern heat treatment technologies and high-precision full-profile machining in wheel production. The raw materials are currently supplied by foreign producers that ensure the required quality characteristics and stable supplies.

Following completion of the construction of an electrometallurgical plant in Ekibastuz, the holding plans to use its own raw materials and localize production, RWS KZ said.

World.title: Couple stabbed woman in frenzied attack over love triangle, court told
World.content:
A woman was stabbed to death and her body stuffed in a child’s wardrobe after a frenzied attack arising from a “love triangle” that left the walls of a Broadwater home spattered in blood, a Perth court has heard.

WARNING: This story contains graphic details that may distress some readers.

Hannah Louise Glover, 30, and James Anthony Sorgiovanni, 29, are accused of murdering Tara Marie Morrison in the Busselton suburb of Broadwater in April 2024.

The Supreme Court heard Ms Morrison had been in a sexual relationship with Ms Glover before the accused started a relationship with Mr Sorgiovanni, with whom she lived at Bell Drive.

Tara Morrison went to the couple's home in Busselton the day she was murdered, the court heard. (Facebook)

Listening devices planted in prison by police allegedly captured Ms Glover admitting to the murder to a fellow inmate and saying multiple knives had been used.

Prosecutor Michael Cvetkoski said that on the day she was murdered, Ms Morrison went to the Bell Drive home, where she used methylamphetamine with the couple.

Mr Cvetkoski said a neighbour heard screaming from the house, "like a woman was in pain and distressed", which lasted for 30 minutes.

"She [Ms Morrison] was, in every sense of the word, fighting for her life," he said.

"She had, in every sense, no hope."

The court was shown graphic footage of the blood-spattered house and Ms Morrison's body, which had been stuffed in the wardrobe of Ms Glover's toddler daughter's bedroom.

The court was also shown CCTV of people on a scooter, which Mr Cvetkoski said were Mr Sorgiovanni and Ms Glover leaving the scene with Ms Glover's daughter, then aged 18 months.

The gas had been left on at the house because Ms Glover and Mr Sorgiovanni intended to burn it down, the prosecutor said.

Jealous love triangle

Mr Sorgiovanni told police Ms Glover had attacked Ms Morrison while he tried to help her and call Triple Zero (000), the court was told.

Ms Glover allegedly told a fellow inmate that Mr Sorgiovanni had restrained the victim as she was being stabbed.

Forensics officers scoured the Broadwater home after the alleged murder. (ABC News: Jacqueline Lynch)

Mr Cvetkoski said Ms Glover had referred to a "love triangle" and that Mr Sorgiovanni and Ms Morrison were jealous of each other.

Ms Glover's lawyer, Anthony Eyers, said his client admitted to being in the Bell Drive home when Ms Morrison was killed, but maintained Mr Sorgiovanni had committed the murder.

Defence lawyer Anthony Eyers urged the jury to keep an open mind. (ABC News: David Weber)

He called on the jury members to "keep open minds".

Mr Sorgiovanni's lawyer Lisa Boston said the evidence would show that Ms Glover had killed Ms Morrison.

She said her client had been affected by drugs and had woken up to "a horror show" after passing out on his bed.

The sedative effects of the drugs had prevented Mr Sorgiovanni from stopping Ms Glover, his lawyer said.

The trial is set down for six weeks.

World.title: Baghdad celebrates, Kurds concerned as US completes Iraq withdrawal
World.content:
The US military has completed the withdrawal of its troops from Iraq, ending a 12-year mission to fight the Islamic State group.

The last troops have left the last air base where they had been maintaining a presence in northern Iraq under an agreement between Baghdad and Washington, the military announced on Wednesday.

Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said in a statement that US troops and equipment had completed an "orderly departure" from the air base in Irbil, in northern Iraq's semi-autonomous Kurdish region.

Loading...

"This milestone reflects the success of a 12-year campaign that defeated ISIS as an organised military threat in Iraq and across the region," he said.

"It also marks a transition from a wartime coalition mission to an Iraqi-led security effort supported by a more normal bilateral security relationship."

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi presided over the handover ceremony and described the US withdrawal as the beginning of a "a new phase, one defined by Iraq's sovereignty, the strength of its institutions, the readiness of its forces, the unity of its decision-making, and balanced partnerships with its friends".

Officials concerned over removal of air defence

Some Iraqis say the US troop withdrawal is a breakthrough moment for the nation. (Reuters: Alaa Al-Marjani)

The move, which comes in the midst of an ongoing war between the United States and Iran that has also sometimes spilled over into Iraq, was touted by Baghdad as a sign of the country's increasing strength and sovereignty.

The withdrawal raised concerns among some other other Iraqis, particularly in the Kurdish region.

Officials in Iraq's Kurdish region have expressed anxiety about the departure and particularly about the removal of US air defence systems.

The Kurdish regional government's Peshmerga Ministry said the Kurdish region had faced more than 1,000 drone and ballistic-missile attacks during the recent US-Iran conflict.

"The departure of the United States from the Kurdistan Region under these complex regional circumstances, without the provision of a defense system, is a matter of concern," the statement said.

US strikes Iran-backed militants in Iraq Fresh fighting has erupted after the US accused Iran of launching its first ballistic missile attack on an American base since strikes were paused on Friday. Here's your three-minute briefing on the key developments in the Middle East overnight.

The Iraqi government initially linked the September 30 deadline for US withdrawal to the disarmament of non-state armed groups by that date.

While a handful of less-influential militias have agreed to turn over their weapons, powerful groups close to Iran rejected the prospect or set conditions for disarming that the government would be unlikely to meet.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has since walked back the deadline. He told The New York Times earlier this month that the deadline for militia disarmament has been pushed to June 2027.

Iran-allied groups in Iraq, meanwhile, have celebrated the US withdrawal.

"The expulsion of the occupation forces, defeated, from the land of Iraq is the beginning of full sovereignty," Abu Mujahid al-Assaf, a security official with the powerful Kataib Hezbollah militia, said in a statement.

He added a warning to Mr al-Zaidi and his government not to carry out American plans, threatening that "any government that does not work for the benefit of the people will be overthrown by all means."

Total withdrawal comes after 2024 wind-down

Iraqi forces have supported US efforts to combat Islamic State. (Reuters: Ahmed Saad)

US troops invaded Iraq in 2003 to topple Saddam Hussein.

They departed in 2011, but three years later, Iraqi authorities invited a smaller US-led mission to fight the Islamic State group, which had rampaged across Iraq, seizing large swaths of territory.

With the extremist group reduced to scattered sleeper cells, Washington and Baghdad agreed in 2024 to wind the mission down.

US troops pulled out of bases in most areas of Iraq last year but maintained a small presence of hundreds of troops in the semi-autonomous northern Kurdish region.

Bases there have regularly come under attack since the US and Israel launched their war against Iran on February 28.

Iran-backed Iraqi militias also have coordinated with Yemen's Houthi rebels to attack Saudi Arabia.

AP

World.title: Mining couple have explosive gender reveal at Kalgoorlie's Super Pit
World.content:
A WA couple who fell pregnant after 11 years of IVF treatments have celebrated their baby joy with a unique gender reveal, in the form of an explosive blast at one of Australia's biggest gold mines.

Lance and Kristy Richards both work at Kalgoorlie's Super Pit, about 600 kilometres east of Perth in Western Australia's Goldfields, as a dozer operator and truck driver, respectively.

A puff of pink smoke at the sides of the blast revealed the Richards would be having a baby girl. (ABC Goldfields: Daniel Holmes)

The couple wed in 2014 and are due to welcome their first baby in late January, following what they described as a "rollercoaster" journey with infertility.

"When we started IVF 11 years ago, we had high hopes and got pregnant straight away, but had a miscarriage at seven weeks, which really rattled us," Mr Richards said.

It was an emotional gender reveal for Lance and Kristy Richards. (ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas)

"It's hell. It was a lot of rollercoaster rides ... mentally, physically, emotionally, financially.

"Towards the end, we just accepted it wasn't going to happen, so we went to IVF appointments with no expectations of getting pregnant, but always the hope that maybe this time will be the one."

Lance and Kristy Richards tried for more than a decade to conceive through IVF. (ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas)

Pretty in pink

Mrs Richards, who is 22 weeks' pregnant, said they were in "disbelief" after discovering they had conceived on a European holiday to Spain.

After sharing their baby joy with colleagues, they were convinced to stage a unique gender reveal incorporating the daily explosives blast at the Super Pit.

"We were incredibly private about it at the start, but there's a bit of a stigma around the whole IVF process, so hopefully this helps others to talk about it," Mrs Richards said.

"We live on the opposite side of the country to our family. We came here from Queensland for the work and so our work crew is our family."

Work colleagues presented the couple with a pink balloon immediately after the blast. (ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas)

The couple pushed the button to trigger the blast on Wednesday and a thick cloud of pink smoke told the couple, and hundreds of onlookers, they are expecting a baby girl.

"It was great to share that moment with everyone," Mr Richards said.

"The IVF journey is such a hard one for anyone to go through and for us, sharing that journey with workmates and friends, to hear that cheer, that support, it's amazing."

"It was overwhelming," Mrs Richards said.

Hundreds of onlookers turned up to the public lookout to witness the gender reveal at the Super Pit. (ABC Goldfields: Jarrod Lucas)

Blasts for special occasions

Wednesday was not the first time the daily routine of explosive blasts has taken on a bigger meaning at the Super Pit.

Since 2018, explosive crews have turned blasts pink for International Women's Day as part of a campaign to grow the mine's female workforce.

About 35 per cent of the 1,800-strong workforce at the Super Pit is female, according to Northern Star Resources human resources manager Nicole Musgrave.

An explosive mine blast designed in the shape of the Venus symbol created a large plume of pink smoke to celebrate International Women's Day at the Super Pit in 2019. (Supplied: Kalgoorlie Consolidated Gold Mines)

In 2019, crews went a step further by using 250 kilograms of pink powder and 100kg of high explosive to mark up the blast in the shape of the Venus symbol.

Ms Musgrave said the gold miner had also previously blasted blue powder to raise awareness for men's mental health.

She said she was pleased to approve the special request for two employees, but admitted there were no plans for further gender reveals at the mine.

"We have a lot of things come by our desk but this was a great one to endorse," she said.

The Super Pit has been operating since 1989, measures 4km long and 1.6km at its widest point and is expected to continue operating until at least 2050.

World.title: Youth detention workers reach in-principle pay deal with Qld government
World.content:
Queensland youth detention workers have reached an in-principle pay deal with the state government, ending months of negotiation and industrial action.

Negotiations began in early March, with the Australian Workers' Union (AWU) pushing for better conditions following hundreds of reported assaults on detention centre employees over the past year.

Youth detention workers at centres across the state mounted strike action in June, August and September, citing concerns about overcrowding and understaffing.

On Wednesday night AWU Queensland secretary Stacey Schinnerl said the union had accepted, in principle, the government's latest offer.

"This offer was hard-fought for by AWU members through significant protected industrial action, including strike action and workplace bans," she said.

"This offer will see pay rises, an advanced progression for new starters, a senior position review and lucrative retention payments for long-serving employees."

Stacey Schinnerl said the offer would go some way to helping improve employee retention. (ABC News: Lucy Loram)

The department confirmed an in-principle deal had been reached.

The in-principle deal will still need to be voted upon by the workforce, the AWU said.

The deal will include early progression for new starters and a $3,000 retention bonus at five years of service and $6,000 for 10 years.

Ms Schinnerl said the deal would go "some way" toward improving worker retention.

"But whatever the industrial deal, nothing will shift our laser focus on improving workplace safety and tackling the scourge of occupational violence," she said.

World.title: Garbage truck driver charged over elderly pedestrian's death
World.content:
The driver of a rubbish truck that struck and killed an elderly man in Perth's south-east earlier this month has been charged over the incident.

Police said the 59-year-old driver, from the southern suburb of Riverton, has been charged with dangerous driving causing death.

Chinese national An Yu, 70, suffered critical injuries when he was hit by the truck in Queens Park on September 7.

The incident was captured on CCTV, with vision showing him walking down Balaka Way in Queens Park and the truck reversing into him, knocking him down.

He was rushed to hospital but could not be saved.

Well-known resident

Neighbours described the victim as a quiet, sweet man who walked slowly after suffering a stroke a few years ago.

Residents said they saw him regularly going for morning and afternoon walks.

An Yu, 70, was run over and killed by a reversing garbage truck in Perth. (ABC News: Mitchell Edgar)

Locals told the ABC the road was an unfinished cul-de-sac with a development site at the end, making it difficult for trucks to turn around.

Canning mayor Patrick Hall said the city would take appropriate steps to improve safety on the road, if required.

The driver is due on court in November.

World.title: SA hospital pressure leading to demand 'flashpoint', union warns
World.content:
A non-verbal man with pneumonia waited for more than nine hours in an ambulance outside an Adelaide hospital on a day that the doctors' union has described as "flashpoint" demand for the emergency department.

Alison Marsh was caring for her brother Michael McLean, who has a traumatic brain injury and is unable to communicate, in Adelaide's northern suburbs when a change in his demeanour prompted her to call an ambulance on Tuesday.

Although the ambulance had arrived and taken them to the nearby Lyell McEwin Hospital within 20 minutes, she said it took nine hours for him to be taken from the ambulance to the hospital's emergency room.

Ms Marsh shared her experience as the doctors' union described staff as feeling "helpless" by Tuesday evening, with a period of overwhelming demand reaching more than double that of capacity, according to the South Australian Salaried Medical Officers' Association (SASMOA).

Alison Marsh says her brother had not received treatment for his pneumonia for hours after admission. (Supplied)

Ms Marsh said her brother, who requires to be intubated to receive food and drink, received no nourishment during their time on the ramp. Mr McLean was later diagnosed with pneumonia.

When she spoke to the media alongside opposition spokesperson Jack Batty at 3pm on Wednesday, Ms Marsh said her brother was still yet to receive treatment.

"He is still in the emergency department waiting for a bed," she said.

"He's had nothing, no treatment since he arrived at the hospital yesterday morning.

"He's gone a long time with pneumonia, someone who's already [with] a weakened immune system. He's just had to sit and wait."

Ms Marsh said even when they had been admitted to the emergency department, her family knew it was likely they would need to wait longer for Mr McLean to see a doctor.

"Getting in the door is only a small part of the journey, so we knew that just because he had a bed, when staff asked about how long it would be to see a doctor, there was just … 'We can't tell you when, it will be when a doctor's available.'"

Double capacity

SASMOA's chief industrial officer Bernadette Mulholland said 130 patients were "either waiting for treatment, getting treatment or waiting for a bed" on Tuesday inside the ED, where capacity is under 60.

The state government has acknowledged the intensity of the strain at the hospital, pointing to population growth in Adelaide's north as one of several factors behind the excess pressure.

Average waiting times on Tuesday afternoon were around two hours, according to SA Health's emergency department dashboard.

"We've been watching this build-up in the Lyell McEwin Hospital now for a couple of weeks," Ms Mulholland told 891 ABC Adelaide.

"I think it's just reaching flashpoint in that particular emergency department — unless something is done, and done quickly, to help the clinicians make sure there's space for them to give patients the care they need.

"Patients presenting are much higher in their acuity — the urgent care centres have pulled away those patients maybe needing lesser treatment."

Bernadette Mulholland says staff felt helpless. (ABC News: Marco Catalano)

Ms Mulholland said there was a "sense of helplessness" among staff in the face of the surge in demand, which came days after the union raised separate concerns about the situation at the same hospital earlier this month.

"The Lyell McEwin Hospital has unfortunately become the worst ramped hospital in South Australia," opposition health spokesman Jack Batty said.

"This is not an isolated incident last night. It's a shocking one but not isolated."

A report submitted to SafeWork SA by a SASMOA representative who visited the hospital on September 8 alleged that patients waited more than 13 hours to be treated.

'Real spike' in population growth 'epicentre'

Health Minister Blair Boyer said SafeWork SA had since "closed off" that particular case, but he acknowledged staff at the hospital had been forced to contend with "incredibly difficult circumstances".

The minister said in a three-hour period last night, "walk-ins to the ED at Lyell McEwin were double any other hospital", but added that 20 extra beds had opened at the hospital last week.

"We have seen rising presentations to our EDs for a number of years, but the Lyell McEwin Hospital certainly in the last few months has seen a real spike in that," he said.

"We talk a lot about the aging profile of our population — the oldest mainland state — which has an impact.

" But obviously the northern suburbs are the epicentre of population growth as well, so they get kind of both those factors there. "

Blair Boyer points to various factors including population growth and the flu caseload. (ABC News: Daniel Taylor)

Mr Boyer said the state's current flu caseload was another potential cause of increased system pressure.

While the total number of flu cases in SA this year — around 7,000 — is about 20,000 fewer than at the same time last year, Mr Boyer said there had been a "huge spike" in the past week alone, with more than 900 cases.

"Up until now [we've had a] relatively sedate flu season, but that is starting to shoot up," he said.

World.title: How a 'piece of rural propaganda' became 'compulsory listening' for Aussies
World.content:
It's been 50 years since the iconic theme music for the Blue Hills drama swelled on ABC radio for the last time.

At the time, the show was Australia's longest-running serial radio drama, broadcast from February 1949 until September 1976.

Blue Hills told the stories of the rural families who lived in the fictional town of "Tanimbla".

The cast of the ABC radio drama Blue Hills relaxing on the verandah, from left: Queenie Ashton as Lee Gordon, Nigel Lovell as Bruce, Patricia Crocker as Mandy and Morris Unicomb as Terry. (ABC archives)

Throughout the 1950s, former ABC broadcaster Ian Doyle said "one in two radios in Australia were listening to the Country Hour and Blue Hills" at 1pm.

"It was compulsory listening for people in regional Australia," he told SA Country Hour's Cassandra Hough.

"You couldn't go into a country store in the 50s and expect to be served between 1 and 1:15.

"Anybody selling insurance and knocking on the door in regional Australia, of course, the door wasn't answered. You had to sit and listen to Blue Hills because everything was so compelling."

Former ABC broadcaster and executive producer Ian Doyle (far left) says Blue Hills was an institution for Australian radio. (ABC Rural: Drew Radford)

Lorraine Greenfield grew up on an isolated station in South Australia's north and the ABC was the only radio station the family could tune in to.

"My mother was an absolute devotee of Blue Hills and after I was married, my father-in-law was also a big fan and very strict, so at 1pm everything stopped," Mrs Greenfield said.

"I felt sorry for the stock agents who travelled three or four hours to see him only to be told he couldn't speak until Blue Hills was over.

"He carried that through until the end of Blue Hills.

"It was a very sad day when it ended, I still think about Blue Hills."

'Rural propaganda'

In the late 1940s, author and playwright Gwen Meredith had been tasked with writing a radio series to encourage returning World War Two servicemen to "grow better crops and increase production".

That show, The Lawsons, would be the genesis for Blue Hills.

Blue Hills was the successor series to The Lawsons, a daily radio serial broadcast by the ABC from February 1944 to February 1949. (ABC archives)

"It was a piece of rural propaganda, one way or the other," Mr Doyle said, adding that the ABC's rural department went to great lengths to make sure the show gave an accurate depiction of climate, crops and harvest times as well as new innovations in the farming sector.

"[It was an] attempt to try and improve the production of Australian farmers … [its] connection with the rural department was fundamental and important and she had to be across a whole lot of material to ensure that she got it right."

The Blue Hills cast recording in studio in the 1950s, from left: Vivian Edwards, Charles McCallum, Nellie Lamport, Rupert Chance, Gwen Plumb, unidentified. (ABC archives)

In an old interview, Ms Meredith recalled how the ABC's rural department wanted the show to have as much farming information as possible and this was met with some resistance from the drama department.

"[They] said, 'It'll only ruin the story. It'll all bog [it] down. And I had to run a middle course," she said.

Reflecting the real regional Australia

In the nearly three decades Blue Hills ran, Mr Doyle said she "effectively" wrote 70 novels.

Blue Hills cast members: Mandy (played by Pat Crocker) and her young brother Terry (Morris Unicomb). (ABC archives)

"It was an institution in Australian radio … The Hills was not just about what was happening on the farm, it also dealt with lots of other issues as well."

At the show's height in the 1950s, the White Australia Policy was in effect, as was the Assimilation Policy for First Nations people, as well as segregation and state protection acts.

Against this backdrop, Ms Meredith had written an episode where a relative had a baby with an Indigenous person to try and better reflect Australia's multiracial identity.

"That caused enormous controversy, but she wanted to introduce the idea of the fact that there was multiracial involvement in Australia, and she pushed it as far as she could go," Mr Doyle said.

In other episodes, she was accused by politicians of being "anti-government" by featuring characters commenting on how high interest rates were or how hard it was to get a job.

Blue Hills actors during a studio broadcast in May 1962, from left: Myrna Dodd as Jackie Macarthur, Ethel Lang as Meg Macarthur and Tom Farley as Jim Macarthur. (ABC archives)

"Which was what was happening in regional Australia at the time. The government at the time said … 'She shouldn't be saying those things'," Mr Doyle said.

"Well, she hadn't thought about the politics of it. She's just saying that's what they were talking about in regional Australia."

The writer, who died in 2006 at the age of 98, was the sole writer for all 5,975 episodes.

World.title: ‘A cruel mess’: Families left in limbo as national autism scheme launches without Queensland
World.content:
NationalQueenslandDisability ‘A cruel mess’: Families left in limbo as national autism scheme launches without Queensland Courtney Kruk September 30, 2026 — 8:39pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

The Queensland government says its refusal to sign up to a new program for autistic children is in support of families, despite calls from across the sector to provide certainty for vulnerable kids removed from the NDIS. The first phase of Thriving Kids, a new system for children under nine with developmental delays or autism and low-to-moderate support needs, will launch on Thursday. The federal government says the NDIS alternative will initially include foundational supports, a digital resource hub, and national helplines to guide families. Federal Health Minister Mark Butler announced Thriving Kids, a new system for children under nine with developmental delays and autism, in August last year. The first phase of the program launches this week. Dominic Lorrimer Changes to NDIS access and assessment will not take effect until January 2028.



Queensland the lone holdout Queensland is the only state or territory yet to sign on to the program, with the Crisafulli government repeatedly criticising the scheme’s lack of detail and clear, long-term funding. Disability Services Minister Amanda Camm called Thriving Kids “a bad deal for children with a disability”, and said the LNP was prepared to take a stand, even if it was the only state to do so. Asked on Wednesday whether the government was considering an eleventh-hour agreement, Premier David Crisafulli said he remained “as strong and resolute as ever”. “We’re trying to get common sense out of Canberra to make sure [families] don’t fall through the cracks,” he said.



“We’ll keep working Canberra, [but] we want to see the details.” Related Article Hospitals Albanese ends hospital stalemate with $25b deal to move kids off NDIS A spokesperson for the federal government said while every other state and territory was finalising the implementation of Thriving Kids, Queensland had left families “rightly asking” what children’s services they could access. “Queensland joined every other state and territory earlier this year in signing a national agreement for foundational supports as part of the NHRA [National Health Reform Agreement] deal, as well as a heads of agreement on the national deal that includes Thriving Kids,” the spokesperson said. “The expectation now is those commitments are implemented so the benefits of the agreement can be realised.”



Greens state MP Michael Berkman labelled the situation “a cruel mess”, and said both Labor and the LNP had turned their backs on autistic people. “There’s still very little concrete information on what this Thriving Kids program would actually provide,” he said. Greens MP Michael Berkman says he’s concerned about the lack of detail around the Thriving Kids program. Joe Ruckli/Australian Financial Review “We’ve been told it will include online resources for parents, and there’s been talk of a lot of things it ‘may’ include, like school programs or social groups – all of which sounds pretty weak and undefined to me. “There’s also no information on what will happen to kids after they turn nine, and nothing on adults with autism who will be kicked off the NDIS at the end of next year.”



Related Article Disability Children won’t need an autism diagnosis to use Thriving Kids scheme Families and providers in the dark Brisbane mother Nicole Chesterton has been waiting almost two years to get her seven-year-old son assessed for autism. She was recently told her NDIS funding had been cut and that she wouldn’t be able to dispute it without a formal diagnosis. With the introduction of Thriving Kids looming, she’s even more uncertain about how her son will be supported. “[Under the NDIS] he was allocated around $17,000 a year to use on speech therapy, psychology, and all those allied health offerings,” she said.



“[Now] there’s no funding and I’m off the list. “I have no idea [what Thriving Kids will mean] … there’s no way to keep up with all the changes that they’re making.” Jodi Wolthers, chief executive of Parent to Parent Association Queensland – a support organisation for people with disabilities – said many families were feeling uncertain about what changes to the NDIS would mean in practice. Jodi Wolthers, chief executive of Parent to Parent Association Queensland. Inclusion Australia



“Our biggest concern is some parents we talk to have not heard of Thriving Kids,” she said. “At the same time, we are hearing from families whose young children are being exited from the NDIS. “The risk is that there is no Thriving Kids or other service for them to go to. There is no safety net. “In general, parents are concerned about the whole of the NDIS reform changes and what they will mean for their son/daughter and the impact on their family.” Soul Support provides disability services for children across south-east Queensland, Victoria and NSW.



Related Article Autism ‘We’re lost’: Families, staff devastated as specialist childcare centres close Managing director Breanna Jenkins said children with autism were already disadvantaged by current funding arrangements, and she worried that more would be left behind by a new, ill-defined program. “Who will be assessing the severity of these children and whether they’re eligible for Thriving Kids?” she said. “As we’ve seen with the NDIA [National Disability Insurance Agency] … it can be really challenging for [young people with autism] to get funding, and their funding can just be stripped away. “After how many years the NDIA has been around, we’re still ironing out key things about it … so it’s a real worry if we’re going to be putting up millions of people and families into Thriving Kids and all of these issues [remain].”



Vision Australia’s chief mission officer, Chris Edwards, said Thriving Kids raised questions for children with multiple disabilities and deteriorating conditions. “Where those supports are put into different lanes, that creates challenges to be able to provide a holistic support for a child to ensure they … actually start meeting developmental milestones,” he said. “All programs, whether it’s NDIS or Thriving Kids, should be accepting kids who have deteriorating conditions as early as possible so those interventions can become part of their norm.” What comes next? From Thursday, families of children with extra developmental needs can access expanded information and supports, including the new Thriving Kids Autism Helpline and a new online information hub, which Queenslanders will also be able to access.



The federal government said children with permanent and significant disability or high support needs will continue to access the NDIS. The full Thriving Kids program is expected by 2028. Start the day with a summary of the day’s most important and interesting stories, analysis and insights.

World.title: ‘I want to apologise for all this’: Stawell Gift winner apologises after losing title over drug test
World.content:
SportAthleticsWorld athletics championships ‘I want to apologise for all this’: Stawell Gift winner apologises after losing title over drug test Michael Gleeson Updated September 30, 2026 — 7:59pm ,first published 6:01pm Save You have reached your maximum number of saved items. Remove items from your saved list to add more. Share A A A

The men’s winner of this year’s Stawell Gift, Olufemi Komolafe has been stripped of the title and his prizemoney over a failed drug test. Komalafe has apologised for his accidental breach which saw him fail a doping test after the prestigious Easter Monday 120m sprint. He will lose the title and the $40,000 winner’s cheque. Olufemi Komolafe when he won the Stawell Gift in April. Getty Images “I want to apologise for all this. I won’t keep the title of Stawell Gift winner, but the experience of winning it was invaluable, and I’m eager and confident that I can take it to the next level when I return,” Komalafe said in a message to friends. Komalafe failed a drug test after inadvertently taking a banned substance contained in ADHD medication. He has received a 12-month ban, reduced from the standard four years after Sport Integrity Australia accepted the use was inadvertent and Komalafe co-operated fully with authorities.



He won the race in April off five metres in a time of 12.03 seconds. Jake Ireland, who came second and will be elevated to winner, said it was not the way he wanted to be called a Stawell Gift winner. Jake Ireland (wearing the white singlet) running at Stawell in April. He’s now the retrospective winner of this year’s Gift. Getty Images “Ninety percent of winning is crossing the line and celebrating with your family and friends,” Ireland said. “I certainly don’t feel like a winner, maybe that’s the competitor in me. I was not first over the line.



“I suppose this year has got an asterisk to it. I would hate to come across as gloating or rubbing it in. “It was not like a blatant cheating where it’s deliberate; it was accidental. I feel for him, too, I know he is in a horrible place.” Olufemi Komolafe collected $40,000 as winner of the Stawell Gift. Luke Hemer, Stawell Gift Stawell Gift Event Management said it was aware of a matter relating to the 2026 Stawell Gift that was now being examined by Sport Integrity Australia processes. “[We] respects the integrity of this process, including the rights of all parties involved,” the organisation posted on Instagram.



“The integrity of competition is fundamental to the Stawell Gift. SGEM is committed to providing a fair and level playing field for every athlete and respects the established processes for dealing with matters of this nature.” Loading The Victorian Athletic League’s statement said it could “confirm an integrity issue and process is underway with an athlete related to the 2026 Stawell Gift”. “We can’t comment at this stage until the process is completed by Sport Integrity Australia,” it added. Whether it’s the sound of crashing waves, the water views, the salt air, or the outdoor lifestyle, there’s nothing quite like living in or visiting your holiday home by the coast. Open-plan living, indoor-outdoor flow and natural textures—here are five of our favourite luxury homes by the coast, now on the market. 35 Salonika Street, Sorrento VIC Featuring a palette of natural stone, French oak timber and handmade Krause bricks, this Sorrento home makes a stylish impression.



Designed to capture natural light through large windows, the open-plan kitchen, living, and dining areas open onto an al fresco area for indoor-outdoor entertaining. Outside, there’s an additional private deck, pool and spa, and a dedicated gym at the rear of the home. Situated only a short walk from Sorrento’s main street, you have coastal living at your fingertips. 14 Seaview Crescent, Stanwell Park, NSW



With an elevated position and panoramic Pacific Ocean views, this South Coast home is highly desirable. In addition to the views, the property is close to the beach and to Stanwell Park village. But you may not want to leave the property. With the in-ground pool and spa, a Balinese-style hut, multiple outdoor terraces and tropical landscaping, you have resort-style living right in your backyard. Other features include the designer kitchen, a master suite with a balcony, a four-car garage and a wine cellar. 18 Park Road, Sorrento VIC



This contemporary coastal home features expansive living and dining areas and indoor-outdoor spaces. With a north-facing, undercover deck featuring a plumbed barbecue kitchen and a pizza oven overlooking a heated pool and landscaped gardens, you can enjoy the outdoors year-round. Inside, the home is set up for convenience with hydronic heating, heated towel rails, recycler heating and cooling, double glazing and two gas fireplaces. With five bedrooms, four bathrooms and well-thought-out zoning, the home is well suited for family holidays.



11 Burns Street, Byron Bay, NSW This brand-new double-storey residence in Byron Bay features a contemporary coastal design, ideal for either a permanent family home or a holiday home investment. With a north-facing orientation, the home has plenty of natural light throughout, highlighted in the open-plan kitchen and dining area, which is located in the heart of the home. Outside, a covered entertainment terrace features retractable awnings, a built-in barbecue, and a large family-sized swimming pool.



Other highlights include multiple living zones, a private main bedroom suite with a walk-in robe and en suite, solar panels and proximity to the Byron Bay township and beaches. 92 Cabana Boulevard, Benowa Waters QLD Designed by Stuart Osman, this waterfront home offers coastal living on the Nerang River. The property’s outdoor features make the most of the natural setting and are a definite highlight. These include an infinity pool and spa, two oversized 4.5-metre pivoting umbrella shades, waterside and poolside fire pit zones with built-in bench seating, electric retractable awnings with integrated LED lighting, and outdoor heaters and fans.



And if you like water sports, there is a 10-metre (approximately) pontoon with a jet-ski launch, offering direct access to the Broadwater. The interiors are also impressive, with the tech-savvy home using Google Home integration to control the lighting, fountain and custom wine cellar, and featuring a dedicated media room with surround sound.
